You have seen the headlines. Holidaying in Europe this year may not be as streamlined as it once was due to the introduction of the new biometric data system, which has caused some border points to experience unprecedentedly long queues.

The entry-exit system (EES) requires passengers to provide biometric information, such as fingerprints and facial imagery, upon first entry into Schengen Area countries before passport control.

But the system has been experiencing some teething issues, with the blame being thrown back and forth between industry leaders, from airports not having enough staff to the very design of the EES causing wait times at the borders to increase.

While there are destinations that have managed to implement EES without too much disruption, others have struggled, meaning some travellers have spent the start of their long-awaited holidays standing in hours-long queues before they can even think of lounging on the beach or exploring a city.

The beauty of having Europe at our fingertips is the diverse selection of places that can be visited by travelling for just a few hours. But add a five-hour EES queue into the mix (in the worst-case scenario), and you may as well have booked that flight to Barbados instead.

There are, however, a few places in Europe that are not required to introduce the new EES system at their border as they are not part of the Schengen free movement zone. We have rounded up some of these countries that you may consider for your next break, plus a guide on the European travel jargon you need to know.

Which European countries don’t have EES?

Cyprus

open image in gallery Limassol is a popular beach town ( Getty Images )

While Cyprus is in the EU, it has not fully integrated into the Schengen Zone, making for an EES-free Mediterranean beach break. The island is popular for its beach resorts and buzzy seaside hotspots like Limassol, Larnaca and Ayia Napa, as well as its more laidback regions, including the beachside town of Protaras and the Troodos Mountains, home to Cyprus tallest peak, Mount Olympus.

Aside from catering to party people with its nightlife strips or families with its kid-friendly hotels, Cyprus also catches the eye of history buffs with the ancient ruins in Paphos and Venetian, Ottoman and Byzantine architecture across the capital of Nicosia.



Ireland

open image in gallery Drive on Ireland’s Wild Atlantic Way ( Getty Images )

Only a short hop, skip and jump from the UK, Ireland is one of the best destinations for travellers looking to immerse themselves in nature. Like Cyprus, Ireland is an EU country but has an exceptional agreement to opt out of Schengen rules, meaning that flights and ferries will not be subject to the EES rollout.

Ireland is home to one of Europe’s most acclaimed road trip routes, the Wild Atlantic Way. This 1,600-mile-long winding coastal route stretches past some of the country’s most beautiful natural landmarks, such as the Cliffs of Moher and rock formations like Downpatrick Head.

City breaks are also in abundance. Visit Galway for a traditional music scene, Cork for an artisan foodie haven, and Dublin for its legendary pub culture and Ireland’s most popular attraction, the Guinness Storehouse.



Albania

open image in gallery Ksamil is a popular beach spot ( Getty Images )

Known as “Europe’s best kept secret”, Albania has emerged in the past few years as a more affordable alternative to Greece or Croatia. Its Ionian coastline, known as the Albanian Riviera, has almost Maldivian-like beaches with white sands and turquoise waters, with Ksamil and Himarë being popular seafront spots.

If a beach holiday is not on your list this year, Albania offers plenty more. Bucket-list treks await in the Albanian Alps, such as the 10-mile Valbona Pass with alpine panoramas and limestone cliffs. Or, take a trip to the capital, Tirana, for a budget city break exploring the blend of colourful buildings, from the Ottoman period to the Soviet era, as well as some radical modern structures like Downtown One.



Bosnia and Herzegovina

open image in gallery Mostar is home to the famous Stari Most bridge ( Getty Images/iStockphoto )

This Balkan country has the second smallest coastline in the world, with only a 12-mile sliver on the Adriatic coast, so sand seekers may not find the country as appealing as its neighbours. Yet thoughts of a beach break tend to go out the window when visitors discover how much there is to do – and how extremely cheap it all is.

The Kravica Waterfalls are one of the country’s most beautiful natural spots, with multiple cascades falling through a dense forested area into the lake below. Equally as enchanting is the Una National Park that protects the emerald green Una River and is ideal for white water rafting.

Bosnia and Herzegovina should also be on your radar if you are seeking a budget-friendly city break. Mostar, in the southern region, is known for its famous 16th-century Ottoman Bridge, Stari Most that connects the two parts of the city. The capital, Sarajevo, is one of Europe’s cheapest destinations to visit, with a laidback coffee culture and some very poignant museums like the Tunnels of Salvation, which retells human experiences of the 1990s siege of the city.



North Macedonia

open image in gallery Lake Ohrid is one of Europe’s oldest and deepest lakes ( Getty Images )

The landlocked country of North Macedonia is another overlooked Balkan destination rich in dramatic mountain ranges, thousands of ancient archaeological sites and Ottoman heritage. Its capital, Skopje, sits on the slopes of Mount Vodno, and is filled with fascinating sites left behind from Ottoman rule, such as the Old Bazaar, one of the largest and oldest markets in the Balkans, and the Kale Fortress perched high with views over the city out to the Šar Mountains.

Outside the capital, another must-visit destination is Lake Ohrid, a body of water shared with Albania. Its northeast shore is lined with hilltop fortresses, medieval churches and Ohrid’s red-tiled Old Town with Ottoman-era houses on steep cobbled slopes.



Moldova

open image in gallery Moldova is home to the largest wine cellars in the world ( Getty Images )

While Moldova seldom tops travellers’ bucket lists, the lack of EES queues may make this former Soviet republic more enticing. It is perhaps one of the more overlooked winemaking countries, with a history of cultivating the grape into a classic tipple for over 7,000 years. The Ștefan Vodă region is where you will find wineries producing bottles of red wine such as the local Rară Neagră, as well as Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Malbec. Meanwhile, the Cordu region’s milder climate makes it ideal for vineyards to cultivate grapes for white and sparkling wines. In this region, you will also find the world’s largest wine cellar, Mileștii Mici, which stores over 1.5 million bottles of wine underground.

Chișinău, the country’s capital, is also worth a visit, for its Soviet-era architecture built from white limestone rising up between a huge selection of green spaces and parks.



Montenegro

open image in gallery The Bay of Kotor is surrounded by Venetian-era architecture ( Getty Images/iStockphoto )

Another Balkan country on the list, Montenegro, is unique for being one of Europe’s smallest countries by size and population, with under 630,000 people living in the nation. The country is very mountainous, making places like Durmitor National Park incredibly scenic destinations. Explore the park on hiking trails, visit deep canyons via raft, or ski during the winter. Visitors can arrange stays at kanus, mountainous farm settlements, for a rural retreat in the alpine landscape.

Visitors to Montenegro are usually drawn to the Adriatic Coast, home to luxury beach towns that attract A-list celebrities and billionaires. Think Madonna, Brad Pitt, Marilyn Monroe and Elizabeth Taylor. Towns like Sveti Stefan are particularly exclusive, with an ultra-luxury Aman hotel on one protruding islet. Aside from the lavish stays, there are 117 beaches on Montenegro’s Adriatic coast to explore, while the historic Bay of Kotor is not to be missed.



Kosovo

open image in gallery Prizren is full of historical architecture ( Getty Images/iStockphoto )

Kosovo is Europe’s youngest nation, having declared independence from Serbia in 2008. While Serbia continues to claim the territory as an autonomous province, more than 100 countries recognise the nation, including the UK.

Capital Prishtina is a compact and walkable city, filled with a juxtaposition of architecture from brutalist buildings to Ottoman mosques. The youthful city has a lively coffee culture, while visitors also recommend the Ethnological Museum, which tells the story of the country’s heritage. Located at the foot of the Sharr Mountains in the south, Prizren is another city worth exploring, known for its well-preserved Ottoman-era architecture and ancient fortifications dating back to the Bronze Age.



Serbia

open image in gallery Belgrade is a popular place for a city break ( Getty Images/iStockphoto )

This landlocked Balkan country is another destination favoured by city breakers who make a beeline for the diverse capital of Belgrade. Known for topping lists of the best cities for nightlife in Europe, come the summer, Belgrade’s two rivers come alive with floating splavovi clubs. For a culture fix, the city’s top attractions include the Belgrade Fortress with views over the city, Saint Sava Temple, which is one of the largest churches in the world, and the picturesque Skadarlija bohemian quarter brimming with kafanas (taverns) and antique shops.

Outside the city, Serbia has five national parks to explore, including Tara, filled with mountain peaks, archaeological sites dating back to the Neolithic period, and outstanding valley views such as the one at Banjska Stena.



United Kingdom

open image in gallery The Lake District is ideal for hikers ( Getty Images/iStockphoto )

One of the best ways to avoid the EES queues is to embrace a staycation at home in the UK. There are plenty of popular holiday destinations across our isles – from exploring the highlands and islands of Scotland to escaping to the Pembrokeshire coast in Wales, or taking a trip to the bucolic English countryside, such as the Lake District or the Cotswolds. Northern Ireland is home to one of the most spectacular coastlines, with the Giant's Causeway being an unmissable landmark.

Or why not try some more underrated cities for a weekend break? Instead of London or Edinburgh, have a night or two in Dundee, Birmingham or Newcastle.



What is the Schengen Area?

The EU is a political and economic union of 27 European countries. Not all countries in Europe are in the EU.

The Schengen Area is a border-free zone in Europe that allows citizens and international visitors alike to travel freely between certain EU countries.

The Schengen Area consists of 25 of the 27 EU countries, as well as all members of the European Free Trade Association (Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland).

The new EES system has been installed at the borders of all 29 of these Schengen countries. In theory, travel from country to country within the Schengen area is classed as domestic, so you should only be asked to visit the EES kiosks when you arrive and leave the Schengen area.

The full list of the 29 Schengen countries is as follows: Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Iceland, Italy, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden and Switzerland.

Despite being in the EU, Cyprus and Ireland are not in the Schengen Area, meaning that EES has not been installed at their borders.

For the completists, Andorra, Monaco, San Marino and Vatican City are de facto part of the Schengen Zone because travellers need to pass through Schengen countries to get there.

Belarus and Ukraine are European countries, but are not part of the Schengen Area or the EU, and did not make the above list as the UK’s Foreign Office currently advises people not to travel there.

Non-EU countries including Georgia, Turkey, Azerbaijan, Russia and Armenia, which some may consider partly European, were also not included as they have transcontinental status.

Due to it's geographical location, Cyprus can be considered Middle East or Asia, but we included it in our list as it is part of the EU.

What about overseas territories?

There are various rules for overseas countries and territories (OCTs), outermost regions (ORs), autonomous regions and autonomous constituent countries, all of which mean something different in how they relate geopolitically to European countries.

The majority of territories with ties to Schengen Area countries are not part of the Schengen Area itself, meaning that UK travellers will not have to complete EES when entering or exiting those destinations.

For example, overseas France, such as Reunion, French Guiana and French Polynesia, are not part of the zone.

This is the same for Greenland and the Faroe Islands, which are part of the Kingdom of Denmark, as well as the Kingdom of the Netherlands, which is made up of constituent countries like Aruba and Curaçao. The same goes for Norway’s Svalbard.

There are some territories and regions, however, that have implemented EES as they have been recognised as part of the Schengen Area, including ORs such as the Azores, Madeira and the Canary Islands.

Autonomous regions such as Spain’s Ceuta and Melilla on the North African coast, also have implemented EES checks, while Finland’s Åland can only be reached by passing through Schengen borders, meaning EES will be required to get there.

Recently, there has been a special agreement made between the UK and the European Union regarding Gibraltar, which has made the territory a de facto part of the EU’s Schengen Zone.

UK residents flying in and out of the territory will now have to pass through EES.

News.title: Private sector pay suffers worst growth since Covid
News.content:
Private sector wages are growing at their slowest pace since the pandemic, piling pressure on Andy Burnham as he enters Downing Street facing a fragile economy and strained public finances.

Salaries rose by 2.9pc in the three months to May, the first time growth has dipped below 3pc since October 2020 and only narrowly ahead of inflation at 2.8pc.

The slowdown was most acute in key industries, with wages in finance and business services up just 2.3pc, manufacturing at 2.5pc and construction earnings falling by 0.2pc over the year.

In contrast, public sector pay accelerated to 5.5pc after striking workers secured higher settlements, widening the gap between state and private sectors.

The cooling labour market came as borrowing overshot official forecasts, leaving John Healey, the new Chancellor, with a £2.7bn gap against expectations.

The Government borrowed £57.6bn between April and June – less than a year earlier but still ahead of projections – pushing public debt to nearly £3tn, or 94.9pc of GDP.

Mr Healey said: “The Prime Minister and I have talked about how we will work in lockstep to meet the fiscal rules with a buffer against uncertainty and how we’ll make life more affordable for working people right across the UK.”

However, Sir Mel Stride, the shadow business secretary, said: “If Andy Burnham and John Healey are really serious about the future of our economy then they must get borrowing under control.”

As a cat carer for over 50 years and a vet for nearly 40, I understand the importance of finding the best cat food. It isn’t always easy to get it right. Cats need a complete and balanced diet providing protein, carbohydrate, fats, minerals, vitamins and fibre, as well as some specific nutrients such as taurine and essential fatty acids.

With such a huge range of products available, selecting the right one can be a real challenge. The aim of this article is to offer guidance on how to select the optimal diet for your feline friend. You can read my full reviews of the current best cat foods further down, followed by a comprehensive guide to cat nutrition, where you’ll learn how much and how often to feed your cat, among other things. But if you’re in a hurry, here’s a quick look at my top five:

The best cat foods: At a glance

Are cat food delivery services better than shopping in pet stores?

There are pros and cons to both. Online cat food delivery services such as Untamed, Republic of Cats and Katkin are new options and have the advantages of a wide variety of choice, combined with the convenience of delivery to your door. I write about some of them below. However, pet stores may have a wider choice and, in a physical store, you can pick and choose from products in front of you with expert advice.

How I chose the best cat foods

There are hundreds of different types and brands of cat food on the market: the following recommendations are based on my own experiences as a vet, plus feedback from the many cat owners to whom I talk.

Most brands tailor to different life stages – kitten, adult and senior – but only a few tailor to specific breeds, which is where my top choice Royal Canin really shines. News.title: Scammers stole $114 billion as Southeast Asia’s crime gangs go corporate
News.content:
Scam gangs stole up to $114 billion from people in Asia-Pacific alone in 2025, the UN has warned, as crime syndicates rapidly professionalise their tactics to evade law enforcement in Southeast Asia.

By way of comparison, the sum dwarfs the $85 billion the UK spends each year on defence.

The Asia-Pacific region has emerged as an epicentre for massive cyber fraud operations since the Covid pandemic. Scammers – some willingly, others under duress – are now stealing billions from internet users across the world via fake romance and cryptocurrency investment schemes.

In 2025, these fraud operations stole between $88.3 and $114.1bn from just people across East Asia, Southeast Asia, Australia and New Zealand, according to a report on Tuesday from the UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC).

Those figures are triple the estimated losses in 2023, between $18 and $37bn, and don’t account for victims in Europe or the US.

The scam centres – which began in fortified compounds but are now increasingly housed in innocuous office blocks and villas – are found across the region, but have especially exploited power vacuums caused by war, corruption and weak governance in Cambodia, Myanmar and Laos.

Although the scammers initially targeted people in China, they have dramatically expanded their ambitions. The UNODC said people from at least 80 countries and territories had been identified in compounds, with recruiters seeking people from outside Asia as they look to expand new markets.

News.title: UK borrowing costs rise at fastest pace in G7
News.content:
Britain’s borrowing costs rose at the fastest pace in the G7 after Andy Burnham said he would take a “flexible” approach to the UK’s fiscal rules.

In his maiden speech as prime minister, Mr Burnham on Monday signalled he could bend the rules underpinning Britain’s finances, spooking financial markets fearful of higher government spending.

UK gilts – a benchmark for how much the Government pays on its debt – saw yields rise 0.08 percentage points to an eight-week high of 5.03pc for the 10-year bond. Thirty-year gilts also pushed higher.

The rise was the fastest in the G7, excluding Japan, whose markets are closed for a national holiday.

After markets closed on Monday, Mr Burnham surprised the City by picking John Healey as his next Chancellor.

Mr Healey, who quit over defence funding rising too slowly, will now be tasked with finding billions of pounds in Britain’s stretched public finances.

Shabana Mahmood, the Home Secretary, had widely been expected for the role. Ed Miliband, the former Energy Secretary, was also in contention.

Mr Healey will replace Rachel Reeves, who resigned on Monday.

The appointment of Mr Healey, a veteran of the Blair-Brown government, may calm fears in the City after Mr Burnham pledged to stretch the fiscal rules by using “flexibility” within them.

Speaking in Downing Street, Mr Burnham said: “I’ve said we’ll stick to the fiscal rules, and by that I mean the existing fiscal rules, and use obviously any flexibility within them.”

James Athey, a fund manager at Marlborough, said: “It’s not a good start because bandying around the words fiscal rules seems to be believed within government circles to be a sufficient condition to get financial markets on side, and that just misunderstands an element of the problem.”

He added that investors were watching closely for any signs that the Government will increase borrowing.

Matt Amis, investment director at Aberdeen, said Mr Burnham’s comments had “got the markets’ attention.”

He said “It just shows this week in particular the language from the Burnham administration, the new chancellor, is going to be key here. The gilt market is on edge.”

Mr Burnham, who has become the UK’s seventh prime minister in just a decade, has inherited a troubled economy as businesses grapple with low confidence and strained public finances.

Monday’s comment suggests the new prime minister will use measures to raise borrowing while keeping the additional sums off the Government’s book.

The Resolution Foundation, a think tank, said he could do this by expanding the remit of institutions like the National Wealth Fund, an arms-length government investment vehicle.

His plan to use “flexibility” in the fiscal rules comes after Ms Reeves altered the main indicator of government debt in 2024.

She tweaked the primary measure of the UK’s debt to Public Sector Net Financial Liabilities, meaning that when public financial institutions borrow to invest in a private business it does not count towards the government’s fiscal rules.

However, the think tank warned that boosting the financial capacity of public financial institutions like the National Wealth Fund by £16bn would cost around £400 million a year in debt interest.

Helen Miller, director at the Institute for Fiscal Studies, warned that challenging public finances will mean Mr Burnham will be forced to make tough choices on spending.

She said: “While chancellors come and go, the underlying fiscal constraints remain the same. Public debt, borrowing and debt-interest costs are all high. One in every £12 the government spends currently goes on debt interest.”

Higher borrowing costs threaten to increase the Government’s debt interest bill, which is already forecast to hit £111.2bn for the financial year - equivalent to 8.3pc of public spending.

Mr Burnham said he would announce a set of measures on Tuesday to give households “breathing space” to help with the cost of living.

“I will set out some of those measures starting tomorrow, including how we pay for them,” he said.

“We will help more young people into education... and we will build more council homes. That is the fair and sustainable way to bring the welfare bill down, to meet our fiscal rules and to honour our commitments on defence to our international partners.”

Mr Amis said: “Tomorrow we’re getting some cost of living news. [Burnham] said he was going to state where that funding’s come from. I think that’s key, any unfunded spending from here would get the market’s attention.”

News.title: India approves first dengue vaccine as cases surge in South Asia
News.content:
India has approved its first dengue vaccine as cases of the mosquito-borne disease surge in South Asia.

Japan’s Takeda Pharmaceutical’s dengue vaccine QDENGA has been approved by India’s drug regulator, the Centre Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO).

The global threat posed by dengue has been rising for years, as climate change, urbanisation and international travel aid the spread of the mosquitoes that transmit it.

The approval comes as hospitals across South Asia grapple with a surge in dengue infections.

In Sri Lanka, health authorities reported 2,652 new cases on Sunday alone, taking the total to 76,044 dengue cases so far this year. At least 53 people have died.

Bangladesh is also suffering a major outbreak with over 9,000 cases and 30 deaths that has piled pressure on its health system even as it battles a measles epidemic.

Dengue is transmitted to humans through the bites of infected Aedes mosquitoes.

Its symptoms include fever, severe muscle pain, and in severe cases, shock and internal bleeding that can be fatal.

Although mortality is relatively low, outbreaks place a substantial burden on health systems.

Takeda’s QDENGA jab is a live-attenuated tetravalent vaccine designed to protect against all four dengue virus serotypes. It can be given regardless of previous dengue infections.

“The approval comes at a critical time for public health, as reported dengue cases in India have increased 11-fold in the past two decades,” the company said in a statement.

News.title: Burnham’s plan to restore UK aid spending
News.content:
Andy Burnham is planning to reverse the cuts to Britain’s aid budget made by his predecessors Sir Keir Starmer and Rishi Sunak, according to reports.

A roadmap for returning the UK to spending 0.7 per cent of Gross National Income (GNI) on international aid will be drawn up as part of a major shake-up of the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO), The Independent reported.

Ed Miliband is set to be named Foreign Secretary and put in charge of overhauling Britain’s international development aims, as well as prioritising climate goals, senior Labour sources said.

The aid spending plan was absent from Mr Burnham’s brief first speech as Prime Minister, in which he pledged to end rough sleeping and bring down the welfare bill in order to fund defence and council housing.

But it follows anger within the Labour Party over what was seen as a broken manifesto promise, when Sir Keir and Rachel Reeves, the Chancellor, slashed aid spending to 0.3 per cent of GNI.

Senior Labour MPs have been lobbying for a return to the 0.7 per cent commitment, a target first established by the United Nations in the 1970s.

It has since become a key yardstick for international efforts to reduce poverty and tackle major health issues like the HIV/AIDS epidemic, vaccine access, and maternal mortality in poor countries.

News.title: The best bars and nightlife in Lyon
News.content:
While drinking in this gourmet city remains firmly rooted in the surrounding Rhône Valley’s ancient wine-growing heritage, new-gen addresses have embraced world cocktail culture in style. They’re using Lyon’s long-envied gastronomic know-how and rich bounty of local seasonal produce to create some sensational new drinks and food pairings as only the French can. Artisanal spirits meanwhile are increasingly fashionable: cornichon gin, Mezcal-fuelled soirées at chef Carla Kirsch’s gourmet tacos joint in Croix-Rousse, and the stunning Christian Drouin gin and pine-needle liqueur cocktail with stick of Comté cheese to stir I recently had at Hôtel Dieu’s Le Dôme bar all spring to mind.

Come the warmer days of spring and summer, the city’s fervent café-life spills onto pretty pavement terraces, while floating bars moored along Les Berges du Rhône (the landscaped river banks of the Rhône’s Rive Gauche or Left Bank) hum with after-dark dance parties and festivities. Clubbing remains fairly mainstream.

Sports.title: John Stones set for immediate Premier League return as giants consider free transfer for England World Cup star, 32
Sports.content:
CHELSEA are considering a deal to sign England defender John Stones.

The veteran defender, 32, is a free agent after leaving Manchester City at the end of his contract this summer.



Stones won six Premier League titles, the Champions League, two FA Cups, five League Cups, three Community Shields, the Club World Cup and the Uefa Super Cup during his time at City.

However, appearances have been limited in recent years due to injury issues for the former Everton defender.



Stones would add significant experience to the Blues squad, something new boss Xabi Alonso is keen to address this summer.

He made five appearances for England at the World Cup, including starts in the quarter-final win over Norway and the 2-1 defeat to Argentina in the semis.



Stones would add to Chelsea‘s defensive options in Levi Colwill, Tosin Adarabioyo, Trevoh Chalobah, Josh Acheampong, Wesley Fofana, Jorrel Hato and Benoit Badiashile.

Chelsea made an £8million attempt to sign Sunderland midfielder Granit Xhaka, who won the Bundesliga under Alonso at Bayer Leverkusen, but the Black Cats are confident of keeping the Swiss.

The Blues also remain in talks over a deal for Crystal Palace’s Maxence Lacroix, valued at £60m.

Aston Villa are close to agreeing a loan deal, with an obligation to buy if certain terms are met, for exiled winger Alejandro Garnacho.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Chelsea last week agreed a £117m deal to sign Morgan Rogers and the Argentine winger was discussed as part of those talks – though it is a separate deal.

Garnacho has not trained at Cobham during pre-season having been told to focus on finding another club, just one year after his £40m move from Manchester United to Chelsea.

Another who has been training alone and away from the Blues training ground is French defender Axel Disasi, valued at £25m.

AC Milan are one of a number of Italian clubs to have expressed an interest in Disasi, who was part of the ‘bomb squad’ last season before joining West Ham on loan in January.

The Hammers enquired about bringing Disasi back to the London Stadium this summer but he does not want to join a Championship club. There is also interest in France.

Sports.title: Chelsea files: Shock at record £117m Morgan Rogers deal, no rest for Alonso’s squad & Disasi transfer options
Sports.content:
CHELSEA’S British record deal to sign Morgan Rogers staggered a number of people.

Not least Arsenal who had been pursuing a move for the England man all summer.



But it also came as a surprise to a number of financial bods in the industry, who can hardly compute how Chelsea have managed to fork out £117million.

Chelsea’s record losses of £262.4m, posted in April, had many feeling a scant summer was on the horizon.



Chelsea, who sold £300m worth of talent last summer and have already raised £120m in sales so far this year – with more to come.

The Blues have always maintained that there are no concerns over their financial situation and that the losses incurred were one off write-offs with revenue due to rise in the next set of accounts.



However, with revenue for the coming season set to fall after a 10th place finish means no European football – financial experts feel the Rogers deal is simply unaffordable without further big-ticket sales.

That could mean that World Cup finalist Enzo Fernandez, despite Xabi Alonso‘s desire to keep him, will need to be sold this summer.

A-LON WAY TO GO

XABI ALONSO will be delighted he has a full pre-season to work with many of his players, aside from those World Cup stars now putting their feet up.

What the Spaniard may be less delighted about is the miles put into the legs of his players during the pre-season.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Chelsea famously had just two weeks to prepare for last season following the Club World Cup and struggled with injury problems throughout off the back of it.

While the likes of Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro have been given a surprise but, for the club at least, welcome rest over the summer, there is no taking it easy for the Blues this time.

After two summers in America, for a tour and then the Club World Cup, Chelsea are heading down under and to the Far East.



The Blues squad fly later this week beginning a mammoth tour – and they better have plenty of films downloaded for their flights.

Chelsea are due to spend up to 56 HOURS in the air over their pre-season tour, flying from London to Sydney and then on to Hong Kong, Jakarta and Iskandar Puteri, Malaysia before returning home.

That is a staggering 24,456 miles flown in the air. They will not be able to blame the Club World Cup for fatigue this year, but a few may raise eyebrows at such a grueling schedule.

It is also a huge jump from Chelsea’s previous pre-season tour, which saw them travel around 13,000 miles across the United States under Enzo Maresca.

GIVE HIM THE AX

AXEL DISASI has not been training with Chelsea at Cobham with his future away from Stamford Bridge.



Much like Alejandro Garnacho, the defender has been allowed to train alone and focus on finding a new club.

Disasi was part of the ‘bomb squad’ this time last year and spent six months training alone or with the Under-21s before joining West Ham on loan in January.

West Ham have asked about bringing the Frenchman back but he does not want to move to a Championship club.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

AC Milan are one of a number of Italian sides interested in the defender, while there is also interest in France.

Chelsea value Disasi at up to £25millon this summer and are working to find a permanent move away.

Sports.title: Erling Haaland celebrates birthday with stunning partner on yacht after taking over America at World Cup
Sports.content:
ERLING Haaland has celebrated his birthday with his stunning partner on a yacht.

The Norway striker has taken time off after taking over America at the 2026 World Cup.



Haaland has taken to the ocean to celebrate his 26th birthday on Tuesday.

His girlfriend Isabel Haugseng Johansen, 22, has shared a special post to celebrate the occasion on social media.



She has posted two pictures of the pair together onboard a yacht on Instagram.

Striker Haaland was pictured with his arm around Johansen wearing an all-black outfit.

He was snapped in a black tank top, shorts, and sunglasses.

Haaland accessorized his look with a rosary necklace.

Meanwhile, Johansen appeared glammed up as she smiled in a sky blue dress and gold watch.

“Happy Birthday my love♥️,” Johansen captioned her post.



Her post comes just days after Haaland returned to Norway following the World Cup.

His side were knocked out of the tournament with their quarterfinal loss against England.

But the Manchester City striker has become a cult figure in the USA after leading the nation to their best-ever World Cup finish.

Fans have extended their birthday wishes to the two-time Premier League winner.

“happy birthday our love!” one fan said.



“happy birthdayyyy!!!🥹🥹👏👏❤️,” another commented

Now Haaland has looked to relax ahead of the new season by jetting off to Italy with his girlfriend.

Haaland is entering the third season of his mega ten-year Manchester City contract.

Sports.title: Al-Hilal HIJACK Man Utd and Aston Villa move for Crysencio Summerville as they agree £68MILLION transfer with West Ham
Sports.content:
SAUDI PRO LEAGUE giants Al-Hilal have agreed to sign Crysencio Summerville from West Ham.

The 24-year-old had been heavily linked with a move to Roma in recent days, with Aston Villa and Manchester United also understood to be interested.



But he now looks poised for a move to Saudi Arabia.

Al-Hilal have reached an agreement worth around £68million with West Ham for the winger.



A medical is also scheduled ahead of the proposed transfer.

Summerville – who made four appearances for the Netherlands at the World Cup this summer – is expected to pen a long-term contract with the Saudi Pro League outfit.

Roma had been the latest known club to submit a bid, reportedly worth £39m, for the Dutchman.

Man Utd also enquired about a potential deal, with Aston Villa expressing an interest.

Summerville has three years left on his West Ham contract but is one of several players likely to leave following the club’s Premier League relegation.

The winger has made 56 appearances for the Hammers since joining from Leeds United two years ago, scoring eight goals and providing seven assists.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Seven of those goals came last season.

West Ham have already sold Mateus Fernandes in an £85m deal with Tottenham this summer.

But in a huge boost, club captain Jarrod Bowen committed his future by signing a new contract.

He agreed new terms which include bonuses and a release clause should West Ham not win promotion at the first time of asking.



Bowen said: “The main motivation is staying and bringing this club back into the Premier League where we belong.”

Sports.title: Argentina hold open-top bus parade after LOSING World Cup final but Lionel Messi snubs it after flying home separately
Sports.content:
LIONEL MESSI was missing as Argentina held an open-top bus parade – despite being BEATEN in the World Cup final.

The sore losers returned to Buenos Aires after failing to win the tournament back-to-back in New Jersey.



Messi, 39, broke down in tears on the MetLife Stadium pitch after the South Americans were beaten by a single goal.

Meanwhile his team-mates got into scraps after the final whistle – with Nahuel Molina taking a swing at Rodri and Leandro Paredes lashing out at several Spain stars.





The shameful scenes came after Lionel Scaloni’s side failed to muster a single shot on target, instead focusing on gamesmanship rather than playing football.

But their pitiful showing did not stop them receiving a hero’s welcome as they touched back down in Argentina‘s capital.

Thousands of fans took to the streets to applaud the team as they made their way by bus back to their training complex.

Messi was a notable absentee after flying home separately from his team-mates – to his hometown of Rosario.



The eight-time Ballon d’Or winner faces a short turnaround with Inter Miami‘s season resuming this wee.

David Beckham’s side face Chicago Fire in the MLS on Thursday although the Argentina captain is sure to miss that as he spends time with his family.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Like all World Cup stars he is entitled to three weeks off after his exploits at the tournament.

Other Argentina stars who did not fly back with the team include Rodrigo De Paul, Cristian Romero, Julian Alvarez and Enzo Fernandez.



Boss Scaloni and Nicolas Otamendi were the first off the flight before being followed by the likes of Nicolas Tagliafico and Alexis Mac Allister.

Lisandro Martinez was also spotted walking off the plane with his suitcase and a bag.

The defender went off injury the first half of the final after appearing to hurt his leg.



He has opted to take the plane to his homeland rather than fly from New York to Manchester, where he lives.

Other players that were spotted included Leandro Paredes and Valentin Barco.

Barco became infamous in England after Argentina dumped the Three Lions in the semi-final.



He was filmed wildly celebrating in front of the English players and was slapped in the back of the head by Jude Bellingham.

The former Brighton flop could be seen with a fairly vacant expression on his face as he waited to board the team bus.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

There was plenty of pageantry for the World Cup final losers with a military band playing them in off the plane.

There was also a long red carpet rolled out for them all the way to the bus.

Sports.title: Everton join transfer race for Norway World Cup star, 35, with Man City and Leeds also considering move
Sports.content:
EVERTON have joined the race for Norway keeper Orjan Nyland.

The free agent, 35, was a smash hit for the World Cup quarter-finalists in North America.



SunSport revealed fellow Prem sides Manchester City and Leeds are tracking Nyland, who is out of contract after leaving Sevilla at the end of last season.

Veteran Nyland was outstanding in Norway‘s run to the last-eight where they lost to England 2-1 in extra-time.



He started five out of the six games in the Norwegians’ impressive World Cup campaign, keeping three clean sheets.

Nyland did not feature in the France clash that saw Stale Solbakken make ten changes.



The keeper saved 70 per cent of the shots he faced during the tournament and has now won more than 60 caps for Norway.

The ex-Aston Villa and Norwich man produced a standout display in the knockout win over five-time world champions Brazil.

England No1 Jordan Pickford is the first-choice for Everton boss David Moyes.

But back-up Mark Travers has been linked with a move away from the Hill Dickinson Stadium and that could free up space in the Toffees squad.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Enzo Maresca’s City have been looking around for keepers amid doubts over James Trafford‘s future.

Just home from the World Cup, Trafford, 23, has garnered attention from Premier League clubs, including Newcastle and Leeds.

The latter’s interest joined the race for the goalie after veteran Karl Darlow, 35, joined Manchester United on a free transfer.

Sports.title: Top Premier League referee, 47, RETIRES from football after 831 matches just days after World Cup exit
Sports.content:
TOP Premier League referee Anthony Taylor has retired just days after the World Cup ended.

Taylor, 47, was one of England’s most accomplished officials and one of two at the tournament alongside Michael Oliver.



Taylor’s final match was the last 16 clash between eventual winners Spain and Portugal in Dallas.

Spain clinched a 1-0 victory in Dallas after Mikel Merino scored a last-minute winner to set up a quarter-final against Belgium.



The referee ends his career after 16 Premier League seasons and 831 games – 668 of which were in England.

Taylor took charge of 432 Prem games and every major domestic cup final, including the 2017 and 2020 FA Cup finals.



He also spent 14 years as a Fifa official, reffing games at the 2022 and 2026 World Cups, and Euro 2020 and 2024.

Taylor was shortlisted to referee the 2022 World Cup final but was removed from consideration due to Argentina’s history with England over the Falklands.

Reflecting on his career, Taylor said: “Officiating at the elite level has been an immense privilege, but the pressure is intense and the scrutiny is constant. The time is now right to step aside and look forward to transitioning to the next chapter of my career.



“I want to express my deepest gratitude to my two assistants Gary and Adam, my refereeing colleagues and everyone connected with the game for all their support over the years.

“Most importantly, I want to thank my family and friends for their unwavering support throughout the immense sacrifices this career has demanded.”



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Howard Webb, Chief Refereeing Officer at Pro Ref, added: “Anthony has been a fantastic servant to the game over many years, both domestically and on the international stage.

“He has been repeatedly trusted to officiate in the biggest games including Portugal against Spain in this summer’s World Cup which ultimately capped off an outstanding career.

“He’s consistently demonstrated over a sustained period why he is one of the best and most successful officials that English football has ever produced, but it’s not just his on-field achievements that see him as a role model to many.

“The professionalism he’s shown and the support for his colleagues and the next generation of officials looking to follow in his footsteps is testament to his character.



“We thank him for his immense contribution to the game and wish him every success in the next chapter of his career.”

Taylor has been at the centre of some memorable Premier League moments – including the infamous confrontation between Antonio Conte and Thomas Tuchel after the match between Chelsea and Tottenham in 2022.

And in Europe, he received plenty of media attention after Jose Mourinho waited for him in the Puskas Arena VIP car park following Roma’s 2023 Europa League final defeat to Sevilla.



Mourinho called him a “disgrace” and heavily criticised his refereeing performance to reporters.

At the time, the then-Roma boss fumed: “This is a European final and with this kind of refereeing, it is hard to accept.

“If we talk about refereeing situations, it’s not two or three: it is many, quite apart from the big decisions.

“Those of us who have been in football a long time realise immediately what is going on.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Mourinho was eventually charged by Uefa for using “insulting/abusive language against a match official” numerous times.



Before becoming one of Europe’s top referees, Taylor served as an assistant at the 2014 Uefa Super Cup, the 2015 Europa League final and the finals of both the 2016 Champions League and European Championships.

Sports.title: Sir Alex Ferguson pays heartbreaking tribute to Kevin Keegan and reveals secret meeting after ‘love it if we beat them’
Sports.content:
SIR ALEX FERGUSON has admitted he had the “utmost respect” for old rival Kevin Keegan, who passed away on Monday.

Former Liverpool star, Newcastle boss and two-time Ballon d’Or winner Keegan died aged 75 after battling cancer.



He and Manchester United icon Fergie went toe-to-toe in the Premier League‘s early years, when Keegan was in charge of Toon.

But Ferguson reflected positively on their rivalry and credits the job his rival did on Tyneside.



The Scotsman told Track Radio: “I had the utmost respect for him.

“We had many duels when he was manager of Newcastle, but I have to say the job he did at Newcastle was fantastic.

“He re-energised that club and he brought that enthusiasm and fanaticism that great supporters can give. That’s the job he did.

“I must say, the challenges we had with Newcastle at that time at United were huge.

“Kevin carried the love of the game on his sleeve, there’s no question about that, and that carried right onto the fans, to the players.

“That period at Newcastle was of emotion, it was excitement. They brought great players to the club too and they added to it, and it gave Newcastle – I think – their best ever team.”



The managers’ rivalry peaked in 1996, when Newcastle blew a 12-point lead to hand United the league title.

Weeks before the end of the season, in late April, a fired-up Keegan famously admitted he would “love it” if his Toon side pipped the Red Devils.

He also said Ferguson had “gone down in his estimation” by hinting that teams were trying harder against United than they were against Newcastle.



But they let bygones be bygones in a pub near Wentworth Golf Club, where they spent a night around the piano shortly after the campaign ended.

Sir Alex continued: “The great thing about him, he held no grudges. That was a fantastic quality he had and we had a great night.

“All aside whatever happened in previous weeks, that was soon forgotten. I really respected him for that.”

Sports.title: West Ham strike £68m deal to sell Crysencio Summerville amid Man Utd interest
Sports.content:
West Ham strike £68m deal to sell Crysencio Summerville amid Man Utd interest

Manchester United were among the clubs linked with a move for West Ham winger Crysencio Summerville but it appears that the Dutchman is set to move elsewhere

View 2 Images Summerville is set to leave West Ham after two years (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester United are set to lose out on Crysencio Summerville, with the West Ham star on the verge of a move to Saudi Arabia. The Red Devils were linked with a swoop for the Dutchman this summer, following the Hammers’ relegation from the Premier League.

‌



They were interested in him alongside Mateus Fernandes, who eventually completed a big-money move to Tottenham Hotspur. But United are also set to be frustrated in their pursuit of the former Leeds man.

‌



The Londoners have agreed a £68m deal with Saudi Arabian side Al-Hilal. Italian giants Roma were also interested but were only willing to offer around £39m.

‌



Summerville, who scored five Premier League goals last term, is now expected to undergo a medical ahead of completing his switch to the Middle East. West Ham in the meantime will aim to re-invest the considerable fee as they attempt to earn promotion from the Championship at the first time of asking.

The only signing that the Hammers have made so far is a deal for Venezuelan international Keiber Lamadrid. But one considerable boost has been Jarrod Bowen’s decision to commit his future to the club.

Sports.title: Sepp Blatter blasts FIFA and Gianni Infantino and says World Cup 'lost its credibility'
Sports.content:
Sepp Blatter blasts FIFA and Gianni Infantino and says World Cup 'lost its credibility'

FIFA president Gianni Infantino has faced severe criticism during the World Cup for his close relationship with US President Donald Trump with controversial former chief Sepp Blatter among those to speak out

View 2 Images Sepp Blatter has taken a fresh swipe at Gianni Infantino (Image: Getty Images)

Sepp Blatter has once again called for ‘new leadership’ at FIFA in a brutal dig at Gianni Infantino. The current president has faced serious criticism for a number of decisions throughout this summer’s World Cup.

‌



Ticket prices, over-commercialisation, as well as his close relationship with US President Donald Trump have all been issues. Criticism then sharply increased after the decision to suspend Folarin Balogun’s red card following a phone call from Trump.

‌



Blatter tore into Infantino immediately after that decision. Taking to Twitter, he said: “Red cards are not overturned by political phone calls. They are overturned by rules, evidence and independent bodies.

‌



"If a U.S. President intervenes with the FIFA President — and a player is suddenly cleared before a World Cup knockout match — the question is unavoidable: Quo vadis, FIFA? Quo vadis means 'Where are you going?' in Latin. Football must never become a playground for political power.”

Blatter has now doubled down with a fresh post calling for change right at the top of the organisation just days after the World Cup final.

Lionel Messi sparks conspiracy theories as footage from World Cup final speech leaked READ MORE :

He said: “The longest World Cup has come to an end - with the right champions. But on the way to the final whistle, the tournament had lost its credibility. Politics must not be allowed to overshadow the game. Now it is up to the fans, players and national associations to reclaim football and bring it back to its roots under new leadership.”

‌



While Blatter has called for fresh leadership, it appears that is unlikely. La Liga president Javier Tebas has claimed that due to a lack of opposition, it appears that Infantino is set to stay in charge.

Asked if he should quit, Tebas replied: "In my opinion, yes, I think his time is up." He added: "There's no opposition candidate, nobody wants to stand just to lose. He shouldn't stay, but the current state of affairs means he won't leave.

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino has faced plenty of criticism throughout the World Cup (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"These past few days here in America, I've heard many people who are against Infantino, who disagree with what he's doing,

"They say it, but then they do nothing. I don't know what's worse, the silence or the complicity, because those who stay silent are perfectly aware of the damage football is suffering.

"The suspension of the American player's ban was absolutely serious. They were lucky that Belgium eliminated the USA, because otherwise a case could have arisen that might have cost Infantino his job. Since Belgium won, they managed to bury the matter. But these things are just the tip of the iceberg."

Sports.title: FSG confirm Liverpool sale talks as billionaire family eyes deal after resignation
Sports.content:
FSG confirm Liverpool sale talks as billionaire family eyes deal after resignation

Fenway Sports Group have confirmed that a consortium of investors, led by British-Indian businessman Amit Bhatia, have approached them about a significant minority stake in Liverpool

View 2 Images FSG are in talks over selling a minority stake in Liverpool (Image: Getty Images)

Liverpool's owners have confirmed that a consortium of investors, spearheaded by British-Indian businessman Amit Bhatia, have made an approach regarding a stake in the club. It is understood the group has the backing of the Mittal family, whose fortune was most recently estimated at more than £26billion by Forbes.

‌



No deal is currently in place and discussions remain at a preliminary stage, according to sources with knowledge of the situation. Bhatia was confirmed on Tuesday to have stepped down from his role as co-owner of Queens Park Rangers, with the London outfit announcing his exit on its official website.

‌



Bhatia is the son-in-law of Lakshmi Mittal, who heads up ArcelorMittal, the globe's biggest steel and mining firm, and Fenway Sports Group confirmed that active talks are underway over what has been characterised as a "significant minority stake".

‌



Kevin Keegan's final picture and brave public appearance before sad death aged 75 READ MORE :

Our sister title the Liverpool ECHO understand the discussions are being treated as comparable to the deal struck with Dynasty Equity in 2023, which was valued at between £82m and £164m. An FSG statement provided to the ECHO said: "An investment consortium led, managed and represented by Amit Bhatia has expressed interest in making a strategic minority investment in Liverpool Football Club."

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Mr Bhatia has thus far refused to comment on the developments but made public his decision to resign from QPR on Tuesday, having joined the club at Loftus Road almost two decades ago. Bhatia said: "Since joining the club in 2007, QPR has been a deeply important part of my life, and of my family's life. Over nearly two decades we have shared promotions, relegations, unforgettable highs and painful lows, and the memories we have made at Loftus Road alongside the supporters will stay with us forever.

‌



View 2 Images Amit Bhatia could soon have a stake in Liverpool (Image: Andrew Fosker/REX/Shutterstock)

"Being part of QPR has shaped me in many ways. It has taught me about resilience, responsibility and the importance of stewardship. I am especially proud of the work of QPR in the Community Trust, which reflects the best of the club and the extraordinary role it plays in the local community.

"I step back from my formal responsibilities with pride, gratitude and affection. I want to thank the players, managers, staff, the Community Trust, my fellow board members and, above all, the fans, who have made me and my family feel part of the QPR family for so many years.

‌



"I am grateful to my dear friend Ruben and his family for their friendship and partnership, as I am to Richard, Lee, Christian and everyone continuing to work on behalf of the club. QPR will always have a very special place in my heart."

FSG snapped up Liverpool for £300m back in October 2010. More than 15 years on, the 20-time Premier League champions have been valued at £5.2 billion by the prestigious American financial publication Forbes.

Earlier this year, the club recorded revenues exceeding £700m for the first time in their history.

Article continues below

In 2024, Fenway began exploring the possibility of establishing a multi-club ownership model, but have since put those plans on ice — a move that ultimately contributed to the departure of Michael Edwards, Liverpool's former sporting director, who had been appointed as FSG's CEO of football two years ago.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo 'likes' post calling FIFA 'corrupt' after Lionel Messi's run to World Cup final
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo 'likes' post calling FIFA 'corrupt' after Lionel Messi's run to World Cup final

Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo both played in their last World Cup this summer albeit the Argentina managed to go all the way to the final at the age of 39

View 2 Images Cristiano Ronaldo's Portugal went out of the World Cup at the last 16 stage (Image: Getty Images)

Cristiano Ronaldo has seemingly liked an Instagram post calling FIFA ‘corrupt’ and ‘mafia-like’ just days after the World Cup final. The Portugal icon played in his final tournament this summer, with his nation having reached the round of 16.

‌



Portugal were eventually beaten by Spain. Ronaldo’s long-term rival Lionel Messi did considerably better, having led Argentina to the final just four years after lifting the trophy in Qatar.

‌



There was some criticism about their run this time though, with some claiming that the South American nation got some more than favourable refereeing decisions throughout the duration of the tournament.

‌



Spanish journalists Pilar Rodrigues Losantos and Ruben Amon discussed exactly that with FIFA being labelled as “one of the most corrupt institutions on the planet”, as well as “abject, mafia-like, and shameful organisation” by the pair.

Three things the Premier League must steal from World Cup 2026 and four things it must ditch READ MORE :

World Cup Golden Boot winner confirmed after Kylian Mbappe and Lionel Messi battle READ MORE :

Ronaldo appeared to like a video of the pair’s discussion on Instagram. Messi for his part spoke out in the aftermath of his side’s final heartbreak.

He said: “The pain is immense, and this wound will take time to heal. But I also hold onto all the good things... The matches we turned around by giving it our all - moments that will remain in our memories forever - and the support of an entire country which, combined with this group's hard work and effort, brought us back among the world's elite once again.

‌



"It is hard to fully appreciate our achievement right now, but this group reached two consecutive World Cup finals. Thank you from the bottom of my heart for every greeting and message.

View 2 Images Lionel Messi reached the World Cup final in his final tournament (Image: Getty Images)

"Once again, we managed to unite as a country and stand together, sharing the immense pride of being Argentine. I also want to congratulate Spain on winning the championship."

‌



Ronaldo also released his own statement following Portugal’s exit at the hands of the eventual champions. He said: "I'm sad to be leaving the World Cup like this.

"I gave it my all. I did my best. It was my last World Cup, yes, but I'll now have time to reflect and be with my family. I won't be making any rash decisions.

"I don't decide anything in the heat of the moment. Now is not important whether I will continue [to play]. Tomorrow I will get up the same way I got up today: with a clear conscience.

Article continues below

"I played 23 years in the national team and won three titles. Before Cristiano, Portugal had not won anything. The Euros was the most important. For me, 2016 has the same dimension as a World Cup, honestly."

Sports.title: Kevin Keegan shared three things people will remember him for in heartbreaking final interview
Sports.content:
Kevin Keegan shared three things people will remember him for in heartbreaking final interview

Former Newcastle United and Liverpool star Kevin Keegan has passed away after a battle with cancer and the English football legend was never shy when talking about his career

View 2 Images Kevin Keegan is an iconic figure of English football (Image: BBC Sport)

Kevin Keegan admitted before his death that people mainly remember him for his hair, an appearance on TV show Superstars and his famous "love it if we beat them" line. The 75-year-old died after being diagnosed with cancer.

‌



'King Kev' had an illustrious playing career and built one of the most popular teams of the Premier League era at Newcastle United. The former forward leaves his wife of 51 years, Jean, and their children, Laura Jane, 47, and Sarah Marie, 43.

‌



In a statement released on Monday, his family said: "It is with immense sadness that we announce that Kevin Keegan has passed away at the age of 75. The former England player and manager had been battling cancer and was surrounded by his wife and daughters in his final moments.

‌



"Kevin, a double Ballon D’or winner, was a much loved husband, father and grandfather. The family would like to thank Kevin’s incredible medical team for all their support. This is a hugely difficult time and they are requesting space and privacy."

Kevin Keegan planned one last St James' Park visit before cancer death to see fans he loved READ MORE :

As a player, he was fearless, and famous for his Brut adverts with Henry Cooper, pop singles, curly perm, and an episode of the TV show 'Superstars', filmed in Bracknell in 1976, where he fell in a bike ride but got back on again despite being injured.

In the late 90s, he managed a Newcastle side nicknamed 'The Entertainers' because of their fearless brand of attacking football. Keegan famously said, "I will love it if we beat them," in a TV outburst aimed at then Manchester United manager Sir Alex Ferguson, after the Magpies gave up a 12-point lead and were beaten to the title by United in 1996.

‌



That reaction came after Ferguson questioned whether Leeds United and Nottingham Forest would try as hard against Newcastle as they would against his Red Devils side. And Keegan recalled his career in a BBC interview before his death.

He said: "It's a lesson in life. You can win the Ballon d'Or, you can win the European Cup, you can win all the league titles you want, but people remember me from my hair, the perm, they remember me falling off a bike in Superstars, a lot of people, and they remember the 'I'd love it if we beat them'.

View 2 Images Kevin Keegan and Sir Alex Ferguson went head to head for the title in the 95/96 season

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

He said: "It's a lesson in life. You can win the Ballon d'Or, you can win the European Cup, you can win all the league titles you want, but people remember me from my hair, the perm, they remember me falling off a bike in Superstars, a lot of people, and they remember the 'I'd love it if we beat them'.

"So it's life. You have to accept it.

‌



"It doesn't matter what you think; it's what other people think. It was, [the love it if we beat them line], probably at that time a realisation that we weren't going to win the league."

Ferguson recalled a heartwarming encounter with Keegan, just days after the famous outburst. In an interview with Track Radio, the Scot said: "That was Kevin, he was all emotion and he brought that to the team as well. They played for Kevin Keegan, there's no question about that.

"The interesting thing about the outburst from Kevin, two weeks after the season had finished, I was playing golf with some friends and went to a great bar up the road, nice food. We went up there, and who walks in? Kevin Keegan and he spent the rest of the night on the piano.

Article continues below

"The best thing about him is he held no grudges, that was a fantastic quality he had. We had a great night, he would always say - whatever happened in previous weeks, that was soon forgotten. I really respected him for that."

Sports.title: Lamine Yamal trolls Argentina's Leandro Paredes during Spain victory parade
Sports.content:
Lamine Yamal trolls Argentina's Leandro Paredes during Spain victory parade

The World Cup final between Spain and Argentina ended in drama with Ferran Torres’ goal securing the title, while the South American side had two men sent off including Leandro Paredes

View Image Lamine Yamal during Spain's World Cup celebrations (Image: Getty Images)

Spain star Lamine Yamal mocked Leandro Paredes with a fake boxing fight days after his World Cup final brawl. The European nation secured the World Cup on Sunday in New Jersey, Ferran Torres’ goal sealing victory in extra time.

‌



Argentina also had two men sent off, with Enzo Fernandez being dismissed for two bookable offences including a horrendous tackle on Pau Cubarsi. Paredes was then sent off for angry clashes with both Eric Garcia and Gavi after the full-time whistle.

‌



During Spain’s open-top bus parade, Yamal appeared to mock the Argentina midfielder with a sign reading: “Velada del ano VII: Paredes vs Gav.”

‌



The Velada del Ano is a boxing event similar to the UK’s Misfits. Paredes, 32, has spoken out in the aftermath of Argentina’s World Cup heartbreak but refused to apologise for his actions.

Emi Martinez hints he could quit Argentina duty after World Cup final loss READ MORE :

Lionel Messi snubs Argentina parade as he flies home separately from disgraced team-mates READ MORE :

Taking to social media, he wrote: "THANK YOU, ARGENTINA!!! I LOVE YOU, TODAY AND ALWAYS.

"Today, I write with a heavy heart, having been unable to bring our country the joy it so richly deserves - but with a chest full of pride for having given everything we had and for flying our flag at the very top once again!

‌



"Thank you to everyone who was part of this national team—to this group of players who gave their all to represent this jersey, fighting for it until the very last second of every match! It was an honour to be part of the best Argentine national team in history."

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Elsewhere, FIFA have launched an investigation into the incident with potential disciplinary breaches having been identified.

‌



A statement from world football’s governing body read: “Following an assessment of the relevant match reports for the FIFA World Cup final between Spain and Argentina, and in line with article 36 of the FIFA disciplinary code (FDC), the FIFA disciplinary committee has appointed a disciplinary and ethics prosecutor to investigate potential breaches of the FDC with regard to the post-match incidents.

“Further details will be communicated by the FIFA disciplinary committee once the prosecutor’s report has been completed.”

Paredes is not the only one in possible trouble after the final at MetLife Stadium. Teammate Nahuel Molina was also seen throwing a punch towards Rodri as he ran to celebrate with his Spain teammates at the full-time whistle.

Sports.title: Broad: England Test job less attractive than it was
Sports.content:
Former England bowler Stuart Broad says he understands Andy Flower's decision to turn down the England Test job, and is unsure over who the ECB turn to next, pondering whether the role has become "less attractive".

Brendon McCullum was removed as England's Test head coach after a run of seven defeats in nine and Flower, who led the team to victory in the three Ashes series during his previous spell in charge between 2009 and 2014, quickly emerged as the favourite to replace him.

But Flower cited his current coaching commitments with Indian Premier League franchise Royal Challengers Bengaluru, as well as The Hundred's London Spirit - which would overlap with the English cricket season - as a reason to rule himself out of contention.

Image: Andy Flower was previously coach of Trent Rockets in The Hundred but will be in charge of London Sprit for the 2026 tournament

"Andy Flower is one of the best coaches in the world," Broad told Sky Sports News. "He's done brilliantly with RCB to win back-to-back IPL titles. And he's now gone to the London Spirit from the Trent Rockets.

"I support his decision, really. He's got a very comfortable, steady job at the moment. He's got two brilliant franchises that he works with consistently and he's growing something very special.

"Would he want to leave that for the pressures of and the unknown of the ECB and the Test match job at the moment? Probably not."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Nasser Hussain and Michael Atherton discuss who they think should replace Brendon McCullum as the England Test head coach.

Broad added: "Five, 10 years ago, this was a very sought-after job. I think with the franchise world that surrounds cricket at the moment, it's less attractive.

"But it's still attractive to the right person, and there will be people keen to do that job."

Justin Langer, Darren Lehmann and Jonathan Trott are some of the other names to have been linked with the England Test job.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Southern Brave and Australia all-rounder Marcus Stoinis says Justin Langer's work ethic would make him a good choice if selected to be England's next men's Test head coach.

Broad has "absolutely no idea" who the ECB turn to next, but warned that the "grass isn't always greener" as they look to replace McCullum.

"I saw a very positive side to Brendon McCullum," Broad said. "I'm not saying that results were acceptable at all, in the last year really.

"But unless you get someone better than McCullum, then it's a poor decision. So I'm very interested to see what's coming.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player James Cole breaks down Brendon McCullum's departure from his role as England Test coach and looks into why 'something had to give' for the ECB.

"I don't know who's on their shortlist. I heard [ECB chief executive] Richard Gould talk about succession planning, that they have six to 10 names for every role.

"I don't know how true that can be if the first guy you go to says 'no, I'm not interested.'"

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Stuart Broad's reaction to news that Jacob Bethell will miss The Hundred due to a knee injury he picked up on England duty in the ODI series with India.

'Difficult for Brook to captain in all three formats'

England also have to name a replacement Test captain following Ben Stokes' retirement during the series-ending Test defeat to New Zealand at Trent Bridge in June.

Harry Brook was Stokes' vice-captain and is currently in charge of the white-ball sides, leading to workload concerns if he were to also take the Test job - along with how the move would look after Brook was disciplined during the winter following an altercation with a nightclub bouncer in New Zealand the day before captaining an ODI.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Harry Brook pays tribute to Ben Stokes following his retirement from international cricket and insists that he is up to the challenge of becoming the next England Test captain.

"I think [captaining] three formats is difficult depending on how long you do it," Broad said. "Ultimately, he's one of our best players, so you want him fulfilling his potential with the bat.

"He's done a brilliant job with the T20 side, particularly, and the question will be whether he wants to give that away with T20 World Cups that come around every couple of years?

"He's also got a 50-over World Cup next October in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia, in what will feel like English conditions and will suit them.

"Does he want to give that away to then focus on the Test match job, which brings its own challenges and pressures? There's definitely more pressure in the Test match job than there is in white ball.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Eoin Morgan and Michael Atherton debate what the next steps are for England cricket after Ben Stokes' retirement.

"It's a really interesting call for [director of men's cricket] Rob Key. There's a lot on his shoulders at the minute.

"It's been a disastrous start to the summer from his and England's point of view after the so-called reset [following the 4-1 Ashes defeat in the winter].

"Really big decisions coming their way, and Harry Brook will probably have a decision to make at some stage."

Sports.title: Stokes scores century in first match for Durham after England retirement
Sports.content:
Former England captain Ben Stokes hit a match-winning hundred in his first appearance for Durham following his international retirement.

Stokes struck an unbeaten 108 off 123 balls, hitting 10 boundaries and three sixes, and suffered from cramp at the back end of his innings as Durham chased down 257 to beat Derbyshire by five wickets in the Metro Bank One-Day Cup.

It was Stokes' 10th List A century, and first for Durham since 2014, coming less than a month after he announced his retirement from England duty during the series-ending Test defeat to New Zealand at Trent Bridge.

Sports.title: SunRisers thrash MI London in Hundred opener as Cross suffers injury scare
Sports.content:
SunRisers Leeds Women kicked off a new era for The Hundred with a seven-wicket win over MI London as two teams who have undergone name changes following heavy overseas investment met at The Kia Oval.

Sunrisers, who won the title last year under their Northern Superchargers name, limited MI London, formerly known as Oval Invincibles, to 107-8 once they snapped an opening stand of 57 between Hayley Matthews (33) and Danni Wyatt-Hodge (29).

The visitors then eased to their target with 31 balls to spare as Australian opener Phoebe Litchfield (43 off 26) bounced back from running out her countrywomen Jess Jonassen (14) after attempting a single that was never on.

Another Aussie, Annabel Sutherland, contributed 30 not off 23 deliveries, while skipper Dani Gibson (12no off 7) spanked the winning boundary.

Score summary – MI London Women vs SunRisers Leeds Women MI London 107-8 from 100 balls: Hayley Matthews (33 off 22 balls), Danni Wyatt-Hodge (29 off 20); Hannah Baker (2-16), Dani Gibson (2-17), (Deepti Sharma (2-20) Sunrisers Leeds 109-3 from 69 balls: Phoebe Litchfield (43 off 26), Annabel Sutherland (30no off 13), Dani Gibson (12no off 7); Alexa Stonehouse (1-12), Kirstie Gordon (1-17)

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player SunRisers' Jess Jonassen was 'barbecued' by Phoebe Litchfield as she was run out for 14

The one sour note for SunRisers was the shoulder injury suffered by Kate Cross, shortly after she had taken an excellent running catch at long-on to dismiss Wyatt-Hodge.

Cross landed awkwardly fielding at extra-cover and walked off in pain - she has not dislocated her shoulder but will undergo scans.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player SunRisers' Kate Cross was taken off the field with a shoulder injury

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Cross had earlier taken a terrific catch to dismiss former England team-mate Danni Wyatt Hodge

Gibson (2-17) - the most expensive English player in the Hundred auction earlier this year as SunRisers forked out £190k for her - chipped in with two wickets, including that of Australia's Nicola Carey (5), bowled by a cross-seamer.

Wyatt-Hodge, West Indies skipper Matthews and New Zealand captain Melie Kerr (13) all fell to spin.

Deepti Sharma (2-20) accounted for Wyatt-Hodge and Matthews - the latter was out to a sharp caught-and-bowled by the India all-rounder - while young English leg-spinner Hannah Baker removed Kerr during her 2-16.

'Litchfield looks like best player in the world'

Sky Sports Cricket's Stuart Broad on Phoebe Litchfield:

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports Cricket's Stuart Broad had high praise for Phoebe Litchfield after she helped SunRisers to victory over MI London

"She looks the best player in the world to me - she has everything covered.

"She can hit the ball anywhere, has so much time, opens up the off-side and drives the ball beautifully.

"In addition, she uses her feet when the wicketkeeper is up. She might move a bit too much at times but she has incredible talent.

"The sound off the bat is just different - it is when top-level players hit the ball - and she can score 360."

Wednesday's Hundred double-header comes from the Utilita Bowl in Southampton as Southern Brave take on Welsh Fire.

Sports.title: Premier League referee Taylor retires
Sports.content:
Long-serving Premier League referee Anthony Taylor is standing down after 16 years in England's top flight at the conclusion of the World Cup.

The 47-year-old hangs up his whistle following 831 games in the English, European and international game, with his final match the World Cup last-16 clash between Portugal and tournament winners Spain.

Domestically, Taylor refereed in every major domestic English cup final, officiating the 2017 and 2020 FA Cup finals and the 215 League Cup final, as well as 432 Premier League matches.

He also served for 14 years on the FIFA international list, and was selected to represent England at both the 2022 and 2026 World Cups.

Anthony Taylor's career in numbers 668 professional matches in England

16 seasons in the Premier League

432 top-flight matches

Officiated every major domestic cup final

14 years on FIFA International List

163 international matches

Two World Cups (2022 and 2026), two European Championships (2020 and 2024) and two Club World Cups (2022 and 2025)

Gave 14 yellow cards in a Premier League match - the most ever

In announcing his retirement, Taylor suggested his decision had been fuelled by the "intense" pressure and "constant" scrutiny he faced in the role.

Speaking in a statement through refereeing body Pro Ref, formerly PGMOL, Taylor said: "Officiating at the elite level has been an immense privilege, but the pressure is intense and the scrutiny is constant. The time is now right to step aside and look forward to transitioning to the next chapter of my career."

He was publicly targeted by Roma fans at Budapest Airport in 2023 after being criticised by their then-manager Jose Mourinho following the club's Europa League final defeat by Sevilla.

Last year, he revealed his family no longer came to matches he was officiating while criticising the "expectation of perfection" placed on referees and admitted he had repeatedly considered quitting the game.

Commenting on the incident in Hungary, he told BBC Sport: "That's for sure the worst situation I've dealt with in terms of abuse.

"Not only because I was travelling with family members at the time, but it also highlights the impact of people's behaviour on others.

"It makes you reflect back on whether you made a mistake travelling with your family in the first place."

Taylor refereed more Premier League games than anyone else in 2025/26, with his last game West Ham's final-day 3-0 win over Leeds, which was not enough to save the Hammers from relegation to the Championship.

The Premier League has no set limit on retirement age for referees, with a number of officials continuing into their 50s including Neil Swarbrick and Graham Scott, who refereed in the top flight until they were 52 and 56 respectively.
