Sports.title: Lionel Messi tells Argentina stars to ‘relax and forget everything’ in cryptic message moments before World Cup final
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi tells Argentina stars to ‘relax and forget everything’ in cryptic message moments before World Cup final

New footage shows Lionel Messi telling his Argentina teammates to 'forget about everything else' moments before their World Cup final defeat.

The football icon was unable to inspire his country to back-to-back World Cup titles on Sunday as they were beaten 1-0 by Spain after extra-time in a one-sided final.

3 Messi was in tears after collecting his World Cup runners-up medal Credit: Getty

Ferran Torres scored the decisive goal in the 106th-minute, as La Roja finally made their possession and man advantage count.

But their victory was marred by ugly scenes afterwards, with a mass brawl breaking out when Argentina's players were involved in a series of bust-ups, which saw Leandro Paredes initially sent off having thrown punches.

Messi was left heartbroken by the defeat in New York, breaking down in tears after receiving his World Cup runners-up medal.

At 39, there is widespread speculation that he could have played his last match for Argentina.

The sporting great is yet to make an announcement on his international future, but some believe he may have informed his teammates of just prior to kick-off.

'Concentrate on playing'

Newly released footage of the moments leading up to Sunday's final has led to many question what was said in the Argentina dressing room before the game.

In a video captured by Argentine television company RLC Noticias, Messi can be seen addressing his teammates as they prepare to head out down the tunnel, who all appear downbeat.

He tells the players: "Let's go, boys, [let's keep] calm people, calm. The main thing is for us to remain calm, boys, that we remain calm.

"Let's just concentrate on playing, nothing else - calm, okay? Forget everything else.

"Let's just play, let's just concentrate on playing. Let's go."

Messi's cryptic message has led to speculation over whether Argentina were in the right frame of mind heading into the final.

It is currently unclear what exactly the Albiceleste captain was telling his teammates to forget about, although some believe it could be in response to him announcing his international retirement to them.

This would perhaps explain the emotionally charged performance from the 2022 world champions in the final.

While they were typically aggressive, this boiled over in the latter stages, with Enzo Fernandez being sent off towards the end of normal time.

And Argentina lost all composure after the final whistle, as an ugly brawl unfolded, which saw Paredes throw punches at Gavi and Eric Garcia, while Nahuel Molina struck Spain captain Rodri.

Meanwhile, others have pondered whether Messi had been urging his teammates to ignore the accusations of preferential treatment they had faced throughout the tournament.

3 Messi could be set to retire from Argentina duty having scored 125 goals in 207 appearances for them Credit: AFP

The last dance?

After what was almost certainly his last ever appearance at the World Cup, Messi released an emotional statement.

He wrote on Instagram: "The pain is immense, and it will take time for this wound to heal. But I also hold on to all the good.

"The matches we turned around, giving our all, matches that will forever remain in our memories, the support of an entire country that, together with the hard work and effort of this group, led us to be, once again, among the best in the world.

"Today it's hard to fully appreciate what we accomplished, but this group reached two consecutive World Cup finals.

"Thank you from the bottom of my heart for every greeting and every message. Once again, we managed to unite as a country and be together, sharing the immense pride of being Argentinian.

"I also want to congratulate Spain on winning the championship."

3 The football icon missed out on winning a second World Cup, after his crowning moment in 2022 Credit: AFP

Messi scored eight goals and assisted another four for Argentina in their World Cup run - only failing to contribute against Spain.

He hinted at possible retirement before kick-off as his boots for the final had 'El Ultimo Tango', which is 'The Last Tango', written on them.

However, he is under contract at Inter Miami until December 2028, and there is nothing concrete in regards to him calling it quits.

Sports.title: Liverpool could become worth $6billion as club enters talks with consortium backed by Mittal family
Sports.content:
Liverpool could become worth $6billion as club enters talks with consortium backed by Mittal family

A consortium backed by the Mittal family are in talks with Liverpool to buy a minority stake in the club, talkSPORT understands.

Negotiations are happening between the Reds and the consortium led by Amit Bhatia, but nothing is finalised at this stage.



2 Liverpool could be become worth more than $6billion if deal is completed Credit: Getty

Bhatia, who left his position as director and co-owner of Queens Park Rangers on Tuesday, is the son-in-law of billionaire Lakshmi Mittal.

Liverpool's owners, Fenway Sports Group, have confirmed that they have been approached in a statement.

It reads: “An investment consortium led, managed, and represented by Amit Bhatia has expressed interest in making a strategic minority investment in Liverpool Football Club."



The club is expected to be valued at more than $6billion in any transaction, which is one of the highest valuations ever.

It is reported that Bhatia has hired advisers to work on an offer amid the negotiations with current owners FSG.



However, he has yet to comment on the ongoing talks.

Freeing up for a new investment

As mentioned, Bhatia departed QPR on Tuesday by transferring his ownership to majority owner Ruben Gnanalingam.

He is said to have done this to avoid holding a stake in two clubs, which owners are not allowed to do in English football.



Speaking after his exit, Bhatia said: “Since joining the club in 2007, QPR has been a deeply important part of my life, and of my family’s life. Over nearly two decades we have shared promotions, relegations, unforgettable highs and painful lows, and the memories we have made at Loftus Road alongside the supporters will stay with us forever.

“I step back from my formal responsibilities with pride, gratitude and affection. I want to thank the players, managers, staff, the Community Trust, my fellow board members and, above all, the fans, who have made me and my family feel part of the QPR family for so many years."

Who are the Mittal family?

Lakshmi Mittal is the executive chairman of ArcelorMittal, who are the world's second-biggest steelmaking company.

He is also the chairman of stainless steel manufacturer Aperam.

The Mittal family are also involved in Indian Premier League cricket side Rajasthan Royals, holding a 75 per cent stake.



They also have a three per cent stake in QPR.

Bhatia is married to Lakshmi's daughter Vanisha Mittal.

And the family are now working on a deal to acquire a stake in Liverpool and make it one of the highest-valued clubs.

2 Mittal is a billionaire who has made his money in the steel industry Credit: Getty

Liverpool could become worth $6bn

With the prospect of becoming worth $6bn potentially becoming a reality, Liverpool would join an elite list.

The Reds are already one of the biggest clubs on the planet, but they would be fourth if they were officially valued that high.



According to Forbes, Real Madrid are the highest-valued side at a whopping $9.5bn, with Barcelona at $7.5bn.

Manchester United, who sold 25 per cent of the club to Sir Jim Ratcliffe for £1.25bn in 2023, are valued at $7.2bn.

Liverpool would slot in behind their Premier League rivals and above European giants Paris Saint-Germain and Bayern Munich.

Manchester City, Arsenal and Chelsea are sixth, seventh and eighth on the 2026 list of most-valuable clubs in the world.

Sports.title: Lamine Yamal mocks Argentina brute Leandro Paredes with hilarious sign at Madrid's celebration parade after star's shameful violence at the World Cup final - as red carded villain claims they represented nation 'in best possible way'
Sports.content:
Spain superstar Lamine Yamal mocked Argentina brute Leandro Paredes with a punchy sign at the champions' World Cup celebrations in Madrid.

Two million supporters crowded the streets of the capital to welcome their heroes after they defeated Argentina 1-0 in the World Cup final.

But the immediate aftermath of the match was marred by the barbarous antics of Paredes, who attacked two Spain players.

He grabbed Eric Garcia by the throat before shoving over substitute Gavi, causing a large-scale melee in the middle of the pitch - and it's that second act to which Yamal's sign referred.

Yamal held up a sign which read: 'Velada del ano VII: Paredes vs Gavi'. The Velada del Ano is a celebrity boxing event in Spain, not unlike Misfits.

Argentina were widely condemned for their behaviour after losing the final - but they have maintained a siege mentality following the game.

Midfielder Enzo Fernandez, who was sent off in normal time, claimed that they had represented their nation in the 'best way possible'.

Lamine Yamal mocked Argentina's Leandro Paredes at celebrations in Madrid, holding up a sign referring to his altercation with Gavi after the World Cup final

Boca Juniors midfielder Paredes was lambasted after the whistle for punching Eric Garcia and pushing Gavi to the ground

He said: 'As time passes, you realize there is something much bigger than a result.

'For years, this group has represented our country in the best possible way.

'It teaches that competing isn’t just about winning, but about giving everything for the shirt and never giving up. Being part of this group, which has always stood up, competed to the very end, and defended these colors with pride, humility, and commitment, is something I’ll always cherish.

'I want to thank all the Argentine fans. Thank you for always being there, for supporting us in every match, for your affection, for your unconditional support, and for making us feel at home no matter where we are in the world.

'Wearing my country’s shirt is the greatest honour of my career, and I will continue to give everything I have every time I’m called upon to defend it.'

Defending the shirt with violence is another matter, though, and the BBC's pundits weren't impressed. Micah Richards said of Argentina's behaviour: 'It's embarrassing. They were on the cusp every single time.

'Seeing that sort of stuff after the game was played, it's not good, it's embarrassing to be honest. Paredes is better than that. We all know what it's like to lose a game but this is not good enough.'

Joe Hart had a similar opinion, saying: 'Disgusting behaviour. There was one man on that pitch with class and that was Lionel Messi.'

Captain Rodri lifted the World Cup as Spain touched down in Madrid yesterday

Yamal carried his luggage, including an oversized Hermes Birkin bag, off the plane

Wayne Rooney also said: 'It doesn't surprise me. We've seen this from Argentina before. It's just sad, very poor from them.

'If you lose a game of football, be graceful. It's a reaction to them being outplayed. Enzo Fernandez has got what he deserves.'

Argentina were thuggish throughout the World Cup final, just as they had been against England in the semis.

Chelsea star Fernandez complained against his dismissal for a second yellow but his late foul on Pau Cubarsi, which sent the defender flying, was atrocious.

Boca Juniors midfielder Paredes was also fortunate to not be sent off in regular time for a foul on the edge of the box which presented Yamal with a last-breath free-kick before extra-time.

Argentina only had two shots in the entire match, the first of which came in the 117th minute.

By contrast, they were trigger-happy on the fouls with 24 - though Spain didn't have clean hands themselves, as they gave away 21.

Alan Shearer said: 'There's a way to lose. Too many times we've seen that reaction from them. They were trying to win free-kicks and their reaction after full time was terrible. The best team won. It's a result for football because of the way Spain have played.'

Spain were in high spirits as they celebrated winning the World Cup on their bus home to Madrid in the early hours of yesterday

Festivities in the hotel were limited to a bottle of £1,000 red wine drunk by Marcos Llorente, goalscorer Ferran Torres and Marc Pubill

Marc Cucurella and Gavi posed in front of the team's Airbus as they prepared to go home

The airplane arrived hours later as the city of Madrid readied a welcome home fit for heroes

Aymeric Laporte and Alex Baena both posed with the World Cup trophy onboard their plane

Even Lionel Messi didn't rise above the dark arts. The legendary forward was lambasted by Wayne Rooney after he tried to get Marc Cucurella sent off during the latter stages of the game.

The game descended into chaos when Fernandez received his second yellow card.

This led to a melee between both sets of players and Cucurella was spotted saying something to Messi.

The left-back then put a couple of fingers over his mouth and continued speaking, a move which the Argentine immediately reacted to and waved over the referee.

As per FIFA's rules for this tournament, if a player holds their hand over their mouth in a confrontational situation, they will be sent off.

This was seen with Miguel Almiron for Paraguay in the group stage and Piero Hincapie in the knockout stages for Ecuador.

However, it didn't appear that Cucurella was speaking in a confrontational manner and the referee, nor VAR, decided to intervene.

The BBC pundits were quick to hit out at Messi's behaviour as his team headed into extra time a man down.

Rodri led a bus full of Spanish players in rounds of singing as they headed for Newark airport

Yamal had previously enjoyed a cigar in the lift as he began his journey back to Spain

The prodigious Barcelona star had celebrated earlier on the pitch with his girlfriend Ines Garcia

Hart said: 'Oh wow! Wow! Yeah, I didn't enjoy that at all from Lionel Messi.

'You realise how on top Spain are if even Lionel Messi is reverting to that.'

Richards added: 'We don't want to see people getting sent off in a World Cup final for that.'

Rooney was similarly furious with Messi's behaviour as he said: 'It is desperation.

'Argentina play like that, we know that's what they do.

'But the one thing you want is good sportsmanship and that was sad to see Lionel Messi doing that.'

After lifting the trophy in front of a full house of their adoring fans, La Roja opted not to ring in their victory with a night of partying in the city that never sleeps.

Instead, Golden Ball winner Rodri got the party started in transit, leading a round of singing on the team bus as the jubilant players sped back to their hotel for a team meal, before moving on to Newark Airport.

Back at the hotel, noted wine connoisseur Marcos Llorente enjoyed a bottle of Chateau Rayas Chateauneuf-du-Pape Reserve 2014 - which costs £1,009 to uncork - in his room with team-mates Ferran Torres and Marc Pubil.

The stars then boarded the Airbus A350-941 waiting for them - clad in their team's livery - and took off shortly after 2am local time.

Spain's players landed at Madrid's Barajas Airport at 2.30pm local time, and stepped out onto the tarmac with the World Cup trophy held aloft.

Sports.title: West Ham agree £68m fee to sell Crysencio Summerville to Al-Hilal, Fulham prepare £24m bid for Shea Charles and Ipswich have £10m bid for Daizen Maeda accepted by Celtic: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
West Ham agree £60m fee to sell Crysencio Summerville to Al-Hilal, Fulham prepare £24m bid for Shea Charles and Ipswich have £10m bid for Daizen Maeda accepted by Celtic: WINDOW WATCH

For all of yesterday's developments - including the latest on Chelsea's move for Crystal Palace defender Maxence Lacroix - click HERE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Welcome (back) to Hull! Zambrano's a Tiger again

Hull City have confirmed the signing of Ecuadorian midfielder Oscar Zambrano from Maribor for an undisclosed fee.

The 22-year-old was on loan at Hull in 2024-25. He has signed a four-year contract, with the club holding an option to extend by a further 12 months.

Fulham set to bid £24m for Saint Shea

Fulham are preparing a £24million offer for Southampton midfielder Shea Charles.

Leeds United have so far fallen short of Southampton's demands for the Northern Ireland international with the Championship side holding out for £25million plus add-ons.

Leeds have made three proposals with add-ons but with agreement still to be found, Fulham are ready to make their move.

Manager Alvaro Arbeloa is on board with bringing in the 22-year-old who started out at Manchester City and talks are expected to advance.

Charles scored the winning goal against Middlesbrough which looked to have secured their place in the play-off final against Hull City only for Spygate to end their season abruptly.

He was left out of their squad to face Eastleigh in a friendly at the weekend however as he had been afforded more time off after being involved in international friendlies for Northern Ireland.

Shea Charles' goal against Boro looked to have sent Saints to Wembley before they were expelled for the Spygate scandal

Sutton send for City's Spike

Manchester City goalkeeper Spike Brits has joined National League side Sutton United on a season-long loan.

The 19-year-old, an England U18 international, has been at City since 2023 when they brought him in from AFC Wimbledon's academy.

Hull could throw a line for Fisher

Hull are keen on Norwich City right-back Kellen Fisher, 22, but have yet to make a formal bid.

Norwich remain determined to hold onto their first-choice right back this summer despite interest from Premier League sides.

Kellen Fisher competes with Fulham's Willian back in 2023

Forest set to offer £32m for Sporting's Diomande

Nottingham Forest are advancing in their talks for Sporting Lisbon defender Ousmane Diomande.

The centre back was a target for Oliver Glasner at Crystal Palace and the Ivory Coast international is open to moving to the Premier League.

Sources in Portugal say Sporting are pushing for £42million for the centre-back amid interest from AC Milan, Newcastle United, Crystal Palace and Leeds United. Forest are understood to be offering £32m. However, it is understood the other Premier League sides are yet to step up their interest.

Forest are light in central defence with Murillo returning from injury and interest building in Jair Cunha. They have signed Xaver Schlager and are ready to offer over £45m for Tottenham's Lucas Bergvall.

£60m deal agreed for Summerville

Al-Hilal have agreed a £60million deal with West Ham for winger Crysencio Summerville.

The offer outstrips the £39m plus add-ons tabled by Roma and the Netherlands international has been offered a long term contract pending his medical.

Final details are being discussed for the 24-year-old but Premier League and European clubs are unlikely to compete with the Saudi offer.

For more on this story click HERE

Crysencio Summerville has been a target for several clubs this summer

Ipswich's £10m Daizen bid does trick

Ipswich Town have had a £10m bid for Celtic’s Daizen Maeda accepted. A deal worth £8m up front and £2m in add-ons has been agreed in principle.

Earlier this month the forward confirmed his wish to move to England .

‘Since I went to Celtic, I became interested in the Premier League,’ he told Japanese YouTube show Pivot. ‘I started watching a lot of Premier League games. I have a strong desire to play in the Premier League.'

The Tractor Boys have also completed their deal for Leicester winger Abdul Fatawu today, with manager Gary O'Neil saying of the 22-year-old: 'Abdul is a young player who has already gained good experience in the game and we’re excited to have him with us.

'He has strong physical and technical attributes, is comfortable on the ball and can test the opposition in one-on-one situations, so will provide us with good options within the squad.

'Having represented his country at the World Cup this summer, I know he is now looking forward to getting to work ahead of the Premier League season.'

Daizen Maeda played a big role for Japan at the World Cup this summer

Villa likely to seal deal for Garnacho

Aston Villa are expected to land Chelsea winger Alejandro Garnacho.

After enquiries during conversations over Morgan Rogers’ £117m sale, Villa have proposed a loan for the Argentine with obligation to buy if certain conditions are met.

Chelsea have been holding out for a permanent sale around £40m as Manchester United are also due a sell in percentage.

Aston Villa have stepped up their interest in Chelsea winger Alejandro Garnacho

Roma have also offered a loan with options for Garnacho who was of interest to Villa before he left Manchester United last summer.

Villa remain keen to sign Nicolas Jackson from Chelsea and are monitoring developments with Crysencio Summerville at West Ham.

The Hammers have a £39m offer plus add ons on the table from Roma and have added interest from Al Hilal.

PFA free agent squad in action tonight

Former Crystal Palace midfielder Jonny Williams and Egypt international Samy Morsy are in the PFA free agent squad of 21 to face Hednesford Town at Key's Park Stadium at 7.45 pm tonight.

Former Crystal Palace midfielder Jonny Williams and Egypt international Samy Morsy are in the PFA free agent squad of 21 to face Hednesford Town at Key's Park Stadium at 7.45 pm tonight.

Around 48 players have now joined the PFA pre-season camp where they train and play a series of friendlies to showcase their availability to clubs over the summer.

Former Manchester United and Port Vale keeper Ben Amos and ex-Ipswich Town striker Connor Wickham are among a growing band of players looking to earn contracts elsewhere.

Another friendly is planned at Tranmere Rovers on Friday.

The games can be viewed on the PFA's live YouTube stream.

Spurs agree to sell Lankshear to Middlesbrough

Tottenham have agreed to sell Will Lankshear to Middlesbrough for £14million potentially rising to £20m with add-ons.

There is also a 20 per cent sell on clause and Spurs have matching rights on any bids from other clubs in the future.

Striker Lankshear, 21, who was on loan at Oxford United last season, is expected for a medical later today.

Nicolas Jackson interested in Aston Villa move

Chelsea striker Nicolas Jackson is interested in his potential switch to Aston Villa to work with his former head coach Unai Emery again.

Chelsea striker Nicolas Jackson is interested in his potential switch to Aston Villa

Jackson's name came up during conversations between Chelsea and Villa centred on Morgan Rogers, who is set to move to Stamford Bridge for a club-record £117million and sign a six-year deal with the option of an extra year.

Villa have long been admirers of Jackson under Emery, who had the striker at Villarreal. Chelsea have been taking their time to decide on the 25-year-old Senegal international's future.

With Jackson, Liam Delap, Emmanuel Emegha, Marc Guiu and Joao Pedro as Xabi Alonso's striker options currently, there is an acceptance inside of Chelsea that they need to reduce their numbers, especially while facing a season out of Europe.

Joao Pedro is considered untouchable and so not for sale. Delap is keen to have another season to prove himself after a disappointing campaign following his move from Ipswich, while Emegha has only just arrived this summer from their sister side Strasbourg. Guiu is expected to leave either permanently or on loan.

There remains a market for Jackson, who spent the last season on loan at Bayern Munich. Chelsea are believed to value him at £65m.

That is down on the £80m they were understood to be seeking last summer before sanctioning his temporary switch to Bayern. That came at a time when the relationship between Jackson and then-manager Enzo Maresca had broken down.

Chelsea's plan for Jackson was to have him return in pre-season so that Xabi Alonso could take a closer look at the scorer. Alonso said at his unveiling last week that Jackson was due to join them on their tour of Australia and Asia after his post-World Cup break.

However, sources close to Jackson have told Daily Mail Sport that they are seriously considering Villa as an option after his name was discussed during talks about Rogers. Alejandro Garnacho has also been linked with Villa, but the Argentinian is said to be prioritising a move to Italy.

KIERAN GILL

West Ham mulling over Roma's Summerville bid

Roma are awaiting a reply from West Ham on their latest efforts to sign winger Crysencio Summerville.

As reported yesterday, Roma's latest bid of £39million plus add ons is a marginal increase and restructure on their second bid which was rejected.

Aston Villa have also been monitoring developments on the 24-year-old.

Roma are awaiting a reply from West Ham on their latest efforts to sign Crysencio Summerville

West Ham have enquired about Cardiff defender Dylan Lawlor.

Ipswich seal deal for new goalkeeper

Ipswich have completed the signing of goalkeeper Kayne van Oevelen from Volendam.

The fee is £4.25m with an initial £3.4m followed by £850,000 in add-ons.

The 22-year-old, who is seen as one for the future, has signed until 2031.

Ipswich have had a bid rejected for another goalkeeper, Kjell Scherpen from Union Saint-Gilloise.

As reported on Window Watch yesterday, Ipswich are close to sealing a £20m deal for Leicester City winger Abdul Fatawu with a further £3m in add-ons.

Ipswich are overhauling their goalkeeping department and discussing an £8.5m deal for Fulham's Issa Diop (right)

They are discussing an £8.5m deal for Fulham's Issa Diop and are negotiating with Celtic for versatile forward Daizen Maeda and free agent midfielder Hidemasa Morita who is leaving Sporting Lisbon and had been close to joining Leeds United.

QPR snap up Lamptey

Former Chelsea and Brighton full-back Tariq Lamptey has joined QPR on a permanent deal.

The 25-year-old has signed on a free transfer after leaving Serie A side Fiorentina.

Lamptey said: 'I like to get up and down, a lot of energy, a lot of fun. Hopefully I'll keep the fans on the edge of their seats.

Former Chelsea and Brighton full-back Tariq Lamptey has joined QPR on a permanent deal

'I'm tough tackling, I love one-v-ones, defensive and attacking, I just love playing the game.'

Lamptey's Fiorentina contract was terminated by mutual consent in May after the full-back ruptured his cruciate just three weeks after joining the Italian side from Brighton.

Fiorentina paid £6m for the Ghanaian.

Sheffield United weigh up Matondo move

Sheffield United are continuing to evaluate winger Rabbi Matondo who has impressed during their training camp in Valencia.

The Wales international, who is free to leave SK Brann, is due to play in a behind closed doors friendly against Huddersfield Town today.

Matondo figured in the Blades friendly against Levante last week and Chris Wilder is expected to make a decision this week with the likes of Derby County and Middlesbrough also showing interest.

Sheffield United are weighing up a move for Wales international Rabbi Matondo

Sheffield Wednesday close in on TENTH summer signing

Aston Villa forward Tommi O'Reilly is poised to become Sheffield Wednesday's 10th summer signing.

The 22-year-old, who impressed on loan at Crewe in League Two last season, is due to sign on loan again at Wednesday.

The Owls' young goalkeeper Logan Stretch, 19, has been loaned out to National League North side Buxton, who are managed by former Wednesday youth coach Jordan Broadbent.

Man City teenager joins Northampton

Manchester City striker Matty Warhurst has joined Northampton Town.

The prolific 19-year-old was keen to leave for first team football and had interest from a host of clubs in League One and League Two including Stockport County, Cambridge United, Leyton Orient and Swindon Town.

Warhurst, who turns 20 in September, has scored 61 goals in 97 games for various City sides in the last few seasons, including 36 goals in 41 games for the under-18s before adding 13 goals in 18 Premier League 2 appearances and eight goals in 11 FA Youth Cup games.

Alex Scott turns down new Bournemouth deal

Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott has turned down a new contract.

Scott has two years remaining on his current deal and was offered fresh terms by the Cherries in March this year.

Arsenal, Chelsea and Manchester United all hold an interest in the 22-year-old, but Bournemouth's stance is that he is not for sale this summer - regardless of his contract situation.

Daily Mail Sport understands Bournemouth have not put a price or valuation on the Under-21 European Championship winner as they do not consider him for sale.

Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott has turned down a new contract at the club

Just last week, new Cherries boss Marco Rose told the media he was confident that in-demand Scott and Junior Kroupi would remain on the South Coast for their Europa League campaign.

Bournemouth's policy this summer is to keep hold of their best players for Europe - including Scott, Kroupi and winger Rayan - but it remains to be seen if substantial offers would test their resolve.

Scott played 39 times for Bournemouth last season and was key to securing European football for the first time in the club's history.

Thomas Tuchel awarded Scott his first international call-up last November, although he did not earn a cap.

The midfielder also travelled to the United States with the Three Lions before the World Cup to take part in their tournament preparation camp.

Even if Bournemouth could be persuaded to do business over Scott, it's understood that United would have to sell players to afford the £80m it would be likely to cost to prise him away from the Vitality Stadium.

The club want to sell top-earner Marcus Rashford following his loan spells at Barcelona and Aston Villa, and would listen to offers for Joshua Zirkzee. Manuel Ugarte would also have been available, but the Uruguay midfielder sustained a serious knee injury at the World Cup and will spend much of next season recuperating at Carrington.

As it stands, United will struggle to sign Scott and Roma midfielder Manu Kone appears to be a more realistic option after United held talks with the Frenchman's camp.

Sports.title: Spain dominate the defence, there's a surprise name in goal... but Harry Kane is edged out: Stats boffins reveal their World Cup team of the tournament
Sports.content:
Spain dominate the defence, there's a surprise name in goal... but Harry Kane is edged out: Stats boffins reveal their World Cup team of the tournament

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Spain’s dramatic victory over Argentina in the World Cup final completed what has been a tumultuous yet exhilarating tournament, providing us with a number of incredible moments and sublime performances.

As the dust settles, it's time to look back and discuss the truly elite performers from the tournament from each position and the moments that defined their campaigns.

From members of the victorious Spanish side to star performers from the tournament’s dark horses, Daily Mail Sport looks at SofaScore’s 2026 World Cup Team of the Tournament...

GK: Gregor Kobel (Switzerland) – 7.52

While the Swiss No 1’s inclusion may be a surprise to some football fans, it could not be more deserved. The Borussia Dortmund keeper gloriously maintained the stellar reputation of Swiss goalkeepers in modern football.

Stepping into the very large shoes - or gloves - of the legendary Yann Sommer he turned in a series of standout performances.

The earliest of those came against Canada, in which he prevented a chance with a staggering 0.99 XG. He followed it against Colombia in the last 16, when he was the shootout hero by saving the crucial fourth penalty during the shootout, sending his country through to the World Cup quarter-finals for the first time since 1954.

Moreover, Kobel continued to prove his ability to perform as the ideal modern goalkeeper. Throughout the tournament the Dortmund man maintained a 75 per cent pass completion rate, even achieving an 83 percent and above pass completion rate in the opening three group games.

Gregor Kobel was Switzerland's shootout hero against Colombia in their last-16 clash

LB: Marc Cucurella (Spain) – 7.09

The first member of the 2026 world champions in SofaScore’s team is unsurprisingly Real Madrid’s latest acquisition. A man who often divides opinion and earns a large amount of criticism off the pitch has been superb on it throughout the tournament.

Cucurella maintained an admirable level of consistency, completing 398 out of 431 passes across his eight appearances whilst also achieving 25 ball recoveries and nine clearances.

His attacking contributions were not minimal either as he was a constant threat to opposing defences down in De La Fuente’s 4-2-3-1 system and contributed two assists in Spain’s 3-0 victory over Austria, the Spaniard once again silencing his critics on the world stage.

CB: Aymeric Laporte (Spain) – 7.40

As is expected the vast majority of the back four from this elite XI are Spanish as the champions only conceded one goal in the tournament. One central pillar of their back four was Athletic Bilbao’s warhorse, Aymeric Laporte.

Now entering the latter stages of his career at 32 there were doubts over Laporte’s quality but De La Fuente was vindicated in his decision to start the former Manchester City man in every game of their campaign.

The former Premier League winner impressed both on the eye and on the stat sheet as Laporte achieved; a 93.47 per cent pass completion rate, 15 interceptions as well as a staggering 29 clearances on his way to World Cup glory.

CB: Pau Cubarsi (Spain) – 7.56

Next up is Laporte’s right-sided partner Pau Cubarsi. The Barcelona man became only the ninth player to have won the World Cup before their 20th birthday and joins Kylian Mbappe in a two-man club of players who have won the Young Player of the Tournament award alongside a winner’s medal as a teenager.

Cubarsi’s composure and quality on the ball - combined with his capacity for brutish and brave defensive contributions when required - reminded fans of the Spanish centre halves that anchored Spain’s 2010 World Cup winning team.

While starting every game for his nation at the tournament this incredible young talent was able to maintain a 96.13 per cent pass completion rate, even besting his centre back partner 13 years his senior. he also achieved five interceptions, 32 clearances and two blocked shots, making the decision to award YPOTT to the Spaniard a no-brainer.

Pedro Porro (left) and Pau Cubarsi track Kylian Mbappe in Spain's semi-final win over France

RB: Pedro Porro (Spain) – 7.54

Completing the back four is Cucurella’s full-back partner in De La Fuente’s winning system, Pedro Porro. Despite being part of a Spurs team that finished one place above the Premier League drop zone, the right back was crucial to Spain’s success.

Whilst Porro is the only member of the Spanish ensemble included in this XI to have not started every game of the World Cup, his impact was key.

Perhaps the most memorable moment of the grudge match we saw Spain compete in against France belonged to Porro. He netted the second goal in their victory and the 2-0 only goal from open play, whilst also helping Spain to a clean sheet against the joint most prolific side at the tournament.

His performances reflected a keen desire and ability to contribute going forward with the two excellent goals scored against France and Austria but he was no defensive slouch either, with the full back racking up eight interceptions, 14 clearances and 30 ball recoveries across the tournament.

CDM: Rodri (Spain) - 7.76

No prizes for guessing who anchors this star-studded midfield three, as it could not have been anyone else but Rodri.

Over the last four weeks the 2024 Ballon D’or winner has only further solidified his reputation as one of the all-time greats.

The fact that a player who did not register a single goal and just 1 assist can unanimously be the POTT speaks so highly to Rodri’s brilliance in his position, combining traditional Spanish elegance with defensive discipline.

The Manchester City midfielder was at the heart of everything the Spanish did at either end of the pitch, with 11 key passes, 26 tackles and 11 clearances over 726 minutes on the field.

CAM: Jude Bellingham (England) 7.81

Entering the more attacking section of the midfield, one obvious inclusion is our very own Madrista. During this tournament it is fair to say that Jude Bellingham provided the greatest World Cup campaign we have seen from an England player in 60 years.

England’s No10 was world class from the word go, scoring in two of England’s group games and marshalling the midfield with incredible maturity.

It was clear he should make waves in the knockouts, but even the most ambitious England fans would not have anticipated a brace in both the round of 16 clash against Mexico and the quarter-final against Norway. Bellingham's performances at the Azteca and Hard Rock Stadiums will be spoken about for years to come as the Birmingham-born midfielder wrote himself into English football folklore.

Yes, England fell short in the end but Bellingham’s displays were almost flawless. Seven goals, one assist, 14 tackles and three big chances created are amongst just some of the stats that demonstrate the England man’s heroic performances.

Jude Bellingham scores his seventh of the tournament in the crazy 6-4 win over France

CAM: Ousmane Dembele (France) 7.91

The first member of France’s team to make this XI is of course the Ballon D’or holder and back-to-back Champions League final scorer and winner. With the form Dembele took into this tournament it was inevitable that he would further demonstrate his quality.

Even in a team with so many superstars and egos Dembele stood out amongst the best. Six goals - including a marvellous hat-trick against Norway - placed the PSG forward at joint fifth place in the scoring charts and his link-up play with Michael Olise and Kylian Mbappe provided some exhilarating moments during France’s journey and resulted in two assists for Dembele.

Despite France leaving the tournament with something of a whimper in their semi-final defeat by Spain, Dembele displayed his quality on the major international stage for the first real time and was one third of the joint most potent attacking force at the tournament. Dembele and Co’s stellar performances have given us a taste of what is still to come for this young, free-flowing French squad.

RW: Lionel Messi (Argentina) 8.79

What is there left to say about this man? A genius. The greatest of all time confirmed what we already knew and then some at this tournament.

With many critics saying that the 39-year-old was a spent force coming into the tournament the little man proved them all wrong - and achieved the highest average SofaScore rating of any player at this year’s tournament. Messi achieved his highest ever output at a World Cup, scoring an astounding eight goals and registering four assists.

The little magician provided us with some of the greatest moments in World Cup history: a hat-trick in the opening match, a goal and assist to save his nation from the brink of elimination against Egypt and, of course, two goals in seven minutes to send England packing in the semi-final.

He may have fallen short at the final hurdle this time, however his legacy on the world stage is unquestionable. We seldom see a footballer perform at such a high level so late in his career, but then again Lionel Messi is no normal footballer.

Lionel Messi scored eight goals but couldn't quite secure back-to-back World Cup triumphs

ST: Erling Haaland (Norway) 7.90

As debut World Cup campaigns go this is not bad from the Norwegian phenomenon. Norway had a tough group but the Premier League Golden Boot winner led his team into battle with a Viking-like ferocity that saw him bag seven goals - including three braces - and also allowing his team-mates to flourish with his hold-up play and supreme positional nous.

Amongst many strong performances, the one that really stood out from Haaland was in Norway’s round of 16 clash with Brazil. With this being only Norway’s third appearance at this stage and facing the five-time winners many felt they were second favourites. However, two excellent finishes from this man late on sent the Selecao packing.

Despite losing out to England in the end, Haaland propelled his nation to their first ever World Cup quarter final and did it in some style. It may have been his first time on the world's biggest stage but it will not be his last.

Erling Haaland will go back to Manchester City having shone at his debut World Cup

LW: Kylian Mbappe (France) 8.24

It seemed impossible for the Frenchman to eclipse his achievements in Qatar, where he scored eight goals including a hat-trick in the final. But while he may have only got as far as the semis this time around, 10 goals to make him the competition's all-time goal scorer with a mind-boggling 22 is magnificent.

Deschamps was able to engineer a dynamic attack around Mbappe maximising his qualities. Using Olise and Dembele, the French attack seemed as if all of them played in every position along the front line, unlocking Mbappe’s pace, finishing and capacity for link up play.

Mbappe failed to truly affect the game in a significant way against Spain, however his performances in any other game were mesmerising, only falling short to Messi for highest average SofaScore rating it was another Mbappe masterclass at the World Cup.

Sports.title: Frustrated Man United fans urge club to relax measures against supporters who face losing season tickets amid 'ban first and ask questions later' approach to touting row
Sports.content:
Frustrated Man United fans urge club to relax measures against supporters who face losing season tickets amid 'ban first and ask questions later' approach to touting row

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Manchester United supporters have urged the club to pause a clampdown on ticket touts that they claim is targeting innocent fans.

Since United launched the operation last week, thousands of fans have received emails warning that their accounts have been restricted and their season tickets could be revoked.

On Tuesday night, a number of fan groups – including The ’58, Manchester United Supporters’ Trust and The Red Army – joined forces to issue a statement calling on the club to stop its ‘ban first and ask questions later’ approach.

While the groups insist they support United’s campaign against the touts, there is a concern that genuine fans are being caught in the net. They have backed a letter sent to United by the Fans’ Forum last week calling for the crackdown to be suspended.

The statement read: ‘Professional touting, automated purchasing and those who exploit supporters for financial gain have no place at Manchester United and deserve robust action.

‘However, that action must be fair, proportionate and transparent. Long-standing supporters who have followed Manchester United for decades, often across multiple generations of the same family, should never feel they are being treated as suspects without clear evidence, due process or a meaningful opportunity to respond to the allegations made against them.

Manchester United fan group The 1958 have previously organised protests against the club's ownership under Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazers

‘The current approach has created a growing perception among supporters of a “ban first and ask questions later” process. That is not how trust is built, nor is it consistent with the standards of fairness that loyal supporters should expect from their football club.

‘Investigations should establish the facts before sanctions are imposed, particularly where the potential consequence is the loss of a season ticket.

The Fans’ Forum has rightly called on the club to pause the issuing of further suspensions and to halt any cancellation of season tickets while meaningful discussions take place. We fully support that request.

‘The club and its supporters share the same objective: ensuring tickets are used fairly by genuine Manchester United supporters while protecting the integrity of the ticketing system.

That objective will only be achieved through trust, transparency, proportionate enforcement,

better-designed systems and meaningful engagement with supporters, not by creating an environment where loyal fans fear losing relationships with the club that have been built over decades.

‘This is also a significant moment for supporter representation. For the first time, supporter organisations from across the fanbase have come together to support a common position.

‘While each group has its own perspective and priorities, we are united by our commitment to protecting Manchester United, its supporters and the unique supporter culture that has been built over generations.’

United’s ticketing policy allows for fans to forward their season tickets to approved friends or family members. However, many supporters received emails last week informing them of suspicious activity on their account and asking them to identify every device used to access it. Another round of emails followed on Monday night, and there are fears that more will follow.

United fans now fear losing their season tickets over claims they breached the rules

The restrictions on buying and transferring tickets have been lifted on some accounts, with the club admitting that innocent fans may have been affected and apologising for the inconvenience.

However, other fans have been left in the dark and in fear of losing their season tickets, which they have already paid for. It’s unclear if they would be refunded if found to have breached the rules.

United are said be aware of the backlash but will not share any data until the process is complete as they continue to target touts who threaten the integrity of the club’s ticketing operation.

Insiders point out that supporters are merely being sent a request for information, and no sanctions are being imposed until they have replied or 14 days have elapsed without a response.

While they acknowledged the concern and distress caused to anyone receiving the emails, they say the messages are only sent if there is a technical anomaly on the account consistent with touting, and no sanctions will be issued if there is a straightforward explanation. Even then, sanctions are imposed at the end of the process and not with the initial emails.

The club have also pushed back on suggestions that the crackdown is designed to reduce the number of season-ticket holders or increase revenue, with sources saying that any tickets cancelled after the appeals process will be re-issued as a season ticket to someone on the waiting list.

Sports.title: Chelsea consider shock move for England centre back John Stones, 32, after his Man City exit
Sports.content:
Chelsea are considering a move for John Stones after his release by Manchester City following the expiry of his contract.

The 32-year-old central defender is available on a free this summer, and is now enjoying downtime after representing England at the World Cup, including starting in their semi-final exit to Argentina.

Chelsea’s interest comes a month after club sources tried to kill off rumours circulating within football circles that they were looking at Stones. However, he is now a legitimate candidate, it can be confirmed.

Chelsea have benefited from having experienced heads in defence before, such as Thiago Silva. However, Arsenal have also been linked with Stones, who is reportedly seen as a possible short-term option if William Saliba’s injury proves serious.

Chelsea have been in talks for Maxence Lacroix, with negotiations even held at ownership level in a meeting between Behdad Eghbali and Steve Parish at a hotel in New York.

John Stones played in five of England's World Cup matches, including the agonising semi-final exit to Argentina

Palace want around £60million for the 26-year-old who was with France at the World Cup. Como’s Jacobo Ramon, 21, is also a candidate who has featured on Chelsea’s shortlist for some time.

While chasing at least one central-defender signing, Chelsea have long maintained that their highly-rated academy graduate Josh Acheampong is not for sale despite multiple approaches.

However, the 20-year-old would be forgiven for wondering whether he will receive meaningful minutes in the upcoming season, with Chelsea having fallen out of European football. Sources close to Acheampong believe he is ready to play.

Chelsea are scheduled to fly to Sydney, Australia at the end of this week to begin their pre-season tour under Xabi Alonso. The club have not yet confirmed their travelling squad.

Chelsea are still waiting for several of their World Cup representatives to return with players entitled to three-week breaks. Some with loan options, particularly among the youngsters from Cobham, could also be left at home to focus on finalising that opportunity.

Sports.title: Inside Michael Carrick's Man United revolution: How Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos take team to next level, latest on search for another midfield star, the Lisandro Martinez issue and academy talents pushing for first-team spot
Sports.content:
Inside Michael Carrick's Man United revolution: How Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos take team to next level, latest on search for another midfield star, the Lisandro Martinez issue and academy talents pushing for first-team spot

Unlock more from our team inside the Man United camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

As Manchester United’s players and staff left Helsinki’s Olympic Stadium on Saturday, there was disappointment at a 1-0 defeat by Wrexham – but also excitement at what a full season under Michael Carrick will look like.

The pre-season opener was the moment to dust off the cobwebs. United are not at full tilt with some key pieces of the Carrick puzzle still on their post-World Cup holidays, and many of the club’s best young academy players are continuing to jockey for a spot in the squad when the season commences.

New midfielder Andrey Santos is already said to be impressing team-mates with his intensity in training, while goalkeeper Karl Darlow, nursing a small injury after a procedure at the back end of last season, and Youri Tielemans, on a post-World Cup break, are still to come in and make their mark.

But United’s transfer business is far from done. Carrick and his staff are still keen on a third midfielder, want to ease the load on Benjamin Sesko up top, and are targeting a left-sided addition (it is still to be decided if that is a left winger or left back).

The manager's revolution is still gathering momentum. Here Daily Mail Sport looks at the state of play ahead of this week’s second pre-season friendly against Norwegian side Rosenborg in Trondheim on Friday.

Manager Michael Carrick knows there is still plenty to be done at Manchester United ahead of the new season

WHAT’S THE LATEST WITH DEFENDERS?

United need to assess the extent of the injury suffered by Lisandro Martinez in the World Cup final before deciding if a new centre back needs boosting up the shopping list.

Matthijs de Ligt is set to miss the start of the season while he recovers from back surgery, leaving Harry Maguire, Ayden Heaven and Leny Yoro as the only senior centre back options.

United feel well stocked at right back with Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui, both of whom can play on the left too, but Carrick is keen to have a reliable ball-playing centre back in his line-up to help break the lines, something Martinez excels at.

The two have a very close relationship and the extent of Martinez’s injury issue is likely to put significant weight on whether a new central defender – United were keen on Murillo before he signed a new deal with Nottingham Forest – is back on the agenda.

Left back is a position higher up the priority list, largely because Luke Shaw starting every game last season has to be seen as an anomaly, as positive as it was.

Left back Harry Amass is determined to leave a lasting impression during pre-season and was among the stand-outs for United in Helsinki. But there is significant Championship interest in him and the feeling is that a late move will be sanctioned, particularly if Patrick Dorgu’s role is re-allocated from wing back to full back.

A nugget of information from academy circles: there is A-League interest from Australia in rising star full-back James Overy, while Rangers are also monitoring him. One to watch.

Left back Harry Amass in action for United against Wrexham on Saturday. The 19-year-old is determined to impress during pre-season

United need to ascertain the extent of the injury sustained by Lisandro Martinez during the World Cup final

WHAT NEXT FOR THE MIDFIELD REBUILD?

This is the defining area of the pitch for United to get right and has been the focus of months and months of meetings by Ineos and the decision-makers at Old Trafford.

Carrick wants United to play with greater control next season so they can dominate matches and not rely on playing in transition, which they did effectively for so much of his time in charge last term.

Casemiro and Kobbie Mainoo worked well as a partnership but the emphasis at United this summer has been to find a combination of midfielders who can disrupt their opponents while also being able to dictate from a deeper base.

United’s top target was Elliot Anderson before that move became too much of a stretch financially and he went to Manchester City for £116million. Similarly Mateus Fernandes, whom many inside United were convinced would join, went to Tottenham Hotspur for £85m.

Those missed targets ultimately led them back to a player who they wanted when Alejandro Garnacho went to Chelsea, and another that figures inside United believe could be the pound-for-pound signing of the season.

Santos was requested by United as part of the Garnacho deal, only for Chelsea to shoot that down. But now they have their man. And the Brazil international is viewed as someone who has the natural instincts to play as a No 6, a more defensive screening midfielder, in front of the defence. He is expected to provide the midfield protection that was severely lacking in the final knockings of the Erik ten Hag era, and often a bone of contention during Ruben Amorim's reign.

Then there is Youri Tielemans. United activated his £35m release clause, a deal they desperately tried to keep under wraps as part of a concerted effort to do their business in the shadows and away from the media.

The Belgian is Premier League proven, a player United believe can dictate matches, and should ease the creative burden on Bruno Fernandes in front of him.

United hope that Youri Tielemans will bring the control to United's midfield that was lacking last season

United still want a third midfielder and they hold interest in Morocco star Ayyoub Bouaddi, among others

United still want a third midfielder and they hold interest in Bournemouth's Alex Scott, who declined to sign a new contract on Tuesday, Lille's Ayyoub Bouaddi, Roma's Manu Kone, Aurelien Tchouameni of Real Madrid and Fulham's Sander Berge - and this is the signing that stylistically should tell us a lot about Carrick’s United.

The expectation is that he will stick with the 4-2-3-1 system that served him so well last season, allowing Fernandes to flourish as the No 10, with two players, one more defensive than the other, at the base of midfield.

But a move for Scott, over say, Kone, would allow United to hold the tactical flexibility for a more ball-dominant 4-3-3 that Paris Saint-Germain, for example, have used to great effect.

United sources have been more tight-lipped than ever about Ineos' thinking, but what is abundantly clear is United won’t overpay for players, won’t pay enormous wages, and want to continue to pull rabbits out of the hat just when you think you’ve figured out their next move.

IS CARRICK SETTLED ON HIS GOALKEEPERS?

Yes. Senne Lammens is his No 1 and there are no question marks about the Belgian despite his costly error against Spain in their World Cup quarter-final.

Team-mates, including fellow goalkeeper Tom Heaton, have already reached out to Lammens and the sense inside the United camp is that the summer adversity can actually make him a better goalkeeper in the long run, to United’s benefit.

Landing a back-up goalkeeper early in the summer was seen as essential and the free agent move for Darlow frees up Altay Bayindir and Radek Vitek to depart.

Depending on who you speak to at United, some sources believe a realistic fee for Vitek comes in at around £15m, with the Czech shot-stopper open to leaving permanently, which appears, as of now, to be United’s preferred route.

‘I'm ready to go somewhere again and hopefully be No 1,’ Vitek told a few of us after the Helsinki match. ‘There has been a few (clubs) on the table. We're hoping to choose the best one and hopefully it will happen soon.’

‘I'm ready to go somewhere again and hopefully be No 1,’ United's Radek Vitek said after the Wrexham match

There is a sense inside the United camp that his World Cup adversity can actually make Senne Lammens a better goalkeeper in the long run

The move to keep Heaton around was seen as imperative by all because of his experience and his leadership in the dressing room; a key conduit between the players and staff.

The goalkeepers are set: 1. Lammens. 2. Darlow. 3. Heaton.

ANY YOUNGSTERS WHO CAN CHIP IN?

Simply put, United have too many young players that have outgrown academy football but are also not ready to be thrust into the first team.

There are a lot of youngsters determined to find a role for themselves in the squad for next season, not least with United’s budget unable to stretch to refreshing every position, but also because Carrick and his staff have an immense amount of data on each of them.

Amass is particularly interesting at left back, while midfielder Jacob Devaney, who shone out on loan with St Mirren, is among those fighting to be the additional midfielder promoted from the academy for the coming season.

Tyler Fletcher has loan interest from Kilmarnock but wants to stay and fight for his place, while others such as Sekou Kone (Lausanne), Jack Moorhouse (countless options across League One, as well as abroad), and Jack Fletcher (lots of EFL loan interest) are expected to play elsewhere.

Chido Obi did not get on in Helsinki and there is a degree of uncertainty about the next best move for him. Some inside United are reluctant to send him out on loan but there is also an acknowledgement that he needs to be tested after spending the entirety of last season in the academy set-up.

Cristian Orozco, the physical defensive midfielder who has arrived from Fortaleza after turning 18, will start with the club’s Under 21s before being assessed for his suitability to be in and around the first team. David Eze and Karim Cassim are two Man City youth players United are focused on acquiring this summer as part of their aggressive academy recruitment drive, too.

Tyler Fletcher has loan interest from Kilmarnock but wants to stay and fight for his place

Midfielder Jacob Devaney is fighting to be the additional midfielder promoted to the first team from the academy for the coming season

HOW IS THE LEFT WING LOOKING?

The £8m signing of Tynan Thompson only added to the intrigue around what is happening on the left wing.

Thompson has joined from Tottenham Hotspur as an Emerging Talent Signing, similar to the 2025 deal for Heaven, which has since proved a steal. While Thompson will have to earn a shot at the first team, a key part of the vision sold to the player was that the pathway is right in front of him, as evidenced by Heaven.

Speaking to one key figure in the England player pathway, Daily Mail Sport was told that Thompson is a ‘United-type winger from the 90s’ who will bring a strong one-versus-one ability which has been missing off the left across United’s academy sides.

Adding to the left wing conundrum is the fact Marcus Rashford and his £325,000-a-week contract remains on the books after Barcelona passed up on the chance to sign him, while Dorgu has been viewed as a winger, rather than a left back option, under Carrick.

Noah Ajayi, a 17-year-old who is one of the academy’s brightest players and was in line to play a part in pre-season until an ankle injury put paid to that, needs to see a pathway is there for him, too, amid interest from top clubs in Germany, Italy and Portugal.

Interest in West Ham’s Crysencio Summerville, who is now bound for Saudi Arabia, was dependent on any potential exit for Rashford, while the role of Dorgu further complicates recruitment. Should Rashford, who doesn’t have an allocated squad number at United right now, be fully reintroduced, he will expect to be a major factor out on the left.

The £8million signing of Tynan Thompson from Spurs only adds to the intrigue around what will happen on the left wing for United

All of which is tied up in the future of £325,000-a-week Marcus Rashford, whom Barcelona have declined to sign

IS ANOTHER CENTRE FORWARD AN OPTION?

Sesko’s shin injury is a lingering problem for United and there is a real lack of depth up top. Matheus Cunha is capable in that position, as is Bryan Mbeumo, and Carrick does like the false-nine approach, particularly in games where United are not expecting to dominate the ball.

United are open to moving on Joshua Zirkzee but he is one of the most popular members of the dressing room and is eager to fight for his place with more games available now United are back in Europe.

Sports.title: Josh Kerr says Glasgow 2026 will be 'much more of a fun time' after world record
Sports.content:
Josh Kerr says Glasgow 2026 will be 'much more of a fun time' after world record

Josh Kerr, who is from Edinburgh, had a 'Commonwealth Games hopeful' T-shirt as a teenager. He told of his early career before he races for Scotland at Glasgow 2026.

View 2 Images BIRMINGHAM, ENGLAND - AUGUST 04: Josh Kerr of Team Scotland reacts after competing in the Men's 1500m Round 1 heats on day seven of the Birmingham 2022 Commonwealth Games at Alexander Stadium on August 04, 2022 in Birmingham, England. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

World record holder Josh Kerr was given a "Commonwealth Games hopeful" T-shirt as a teenager.

‌



He told the story of his early career as he returns to Scotland to compete in Glasgow 2026, the biggest UK sporting event of the summer.

‌



At just 13, Kerr tried different events at the main Games venue, including shot put and high jump.

‌



In July 2011, almost 15 years to the day that he will run the Commonwealth Mile, the record books show Kerr ran 4m 30.91 as a 13-year-old.

He also threw the shot 7m 34cm and did a 1m 55cm high jump.

Aldi worker swaps aisles for Scotland boxing team at Commonwealth Games READ MORE :

View 2 Images Oliver Hoare of Team Australia and Josh Kerr of Team Scotland compete during the Men's 1500m Round 1 heats on day seven of the Birmingham 2022

‌



The Glasgow 2026 gold medal contender cut his teeth racing at tracks around Scotland.

And he was no stranger to the Scotstoun Stadium where the Athletics and Para Athletics events will be held from Thursday.

Now that young “hopeful” is running 3mins 42.66 for the mile and is keen to win gold in Glasgow and put on a show for his home crowd.

‌



Kerr recalled: “I grew up in youth academies for future Commonwealth Games hopefuls, and that will never leave me.

"I still have the 'Scottish Commonwealth Games hopeful' T-shirt. It was a bit rough back then but there’s definitely a lot of memories held in it.

"So, to be able to go out there and represent my country in front of a home crowd at the Commonwealth Games, that's all I want for my career.”

‌



Athletics and Para Athletics events will take place over six days at Scotstoun Stadium from July 27 to August 1, with 59 gold medals up for grabs.

The Men’s and Women’s Mile finals are run on August 1 with a small number of tickets remaining in the heats, on 29 July and 30 July.

Kerr will spearhead a strong field in the “Commonwealth Mile” alongside fellow Scots Jake Wightman and Neil Gourley.

‌



He added: “Now it's time to race the best guys in the Commonwealth. So, I'm not too worried about times right now.

"I'm not battling machines and battling personalities, so it'll be a much more of a fun time.

"I think that would be one way of capping off a great couple of weeks.”

Article continues below

Fans are encouraged not to miss out and get their hands on their tickets, available at glasgow2026.com/tickets.

Sports.title: Rayan Cherki singles out Didier Deschamps after backlash to England incident and 'snub'
Sports.content:
Rayan Cherki singles out Didier Deschamps after backlash to England incident and 'snub'

Rayan Cherki was one of the France players taken off at half time in the 6-4 third-place play-off loss to England at the 2026 World Cup

View 2 Images Rayan Cherki was substituted at half time of the third-place play-off match vs England (Image: Jose Hernandez/Anadolu via Getty Images)

Manchester City attacker Rayan Cherki has sent a special message to outgoing France boss Didier Deschamps after what appeared to be a couple of frosty incidents between the pair. Deschamps has ended his 14-year reign in charge of the French team following this summer’s World Cup.

‌



Les Blues were one of the favourites to win the tournament, but a 2-0 loss against eventual winners Spain in the semi-final left them fighting for third place. That’s where they came up against England, who suffered semi-final heartbreak against Argentina.

‌



In what was arguably the game of the tournament, the Three Lions came out as 6-4 winners to claim third place. Thomas Tuchel’s men found themselves 4-0 up at half time, but France almost completed a second-half comeback before a Bukayo Saka penalty and a Jude Bellingham goal put England out of reach.

‌



Both teams have now returned home, with Cherki taking to social media to give his response to the tournament and single out Deschamps. “Naturally, I am saddened by the outcome of a tournament where our mission was to make you all proud and happy,” he wrote on Instagram.

Premier League referee Anthony Taylor retires from football and teases what's next READ MORE :

FIFA president Gianni Infantino told World Cup decision could have cost him his job READ MORE :

“Thank you for the support that stayed with us every day and served as our driving force. I am infinitely grateful to the coach for everything he has achieved for French football and for giving me my first caps for Les Bleus.

“His track record speaks for itself. Thank you to the coaching staff for their dedication, and to all the federation personnel who supported us and ensured we had the best possible conditions, all while looking after our loved ones.

‌



“Thank you to the whole squad for these unforgettable moments of brotherhood. Despite our differences, mistakes, or setbacks, we are one family; it is up to us to remain united so that French football comes back stronger!”

View 2 Images Rayan Cherki has sent a message to outgoing France manager Didier Deschamps (Image: Maddie Meyer - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

The message comes after Cherki appeared to ignore Deschamps, not once, but twice, during the tournament. The first incident came after the team’s round of 32 win over Sweden, where the forward appeared to initially snub the manager before giving him a brief greeting.

‌



The second came during the first half of the game against England. During the first hydration break, with England 2-0 up, an agitated Deschamps appears to try to give Cherki instructions, only for him to wave his hand towards the manager and walk away.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

With England scoring a further two goals before half time, Cherki was one of four France players to be replaced at the break. Speaking about the incident after the match, Deschamps said: “I’m not going to settle scores today.

‌



“The players know perfectly well. I’m not going to point fingers. However, I always tell them, and as Kylian (Mbappe) said, they needed time to process it but it was my mistake, I should have made different choices from the start of the match, you can say that, and perhaps things would have gone better.

“Everyone is judged on their performance. Obviously, some players could have done better. I wish them all the best.”

Cherki’s mention of the French Football Federation in his message is also noticeable, given reports in France around growing tensions between the federation and the team. Issues reportedly include World Cup bonuses, travel and match tickets for families for the World Cup just gone.

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury told exactly why mega-fight will not be jeopardised
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury told exactly why mega-fight will not be jeopardised

Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury will both take part in warm-up fights later this week, and one boxing legend has revealed why fans should not be worried ahead of their clash later this year

View Image Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua are set to finally face off (Image: Getty Images)

Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury are both expected to come away without a scratch in their warm-up fights, finally setting up a long-awaited showdown.

‌



That is according to boxing legend Teddy Atlas - who expects the heavyweight icons to 'wipe the floor' with their respective opponents. Joshua will make a sensational return to the ring on Saturday night - seven months on after being involved in a horrific car crash just days after knocking out Jake Paul.

‌



The former two-time heavyweight champion will take on unknown fighter Kristian Prenga over in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. But just over 24 hours before Joshua makes the walk to the ring, Fury is expected to have a tune-up fight of his own. The 'Gypsy King' will meet Mariusz Wach behind closed doors over in Thailand.

‌



Providing both men win, they will meet later this year. The pair finally agreed to a fight earlier this year, and are expected to settle their 10-year feud in November. While Prenga has vowed to scupper those plans, Atlas is expecting a relatively easy night at the office for both Fury and 'AJ' later this week.

FOLLOW OUR FIGHTING FB PAGE! Latest boxing and MMA news, analysis and much more via our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Anthony Joshua retirement date emerges just days before Tyson Fury warm-up fight READ MORE :

In an interview with CanadaCasino, he said: "I think the warm-up fights are pretty much foregone conclusions. I’m not knocking anyone who gets in the ring, but in a practical sense, they are foregone conclusions. Wach is 46 years old and has been knocked out five times. With Joshua and Prenga, I think it is all up to Joshua and how long the fight goes. But we don’t know where Joshua is emotionally coming off that near-fatal car accident. We don’t know how that has impacted him. We saw how a car accident may have impacted Errol Spence.

"With Joshua, I definitely tell you it has impacted him. I just don’t know how much and how. If he is in a halfway decent place, I think he goes behind the jab, catches Prenga and the fight is over, maybe in two rounds. If he is not, maybe he does not do anything for a few rounds and allows Prenga to survive. But at the end of the day, there should only be one guy left standing, and it should be Joshua."

Anthony Joshua sent brutal warning ahead of boxing comeback READ MORE :

Barry Hearn gives clear verdict on Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury fight collapsing READ MORE :

Fans are chomping at the bit to see both Joshua and Fury trade leather, but Atlas believes the fight has been made far too late, seeing as both men have lost multiple times over the last few years. "It’s definitely a money grab," he said. "Joshua is two fights on from being knocked out badly against Dubois, Fury has lost a couple of times to Usyk, and both of them have lost their most significant fights of recent times. There is no arguing that both of them have slippage in their performances and in their careers at this point in their lives. They are not spring chickens anymore. They have been in tough fights, and it shows.

Article continues below

"Ali and Frazier in Manila were too late. Their skills had been eroded, they had been diminished, but it became one of the great heavyweight fights because they were more available to each other than they would have been when their skills were sharper. The one thing that was not diminished was their character, their resolve, their determination and their championship qualities. So yes, Fury vs Joshua is late, and yes, it’s a money grab, but it still might give you some of that because they’re heavyweights.

Sports.title: Premier League referee Anthony Taylor retires from football and teases what's next
Sports.content:
Premier League referee Anthony Taylor retires from football and teases what's next

Anthony Taylor has retired from refereeing with his final match being at the recent FIFA World Cup

View 2 Images Premier League referee Anthony Taylor has announced his retirement after officiating at the 2026 World Cup (Image: Rico Brouwer/Soccrates/Getty Images)

Premier League referee Anthony Taylor has announced his retirement. The Englishman has hung up his whistle after officiating Spain's 1-0 win over Portugal in the last 16 of this summer's World Cup.

‌



The 47-year-old has called time on his career after over two decades and 831 matches. Taylor officiated in the Premier League for 16 seasons, taking charge of no fewer than 432 top-flight games.

‌



The experienced ref also officiated the 2024 Champions League final between Borussia Dortmund and Real Madrid at Wembley Stadium. But Taylor will no longer referee in the professional game - bowing out after the World Cup.

‌



Emi Martinez hints he could quit Argentina duty after World Cup final loss READ MORE :

FIFA president Gianni Infantino told World Cup decision could have cost him his job READ MORE :

The now former top-flight official announced the news in a post on his LinkedIn account on Tuesday. He said: “The final whistle has blown – moving on to the next chapter.

“After 16 unforgettable seasons officiating at the highest level of English and international football, I have decided that the time has come to retire from elite refereeing. Looking back, I do so with immense pride and gratitude. It has been the greatest privilege to officiate in the Premier League, across FIFA and UEFA competitions, and on some of football’s biggest occasions. Every match, every challenge and every experience has shaped not only my career but also the person I have become.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



“Elite refereeing is about far more than the ninety minutes on the pitch. It demands commitment, resilience, preparation and sacrifice, but it has given me memories, friendships and experiences that I will cherish for the rest of my life. No referee achieves success alone. I have been incredibly fortunate to work alongside so many outstanding colleagues throughout my career. To each of you, thank you. It has been an honour to share this journey together.

“A special thank you must go to Gary Beswick and Adam Nunn . What “Team Tayls” has achieved together makes me immensely proud, and I could not have wished for better colleagues or better friends. Your professionalism, loyalty and unwavering support have meant more than words can express.

View 2 Images Anthony Taylor was an experienced referee (Image: Getty Images)

‌



“It hasn’t always been easy – the pressure is intense and the scutiny is constant – but it has been an immense privilege to be at the heart of the game I love. Football is built on passion, and whilst decisions will always be debated, it has been an honour to serve the game with integrity and professionalism.

“Most importantly, thank you to my family and friends. Your love, patience and unwavering support have been my foundation throughout this journey. The sacrifices you have made alongside me have never gone unnoticed, and I simply would not have achieved any of this without you.

‌



“To everyone who has been part of this remarkable journey, thank you. It has been the privilege of a lifetime. The time is now right to step aside and look forward to transitioning to the next chapter of my career.”

Hinting at future plans in the public eye, Taylor confirmed he will now be represented by barristers Trinity Chambers and added: "To follow what comes next, follow me on Instagram… @anthonytaylor.official."

Taylor is one of several officials to have retired from English football this summer. Referee Darren Bond and assistant referees Natalie Aspinall and Marc Perry also hung up their whistles after the 2025/26 season concluded.

Article continues below

Meanwhile, referee Jeremy Simpson and assistant referee Mark Russell called it a day in the Championship, while referee Cristiana Hattersley retired from WSL duty.
