World.title: Does it really matter how you watch The Odyssey? Film-lovers are divided
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

After purchasing tickets more than a year ago, Christopher Nolan fans finally experienced the award-winning director’s new movie The Odyssey at the Kramer IMAX Theatre in Regina on Thursday. The theatre in the Saskatchewan Science Centre is one of just 41 in the world that can show the movie on 70-millimetre IMAX film.

Fans flock to Regina as The Odyssey hits one of 41 70mm IMAX theatres

Before last Friday, you probably didn’t consider that there could be a wrong way to watch a movie.

Then Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey came out, and the internet erupted with a lot of chatter about the "best" way to see the film, which is based on Homer's epic about a man on a decade-long quest to return home after fighting in the Trojan War.

It all ties back to the Hollywood director’s decision to shoot the entire film with IMAX 70 mm film cameras, the largest format available.

That means the movie will look a little bit different, depending on what kind of theatre you watch it in .

Add in promotional material from star Matt Damon urging audiences to "experience The Odyssey in IMAX 70 mm" and one corner of the internet has concluded this is "the way Nolan intended" the film to be seen.

Another corner of the internet is absolutely roasting him for it.

What kind of filmmaker makes a movie that can only be shown in its "ideal form" at 41 theatres worldwide — only nine of which are in Canada?

One who wants people to be intentional about their movie-going, said Leslie-Ann Coles, f ounder and executive director of the Toronto-based Female Eye Film Festiva l.

" It's absolutely brilliant that he shot it on IMAX cameras that are bigger than God and not well suited to the small screen," she said in an email to CBC News. "Kudos to him. Let's keep cinema alive in theatres."

Audiences make long journeys to IMAX theatres

When CBC News asked if Nolan really did intend for his film to be watched in one specific format, his publicist did not respond.

But that hasn’t stopped a huge number of people from journeying to their nearest IMAX theatre.

WATCH | The Odyssey sells out 70mm IMAX theatres a year in advance: Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey sells out 70 mm Imax screenings a year in advance | Duration 2:15 The movie will be screened in the 70 mm Imax format in 26 theatres worldwide, including the Kramer Imax theatre in Regina's science centre.

IMAX says its theatres accounted for a massive 20 per cent share of The Odyssey’s global debut, delivering $52 million US in sales.

There was so much hype, IMAX put tickets on sale for some 70 mm showtimes a full year in advance. Some theatres even added midnight and 3 a.m. screenings — and they sold out.

On average, it costs about $10 more to see a film on the IMAX screen than on a regular theatre screen. Transportation to the nearest theatre can add a premium, and that is a source of frustration for some people online.

For others, it's simply unnecessary.

Spectacle versus accessibility

Watching this particular movie in an IMAX 70 mm theatre will allow you to "feel the full impact of how it was shot, so you’ll be on The Odyssey with all of us," says Damon in the film’s promotion.

While that may be an incredible experience, it’s simply not an option for Jamesie Fournier, co-ordinator of the Aulajut Nunavut International Film Festival.

Iqaluit has just one movie theatre and Yellowknife, he points out, has none, let alone a 70 mm screen.

Jamesie Fournier, co-ordinator of the Aulajut Nunavut International Film Festival, says the format of a movie can enhance the spectacle of the story but also distract from the heart of its message. (CBC News)

"Ideally, we'd all love to be able to see it in that way but it's just not a reality for a lot of folks out there," Fournier said.

As someone who works hard to bring the movie-theatre experience to communities that don’t have one, he’s not convinced the format is the most important thing.

"Being able to see it in any way is going to be able to make a difference," Fournier said. "Whether you're being kind of stupefied by the brilliant visuals… or if you're kind of internalizing this story."

And there is a lot to internalize in The Odyssey.

“Holding on to so much grief and regret and pain and trauma and being able to finally come back to our home,” is a theme Fournier said will resonate with people, no matter how they watch the movie.

World.title: A 67-year-old died in one of B.C.'s oldest and largest open water swim events. Here's what we know
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

The B.C. Coroners Service is investigating the death of a 67-year-old man at an open water swim event on Okanagan Lake this past weekend.

Police say the man was taking part in the Across the Lake swim event, which has been running since 1949.

In a release, West Kelowna RCMP said the man was found unresponsive in the water roughly two hours after he started the event and was taken to shore. Attempts by B.C. Ambulance crews to resuscitate him failed.

WATCH | Man dies in Okanagan Lake at open water swim event: Man drowns in Okanagan Lake during mass swimming event | Duration 1:49 Police in Kelowna say a man taking part in a mass swim died over the weekend. The event called Across the Lake Swim, attracts more than 1,000 swimmers each year on a course across Okanagan Lake.

Multiple race participants reported being blown off course by high winds and choppy waters unlike those they've experienced in past years.

About the event

Event organizers have yet to comment on the death.

According to the event's website, Across the Lake is "the largest and longest continuously running open water swim event in Canada."

Participants swim either 2.1 kilometres or 1.5 kilometres, starting in West Kelowna and ending at Hot Sands Beach in Kelowna.

The Across the Water sees participants swim either 2.1 or 1.5 kilometres across Okanagan Lake. (Across the Water)

The event includes a competitive category and open swims for all ages. Roughly 1,200 people registered for this year's competition.

Support paddlers — people in boats or paddleboards who provide support to swimmers — are allowed but are not required for participation, the website says.

Choppy waters

Many participants have reported challenging conditions that took them off course.

Tiana Langedyk said she was among those pulled off course as winds picked up.

"A lot of my fellow swimmers and our support paddlers were also going off course ... I was swimming as hard as I could [and] I realized I wasn't moving," she said.

"It was a scary moment."

Tiana Langedyk says she was among the participants to be blown off course as winds picked up and currents swelled. (Marc D'Amours/CBC)

Karlyn Pipes, a former lifeguard and past participant in Across the Lakes, watched the event from shore and said she could see dozens of participants and paddlers being taken off course as they came to the middle of the water.

"On either side it was relatively calm, but as soon as they hit the middle ... they were getting pushed out into the water," she said.

Even the fastest swimmers, she said, were being challenged.

Safety measures

Pipes said it would have been difficult for organizers to anticipate the challenges.

The wind seemed to pick up mid-race, she said, and once people started being pushed around there was no choice but to continue.

Karlyn Pipes, a former lifeguard and past participant in Across the Lake, said there were lots of flotation devices and safety paddlers providing support to swimmers. (Chris Hromek)

"You can't sit there and say everybody get in a boat. If you look at the video, there were hundreds of water safety [craft] out there," she said, adding that there were many instances of people being helped as they encountered problems.

Pipes suggested future events could mandate the inclusion of flotation devices tied to participants so they have something to cling onto if they encounter problems.

"I have swum in races in Europe and it is mandatory of adults," she said.

Investigation ongoing

Pipes said it would be useful to know if the individual who died had a flotation device, and she also had questions about whether he may have encountered a medical emergency that led to him being unconscious out on the water.

"If he had a medical condition or something, this is different than somebody who just got overly tired and couldn't continue," she said, offering her condolences to family.

RCMP have called the death a drowning, but have referred the case to the B.C. Coroners Service for an official cause of death.

The coroner's office says it doesn't usually provide details due to privacy concerns and it may be several months before its investigation is completed.

It marks the fifth death on Okanagan Lake in the past few weeks.

World.title: A Sask. artist's phone fell 1.1 km from a plane. They found it in a canola field in 'pristine' condition
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

A Regina artist is thankful her phone survived after being sucked out of a plane and falling more than a kilometre to the ground below.

Heather Cline says she couldn't believe they were able to successfully track the iPhone to a canola field, and was even more surprised when they discovered it intact and undamaged — despite not being in a case.

"I think it's going to be like buried in the dirt, smashed," Cline said in an interview. "I literally looked at the phone, sitting there face up, just up against a few strands of canola. It's pristine."

A 'great day' for flying

Cline uses the iPhone to capture images from the back seat of the two-seater plane as her husband, David Stanchuk pilots.

She then used those photos and videos as references for aerial paintings.

She's been using the method ever since Stanchuk got his pilot licence.

Heather Cline and David Stanchuk pose for a photo next to their Cessna Skyhawk. (Courtesy Heather Cline)

Stanchuk said he always wanted to be an astronaut and began flying as an air cadet. It wasn't until almost a decade ago that he finally got his flight certification.

"It's just for fun and it's a bonus that the first time I took her up, she was just gobsmacked by the views. It's changed her art practice completely," Stanchuk said.

Cline said the birds-eye view has allowed her to observe the grid-like system of the Saskatchewan prairie, and the collision between cultivated and natural land.

As a full-time working artist, Cline said the iPhone was a "pretty big investment" when she purchased it last month to replace her aging phone and failing digital camera. She even purchased a grip that would help the iPhone feel like a conventional camera.

Friday was a "great day for flying," Cline said, but the grip had yet to arrive in the mail. Instead, she used a small lapel case.

One of the last images captured by Heather Cline from her seat in the Cessna Skyhawk before the iPhone was sucked out of the plane. (Courtesy Heather Cline)

The couple had been in the air for roughly 30 minutes, and were circling wind turbines at an altitude of 1.1 kilometres at speeds in excess of 100 km/h, when things went wrong.

"We have a photographic window and the air stream sucked the phone right out of the case," Cline said.

"I literally was not believing at first, like, that I could have done this. And then he's just looking at me and he's like, 'I told you not to drop the phone.'"

Cline immediately activated the Find My iPhone tool on her Apple Watch, but had little hope they would be able to track down anything salvageable. Stanchuk said he circled the area a couple of times to make sure they had a good GPS location of where the phone was.

Then they headed home, got in a truck and headed out to begin the search.

'Can you even get insurance?'

Cline can't help but laugh when asked about what went through her head as travelled toward the phone.

"I was just sick. I was like, 'can you even get insurance for dropping your phone out of a plane?' Like, what do you say on the claim? 'I'm an idiot?'" Cline said.

The flight plan of the couple's plane is displayed on the iPhone that fell to the ground. (Germain Wilson/CBC)

The couple travelled nearly 100 kilometres east of Regina to an area near Wolseley, Sask., trying to get as close as possible to the fallen phone.

They travelled on grids roads, trails and, eventually, in a canola field on foot. It was there they found the phone undamaged, still capable of recording videos and photographs.

Cline said she doesn't plan to stop her flights, but may take more drastic measures to ensure it's secure.

"Maybe we'll cable-tie it to my hand," Cline said.

World.content:
Article content

The very pages of The Talented Mr. Ripley feel soaked in summer sun and warmed by the sultry heat of the Italian seaside setting. Patricia Highsmith, Queen of the literary crime novel, seduces her readers here with an absorbing tale of murder, secrets, and betrayal. The titular and enigmatic Tom Ripley has an unmatched chameleon-like ability to take on any persona. Can anyone ever really know the true Tom, even Tom himself? When he sets his gaze on the carefree, affluent life of Dickie Greenleaf and love interest, Marge Sherwood, Tom decides he will stop at nothing to make this his life too, no matter the cost.

World.title: De la Espriella denied aspired control over Colombia’s Congress
World.content:
Colombia’s Congress denied control over the legislative agenda to President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella and voted for a president loyal to former President Alvaro Uribe.

De la Espriella proposed his friend, Senator Alfredo Deluque of the U Party, to assume the leadership of the Senate, which would have given the government control over the congressional agenda.

Ahead of the vote, eight parties expressed their support for Deluque’s candidacy, which would have given him a 55-vote majority in the anonymous vote.

Former President Alvaro Uribe, whose Democratic Center party would be granted the presidency, accused “Abelardo’s circle” of trying to “get rid of this party” and vowed to “defend ourselves.”

Uribe had put up Democratic Center Senator Honorio Henriquez for the job and ordered his 17 senators to stick to their original vote.

If the Tiger roars to destroy the Democratic Center, we’ll have to become hardworking bees and defend ourselves, just like bees do when they’re attacked… I’m frightened by the idea circulating among De La Espriella’s inner circle of destroying that party. Former President Alvaro Uribe

The former president got the support of President Gustavo Petro, arguably Abelardo’s biggest political enemy.

At a rally that was held ahead of the vote, Petro warned senators of his leftist Historic Pact party “not to vote for fascism.”

Under the leadership of Senate bench leader Ivan Cepeda, who lost the presidential election to De la Espriella last month, all 26 of the pact’s senators voted for Henriquez.

Enjoying the secrecy of their vote, dissidents from the parties who were ordered to vote Deluque also turned on the president-elect and delivered Henrique 56 votes. Deluque ended up with only 45.

Less than three weeks before taking office, De la Espriella lost the loyalty of its largest coalition partner in Congress and will have to negotiate his agenda with them.

World.title: Petro calls for “peaceful resistance” against Colombia’s incoming “viceroyalty”
World.content:
President Gustavo Petro called on the people to “prepare peaceful resistance” to the “viceroyalty” that “has been imposed as the president of Colombia.”

During an Independence Day speech in the poor south of Bogota, Petro told thousands of supporters that “the next president of Colombia will be a servant to the rulers of the United States who helped him ‘get elected’.”

“We move from the status of a republic to the status of a viceroyalty again, just like 216 years ago,” said Petro, who on Sunday accepted to become the political leader of the leftist opposition.

It is time to give the second cry of independence… Shout freedom and resistance! Gustavo Petro

Rather than a repetition of the 1810 revolution, the outgoing president proposed to “prepare for peaceful resistance” in defense of communities who benefited from the government’s reforms.

How do you repeal the decree on hourly work that ends the labor reform that created stability, a vital wage, and better working conditions? How? Well, with a permanent general strike of millions of working men and women in Colombia! It is not just by shouting, it is not just by raising flags, they are already used to that… No, it is with a production strike, which is permitted by the National Constitution of Colombia, it is a universal right! And that indeed is civil disobedience! If they are going to strike down the stabilities, the working conditions achieved in this government, a general and indefinite strike in Colombia! Gustavo Petro

Petro threatened to “surround the centers of illegitimate power in Colombia until legitimacy exists once again, which can only be achieved through free popular decision without algorithms, and without foreign money.”

To protect the people, the president suggested the creation of unarmed “liberatory guards” that work in a network, “because they want to kill.”

Wherever they touch a neighborhood, wherever they touch a peasant estate, the network must summon solidarity, it must become a demonstration of all adjacent neighborhoods, of all adjacent villages, of the whole country if necessary. Gustavo Petro

“The only way to stop fascism,” said Petro, “is in peace. It is with joy, but it is with millions and millions of Colombian men and women.”

World.title: Petro to assume political leadership of Colombia’s leading leftist party
World.content:
President Gustavo Petro said Sunday that he would become the leader of Colombia’s largest political party on the left, the Historic Pact.

In a tweet, Petro responded to Senator Ivan Cepeda, who proposed him as party president at a political rally in the city of Tunja on Saturday.

Petro said he would “accept the proposal of my party after surrendering power to the far-right President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella.

The president said he would first go “on a vacation I deserve and didn’t have during four years of governance.”

We will work toward peace and social justice and for a national agreement that prevents violent confrontation among Colombians, and we will seek to contribute to the democratic stability of the countries that Simon Bolívar liberated. President Gustavo Petro

The Historic Pact party was formed in March from a coalition of multiple parties that have long supported the political careers of Petro and Cepeda.

Following a significant electoral victory, the party became the largest of Colombia and will assume 25 of 103 seats in the Senate.

Petro’s former party, Colombia Humana, contributed 12 senators to the collective.

The president started his political career while being a member of the M-19 guerrilla group, which demobilized in 1990.

Petro was elected to the House of Representatives in 1998 an became a senator in 2006.

Between 2012 and 2015, the president was mayor of the capital Bogota.

Petro has been the most popular and powerful leftist politician since the violent death of Liberal Party leader Jorge Eliecer Gaitan in 1948, and was sanctioned by the US Government amid his opposition to the genocide in Gaza.

The president has insisted that his successor won the June elections through fraud and has refused to recognize De la Espriella as his successor.

World.title: Colombia’s peace and human rights offices to close: De la Espriella
World.content:
Colombia’s President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella announced on Monday that he will close the Peace Commissioner’s Office, which was in charge of negotiating peace and implementing peace deals with illegal armed groups.

“The Office of the Peace Commissioner is coming to an end, because there will be no more sham peace processes during my administration,” said De la Espriella in his weekly address to the nation that was broadcast on his social media platforms.

According to the far-right president-elect, who will take office on August 7, other presidential commissioners that will disappear are those of National Reconciliation. and the Office of Human Rights and International Humanitarian Law.

The functions of these offices will be taken over by the Interior, Foreign and Defense ministries that, according to De la Espriella, have been doubling the work of the presidential commissioners.

“These are functions that, by law, are already carried out by other ministries,” so the government can “avoid duplication and extra costs,” said the president-elect.

De la Espriella seems keen to abruptly end the peace policy of his predecessor, President Gustavo Petro, for being too lenient to illegal armed groups.

The president-elect also promised to close war crimes tribunal JEP, which has been trying thousands of former guerrillas and former members of the military.

De la Espriella could only do this through legislation that would change the constitution and the international treaties that protect the victims of an armed conflict between the State and the now-defunct guerrilla organization FARC.

World.title: Petro to seek court order to annul election of De la Espriella
World.content:
Colombia’s President Gustavo Petro said Tuesday that he will seek a court order to annul the election of President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella.

In a post on social media platform X, Petro said he had gather enough evidence to prove that his successor “was elected from abroad, with nonexistent votes.”

“Today we are presenting the body of evidence we have gathered to the representatives elected by the people, and we will file a lawsuit with the courts to annul the elections, as is our duty,” said the outgoing president.

We are not making things up when we say that Abelardo’s government was elected from abroad, with nonexistent votes included in the percentage automatically adjusted by algorithms created by private Israeli companies with the endorsement of their genocidal government. President Gustavo Petro

“We are facing not only the imminent rise of fascism in Colombia but also what may be the greatest threat to global democracy since Hitler’s time,” said Petro.

In a response that was broadcast on his social media channels, De la Espriella reiterated that Petro was a “tyrant” who was trying to perpetuate power through a coup d’etat with the help of the leftist runner-up in the election, Senator Ivan Cepeda.

Even before becoming a candidate, I warned you: Petro is a tyrant in the making who seeks to perpetuate himself in power by any means necessary. And today, as the president-elect of all of you, I ratify what I have said for so many years. This is no longer an analysis or an opinion; it is a palpable reality. From the moment nearly 13 million Colombians stood by me to defeat him and his political frontman, Petro and Cepeda began their Plan B to stay in power, no matter what it takes. And they want to do so through a coup d’état. President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella

The president-elect asked the armed forces “to protect the Constitution and democracy, and to disobey any order that Petro may be giving to the contrary.”

Resistance, dear compatriots. We cannot allow them to snatch away what we achieved at the ballot box in an epic democratic battle this past June 21. Let us resist, for August 7 is near. God, the vote, and democracy have spoken; we are going to defend the Constitution and the rule of law as we must. President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella

De la Espriella has long claimed that he will extradite his predecessor to the United States.

World.title: De la Espriella suspends Colombia’s transfer of power
World.content:
President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella on Tuesday suspended the transfer of power after President Gustavo Petro accused him of fraud.

In a post on social media platform X, De la Espriella said he had “given instructions to the vice president-elect of the Republic to immediately suspend the handover process with the corrupt government that is ending its term.”

I have just given instructions to the president-elect of the Republic to immediately suspend the handover process with the corrupt government that is ending its term, a government that, with its decisions and its conduct, seeks to destroy Colombia. Abelardo de la Espriella

“My duty is to protect the interests of the Nation and guarantee a serious, transparent transition at the service of Colombians, never to legitimize the disaster or the disregard for the constitutional order,” said the president-elect.

In a press conference, Finance Minister German Avila said that he had also suspended cooperation with the transition process in response to comments made by a member of De la Espriella’s team, convicted fraudster Carlos ALonso Lucio, that “undermine the respect, dignity, and decency” of the transition process.

Recent statements by members of the incoming transition committee undermine the respect, dignity, and decency of a process such as the one we are carrying out. These statements were surely made intentionally to hinder the transition process. Accusations and insults have been leveled against the president and his administration, alleging that they are criminals, that they are manipulating the justice system, and that they are seeking to extradite us, among other blunders that have been made. German Avila

“All we have received are insults and disrespect, slander and offenses, and we will not tolerate a single further act of aggression or threat,” said the finance minister.

Avila asked Inspector General Gregorio Eljach to oversee the continuation of the process.

In a post on social media platform X, incoming vice-President Jose Manuel Restrepo stressed that his team would continue going through the books to make sure that “those who have betrayed the trust of the Colombian people must answer to the institutions and to history.”

World.title: Colombia’s Petro refuses to recognize successor Abelardo de la Espriella
World.content:
Colombia’s outgoing President Gustavo Petro said Monday that he doesn’t recognize the outcome of the election that made the far-right Abelardo de la Espriella president-elect.

In a post on social media platform X, Petro said he saw “evidence of electoral fraud carried out through algorithms and with foreign funding, which is prohibited by our Constitution.”

The president called the alleged election fraud “the harshest blow to national sovereignty since the Spanish reconquest during the years of the Patria Boba.”

Colombia’s president, according to the decision of the Colombians, is the philosopher Iván Cepeda. We have suffered the harshest blow to national sovereignty since the Spanish reconquest during the years of the “Patria Boba.” President Gustavo Petro

According to Petro, he had “all the information about how, from an IP server located in Los Angeles, California, owned by the Bautista brothers, integrated into the scrutiny operation, algorithms were used that substantially varied the vote in favor of” De la Espriella.

Additionally, the president accused a close associate of US President Donald Trump, Florida attorney Dan Newlin, of paying a $1.8 million Facebook campaign for De la Espriella.

In a post that was published on Sunday, Petro asked De la Espriella of he had registered the alleged campaign contribution of Trump’s former ambassador pick.

In a response, Newlin said that “I have contributed zero dollars, not a single cent, directly or indirectly, to his campaign.”

“I challenge you to provide evidence to the Colombian people to support these demonstrably false accusations. You will not be able to do so, because no such contribution ever occurred,” said the Florida attorney.

Petro has been promoting conspiracy theories about alleged election fraud ever since the June 21 elections that were won by De la Espriella with a 250,000-vote difference.

World.title: Colombia’s land agency claims elections triggered surge in land theft
World.content:
The director of Colombia’s land agency ANT filed criminal complaints about at least eight attempts to steal land from beneficiaries of President Gustavo Petro’s land reform.

According to ANT director Harman Felipe, armed men associated with drug traffickers and paramilitary commanders intimidated the communities at six plots that had been given to victim of the armed conflict.

The incidents we have reported follow the same pattern of intimidation against families who have benefited from the Agrarian Reform. The threats are intended to force communities to leave so that land currently in the hands of small farmers can be reclaimed. What is at stake is not only the safety of these families, but also the defense of the Agrarian Reform and the right of small farmers to remain on their land. Harman Felipe

In one of the attempts, armed land thieves allegedly tortured members of a family that had been given land in Puerto Lopez, a municipality in the central Meta province.

This land used to belong to Ignacio Alvarez, a drug trafficker of the now-defunct Norte del Valle cartel.

Most incidents happened in the Magdalena Medio region, where the legal occupants of five plots were ordered to abandon their properties by armed men.

At one of the plots, which used to be of Daniel Barrera, the owners were told “these lands don’t belong to guerrillas.”

At another plot, a member of the Isaza Clan threatened a women’s association that was given control over land that used to belong to Maria Georgina Arango, the wife of a former commander of paramilitary organization AUC, Ovidio Isaza, a.k.a. “Roque.”

In Cordoba, a Caribbean province, the legal occupants of another one of Alvarez’s plots fled.

“We want the Attorney General’s Office to investigate these incidents, which are not minor matters and could even constitute crimes against humanity due to the displacement they have caused,” the ANT director told press.

Land thieves stole between 6.5 and 8 million hectares of land during the armed conflict between 1964 and 2016, often with the support of corrupt elements within the State.

World.title: Chile declares state of catastrophe in the north after storm leaves at least ten dead
World.content:
Chile declares state of catastrophe in the north after storm leaves at least ten dead

21st Tuesday, July 2026 - 17:59 UTC Full article

The weather front began on July 15 in the south of the country and moved north, where it hit the desert regions — areas where rainfall of this magnitude is uncommon

Chile's president, José Antonio Kast, declared on Monday a 30-day constitutional state of catastrophe in the Coquimbo region and the Huasco province, in the Atacama region, in response to the intense storm battering the country's north. According to the government's latest tally, the phenomenon has left at least ten people dead nationwide, four missing, and nearly 100,000 residents cut off by road closures. Authorities warned the toll could rise, as numerous areas remain unreachable.

“As the situation in the Coquimbo region and the Huasco province has grown more serious,” Kast said in announcing the measure, which allows the deployment of military personnel, restrictions on movement when necessary, and faster delivery of resources and assistance. The government mobilized the army for rescue operations.

The weather front began on July 15 in the south of the country and moved north, where it hit the desert regions of Coquimbo and Atacama with particular intensity — areas where rainfall of this magnitude is uncommon. Swollen rivers blocked the main access routes and left many towns isolated from one another. In Coquimbo, about 460 kilometers north of Santiago, flooding, mudslides, and power cuts also affected the drinking-water supply. In the town of Andacollo, more than 300 millimeters of rain fell in a single night.

The National Service for Disaster Prevention and Response (Senapred) recorded more than 1,100 homes destroyed or seriously damaged and about 2,200 people affected, along with more than 33,000 isolated in Atacama and Coquimbo. The Energy Ministry said around 150,000 people were without electricity. Classes were suspended in several regions.

“What normally falls in a month fell in an hour, which leads us to classify this event as abnormal and extreme rainfall,” said Deputy Interior Minister Máximo Pavez. Arnaldo Zúñiga, of Chile's Meteorological Directorate, said the country had not seen an episode of this kind in about two decades.

The storm comes during a season of extreme events in the region. In recent weeks, a double earthquake in Venezuela left thousands of casualties, and various parts of the Southern Cone have faced severe storms. Chilean authorities expect the rains to continue through the week, and are maintaining alerts and precautionary restrictions at dozens of ports, also affected by high seas and wind gusts of more than 100 kilometers per hour.

World.title: PM Andy Burnham’s first conversation was with President Trump, whom he invited to visit Manchester
World.content:
PM Andy Burnham’s first conversation was with President Trump, whom he invited to visit Manchester

21st Tuesday, July 2026 - 07:16 UTC Full article

The Prime Minister also hoped that he would be able to show the President what Manchester had to offer during a visit in the future.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham spoke to the President of the United States, Donald Trump, shortly after taking office Monday afternoon, 20th July 2026. According to 10 Downing Street, the Prime Minister began by congratulating the President on a successful World Cup and agreed that England had an excellent tournament.

The Prime Minister also hoped that he would be able to show the President what Manchester had to offer during a visit in the future.

Setting out his vision as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, the Prime Minister said he would be focused on ensuring reindustrialization up and down the country to ensure good growth in every postcode.

The Prime Minister also underlined his commitment to defense and security and said ensuring the security of the UK and its Allies was at the top of his agenda.

The President then updated on the situation in the Middle East, and the Prime Minister outlined the UK’s commitment to securing the movement of shipping in the Strait of Hormuz to support global supply chains and drive down costs for businesses and families across the country. They concluded looking forward to speaking again soon.

The report from Washington said the newly appointed UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and US President Donald Trump held a phone call immediately following Burnham's inauguration.

The conversation was described by Trump as “interesting” and going “very well,” and covered the long-standing UK-US alliance, trade, North Sea oil and gas, and stability in the Middle East.

Details of the call indicate that Burnham assured the US President of London's continued commitment to defense, explicitly confirming UK support for securing shipping lanes in the Strait of Hormuz.

Likewise on the North Sea Oil, and energy policy, Trump expressed strong interest in expanding oil drilling in the North Sea.

Finally Burnham used the introductory call to officially invite President Trump to visit Manchester, England, an offer Trump reportedly accepted. The visit may coincide with the 2027 G20 summit, which is rumored to be hosted in Manchester.

Other phone calls by PM Burnham on Monday afternoon included, Chancellor Merz. Germany; President Antonio Costa of the European Council; NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte; President of France, Emmanuel Macron; President of the European Commission Ursula von der Leyen, and Ukraine’ president Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

World.title: The Falklands, FIFA and the Future of the British Overseas Territories
World.content:
The Falklands, FIFA and the Future of the British Overseas Territories 21st Tuesday, July 2026 - 07:10 UTC Full article Members of the Argentine team held up a banner exclaiming ‘Las Malvinas son Argentinas’ (‘The Falklands are Argentine’). By Peter Clegg (*)

I have been researching the British Overseas Territories (BOTs) and their geopolitical relationships for over twenty years, and I cannot remember so much focus on them as there has been in recent days. The FIFA World Cup match between England and Argentina provoked heated discussions over the future of the Falkland Islands (or Malvinas if you are Argentine). Gibraltar has received significant media coverage with the removal of the border infrastructure with Spain. The Caricom Reparations Committee has called for the British Virgin Islands (BVI) to be decolonized by the UK, and new UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham will likely retain the government’s commitment to return the Chagos Islands to Mauritius. So, are we witnessing centrifugal forces that could fracture the BOTs’ relationship with the ‘UK family’? Let us start with the Falkland Islands. It is not unusual for the Falklands to be the source of heated debate when England play Argentina, but there has certainly been a lot of rhetorical exchanges. Before the game, Argentina’s vice-president, Victoria Villarruel, called England ‘usurping pirates’, which The Sun newspaper called ‘a hate-filled tirade’. Then, after Argentina’s win, members of the team held up a banner exclaiming ‘Las Malvinas son Argentinas’ (‘The Falklands are Argentine’). The response from the UK was swift, the government said: ‘The World Cup might not be ours, but the Falkland Islands definitely are’, while Conservative Party leader, Kemi Badenoch declared: ‘The Conservatives fought for them before; we will do so again if necessary’. And Nigel Farage, leader of Reform UK, called for the capacity of the Royal Navy to be boosted. So, what can be discerned from all of this? First, nothing will change in the foreseeable future, but arguably the extent of diplomatic support for UK sovereignty is fraying. The Trump administration has hinted a more sympathetic position towards Argentina’s claim, and it defended the Argentina team’s right to unfurl the banner, while since Brexit the European Union has used ‘Malvinas’ in official communiqués. However, there is not a clear view at the United Nations or in international courts in relation to who has the strongest territorial claim, and the view of Falkland Islanders themselves is important when it comes to self-determination. It is also worth remembering that the Falklands has over 60 nationalities living there and should no longer be considered as a ‘white British’ population. Second, although it is highly unlikely that there will a repeat of the 1982 military conflict, concerns have been raised over the UK’s capability to defend the Falklands, however, the UK government is confident defenses are adequate. Gibraltar was the focus of media attention on 15th July when the border infrastructure with Spain was removed—the last frontier fence in Western Europe. This was the culmination of protracted negotiations to avoid a hard border, which was a possibility after Brexit. The deal eliminates controls and customs checks at the border and gives Spain responsibility for Schengen controls at Gibraltar’s airport and port. In a related development, Spain removed Gibraltar from its blacklist of tax havens; Gibraltar had been on the list since 1991. Gibraltar Chief Minister Fabian Picardo said: ‘The frontier that has so often divided and constrained our region will now become a place of cooperation and shared opportunity’, while Spain’s prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, stated that an ‘open wound’ was finally being closed. Commentary in sections of the UK’s right-wing media was highly critical. For example, Stephen Glover in the Daily Mail, claimed that Gibraltar ‘has virtually been handed to Spain’. Glover admitted that Brexit had posed a problem but then criticized the EU for behaving in a ‘bloody-minded way’. He also slated Picardo for going along with ‘this charade’. This illustrates two points: First, the widespread cognitive dissonance on the part of those who strongly argued for Brexit but can never bring themselves to admit the real challenges the decision caused and that pragmatic compromises are needed to resolve them. Second, the paternalist view towards Gibraltar—the local government was centrally involved in the negotiations and felt that on balance the deal was the right one. If UK politicians and commentators say they support the BOTs, they also need to accept the autonomy of the territories to make their own decisions. The removal of the border infrastructure will undoubtedly bring new challenges, but many opportunities—and it is this effective functional cooperation that is most important and may well lessen the centrality of formal sovereignty. Caribbean BOTs. Then there is the Caricom (Caribbean Community) Reparations Commission, which has recently called on the UK to ‘decolonize’ its remaining territories in the region—the Caribbean BOTs. The Commission focused particularly on the BVI. Sir Hilary Beckles, chair of the commission, argued: ‘We object to the fact that in the Virgin Islands, our people cannot make fundamental decisions because they have to consult with the British governor and consult with Downing Street to make decisions’. This is to an extent true, but the BVI has significant autonomy, though it has not always used that power in the best way (see for example, Commission of Inquiry Report). The focus on the BVI by the Commission coincides with the beginning of constitutional review talks between the territory and the UK. The House of Assembly of the Virgin Islands is asking for a significant reduction in the power of the Governor and greater devolved responsibilities to the local government. It will be interesting to see what is negotiated, but it is unlikely the BVI will get everything it wants and there is little appetite for independence. Thus, the Caricom Reparations Commission intervention is timely, but does not fully acknowledge the nuances of relations between the BVI (and other Caribbean BOTs) and the UK—that independence is not an option and while that remains the case the UK believes it should have certain powers to intervene, if necessary, to ensure its international obligations are upheld. Finally, there is the situation in the Chagos Islands, also known as the British Indian Ocean Territory. I have written previously on the issue, and the handover has been paused because of opposition from the Trump administration despite earlier support. This is because US agreement is needed due to the UK/US military base on Diego Garcia. There is recognition from the UK that there will be a delay, and this was recently illustrated by the renewal of an agreement with another BOT, St Helena—that any migrants arriving in the Chagos Islands will be sent to St Helena (St Helena will receive £9 million from the UK as part of the deal). Notwithstanding, it seems that Burnham will stick to the original agreement and push it through once the US is again supportive. The decision was criticized by many on the right but as has been the case throughout this saga there remains a failure to recognize the real international legal pressures that will lead to the return of the Chagos Islands to Mauritius. In conclusion, while recent events have generated an unusual degree of attention for the BOTs, it would be mistaken to view them as evidence of an imminent unravelling of the UK’s relationships with its remaining territories. One of the most important points is that the BOTs are too often discussed as though they constitute a single category with common interests and identical political aspirations. In reality, big differences exist between territories such as the Falkland Islands, Gibraltar, the BVI, and the Chagos Islands. These distinctions are not always recognized in public debate, yet such nuance is essential if recent developments are to be properly understood. There are undoubtedly pressures on UK relations with the BOTs, but few of these are entirely new. Questions of sovereignty, self-determination, constitutional reform, international law, and decolonization have shaped these ties for decades. Such pressures may have become more acute in the current geopolitical environment, but they are not fundamentally different in character. Indeed, the Chagos agreement is an attempt to address colonial legacies, any new constitutional settlement with the BVI is likely to mitigate similar concerns, and Gibraltar has largely resolved one of the most difficult practical consequences of Brexit. Arguably, the Labour government is achieving a considerable amount in this policy space. Nevertheless, because the BOTs are deeply connected to questions of history, empire, war, and national identity, they will continue to provoke strong opinions and intense political debate. (*) Peter Clegg is Professor of Politics and Head of Social Sciences at University Western England, UWE Bristol. He has written extensively on the political economy of the Caribbean and non-independent territories. Recent publications have focused on the Falkland Islands, the impact of Brexit, and COVID-19.

World.title: Burnham's first moves as UK PM: new chancellor, Miliband to foreign office and a social turn
World.content:
Burnham's first moves as UK PM: new chancellor, Miliband to foreign office and a social turn

20th Monday, July 2026 - 20:52 UTC Full article

Burnham, 56, acknowledged the fragility of his position and said politicians “need to be better” to restore stability

The United Kingdom's new prime minister, Labour's Andy Burnham, began shaping his government with a cabinet reshuffle and a series of socially oriented announcements, hours after taking office in place of Keir Starmer. The former mayor of Greater Manchester, who reached Downing Street without a general election after winning the Labour leadership, is Britain's seventh prime minister in a decade.

Among the cabinet changes, the appointment of John Healey as Chancellor of the Exchequer, in charge of finances, stood out as a move that surprised Westminster, after Rachel Reeves confirmed her departure. Former Energy Secretary Ed Miliband was promoted to foreign secretary, while Shabana Mahmood was reappointed home secretary. Louise Haigh, a close ally who coordinated his preparations for office, was placed in charge of the Cabinet Office as first secretary of state. Deputy Prime Minister and Justice Secretary David Lammy tendered his resignation. Further appointments are expected in the coming hours.

In his first speech outside Downing Street, delivered without a lectern or notes, Burnham promised to “end rough sleeping” among homeless people, a goal backed by an official announcement of an additional £340 million over five years. He proposed a “circuit breaker” for a system that, he said, had taken wrong turns since the 1980s, and previewed a ten-year plan, the construction of more council housing, and changes to the education system. Announcements on the cost of living will begin on Tuesday.

Burnham, 56, acknowledged the fragility of his position and said politicians “need to be better” to restore stability, alluding to the succession of governments in recent years. He pledged to honor defense-spending commitments and to respect the country's fiscal rules. The next general election is not expected for about three years.

Internationally, US President Donald Trump held a phone call with Burnham on Monday, according to the White House. Trump praised on his social network the new prime minister's intention to expand North Sea oil production, having earlier attributed Starmer's downfall to alleged failures on immigration and energy. The change of government also places British foreign policy in Miliband's hands, including the position on the Falklands, which the outgoing Starmer government had reaffirmed in recent days amid the controversy over the banner displayed by Argentine players at the World Cup.

Starmer, who governed for two years after his 2024 victory, bid farewell saying he leaves the country “stronger and fairer.” “I go with good grace, I go with a smile,” he said.

World.title: Petro calls for 'general and indefinite strike' if successor repeals his reforms
World.content:
Petro calls for 'general and indefinite strike' if successor repeals his reforms

20th Monday, July 2026 - 20:12 UTC Full article

Petro warned that a repeal of the labor reform, approved in June last year, would in his view represent a setback for workers' rights

Colombia's outgoing president, Gustavo Petro, called on Monday for a “general and indefinite strike” should the government of his successor, Abelardo de la Espriella, repeal his administration's labor reform or reverse the land reform. De la Espriella, elected in the June 21 runoff, will take office on August 7.

“The opposition is exercised in the streets, with resistance and with peace, but it must be forceful,” Petro said during his last public address in southern Bogotá, delivered to mark Independence Day. He argued that social mobilization should become the main mechanism of opposition to the incoming government and encouraged unions and peasant, Indigenous and grassroots organizations to peacefully defend the reforms passed during his four-year term.

Petro warned that a repeal of the labor reform, approved in June last year, would in his view represent a setback for workers' rights. “If they are going to tear down the job stability and working conditions won under this government, there will be a general and indefinite strike in Colombia,” he said. He added that if the incoming government alters land-access policies, “there will be a national agrarian strike.”

The president-elect, a right-wing leader of the Defensores de la Patria movement, has announced that he will review several of the current government's main reforms, including the labor reform, arguing they harm job creation and the country's competitiveness. De la Espriella has not so far proposed an immediate repeal, but a review.

Petro does not recognize his successor's election, alleging fraud —a claim he has not substantiated and that runs counter to the official validation of the result. The National Electoral Council proclaimed De la Espriella president-elect on June 24, after completing the runoff count, in which he obtained 49.66% of the vote against 48.70% for the leftist Iván Cepeda. Cepeda himself accepted the defeat and announced he would take a seat in Congress under the opposition statute.

Monday's speech was Petro's final address to the public as president. He indicated he would continue to take part in political life from the opposition once he hands over power on August 7. That same Monday he was due to speak again at the seat of Congress, for the installation of the new legislative session.

World.title: Argentina's June trade surplus rises 149% year-on-year on stronger exports
World.content:
Argentina's June trade surplus rises 149% year-on-year on stronger exports

20th Monday, July 2026 - 20:05 UTC Full article

The June surplus, however, marked a 36.4% drop from May's figure, which had been a record $3.450 billion

Argentina posted a trade surplus of $2.194 billion in June, a 149.6% increase from the same month in 2025, driven by growth in exports, the National Institute of Statistics and Census (Indec) reported on Monday.

The June surplus, however, marked a 36.4% drop from May's figure, which had been a record $3.450 billion. With this result, the country strung together 31 consecutive months of surplus in its trade balance.

Trade flows —the sum of exports and imports— grew 16.4% year-on-year in June, to $15.916 billion. Exports totaled $9.055 billion, up 24.5% from June 2025, while imports reached $6.861 billion, a 7.3% year-on-year rise.

In the first half of the year, Argentina accumulated a trade surplus of $13.923 billion, with exports of $49.454 billion and imports of $35.531 billion. The surplus accumulated through June already exceeds that of all of 2025, which had stood at $11.320 billion.

Economy Minister Luis Caputo highlighted that first-half goods exports set “a new all-time record,” with growth of 24.4% compared with the same period the previous year. In a message on social media, Caputo said first-half foreign sales of fuels and energy rose 42.5% year-on-year, industrial manufactures 27.5%, primary products 24.4%, and agricultural manufactures 15.1%. According to the minister, exports of industrial manufactures, fuels and energy, and primary products recorded the highest value in the historical series.

Export performance in recent months has been underpinned largely by the energy sector, whose foreign sales had been showing strong year-on-year increases, partly linked to better international prices. Argentina's trade balance has posted uninterrupted positive results since late 2023.

World.title: Ortega says Nicaragua will hold no more elections
World.content:
Ortega says Nicaragua will hold no more elections

20th Monday, July 2026 - 20:03 UTC Full article

The president announced during the commemoration of the Sandinista revolution that he will pursue legal reforms to prevent the opposition from contesting power through the ballot box

Nicaraguan President Daniel Ortega said on Sunday that the country will no longer hold elections as a mechanism for the opposition to reach power. “There will be no more elections here for them to try to seize the government, to seize power,” he declared during the event marking the 47th anniversary of the Sandinista uprising that overthrew Anastasio Somoza Debayle in 1979, held in Managua.

Ortega, 80, has governed Nicaragua since 2007 and since 2017 has shared power with his wife, Rosario Murillo, named co-president in February 2025 following a constitutional reform pushed by the executive. That amendment extended the presidential term from five to six years and reorganized the structure of the state, meaning the next general elections would in theory be scheduled for November 2027. The reform was criticized by the UN, the Organization of American States, the European Union and the United States.

In his speech, Ortega announced that he would work with the National Assembly —controlled by his party— to pass laws that would “put up a wall” against parties seeking to reach the government through elections. He did not specify how the change would take shape.

While the statement does not immediately alter a known situation —international observers have for years reported the absence of real competition in Nicaraguan elections— it does mark an explicit shift in official rhetoric. In the 2021 presidential election, Ortega and Murillo jailed the main opposition candidates and claimed close to 76% of the vote, in a contest the United States and other governments did not recognize.

Opposition figures in exile interpreted Ortega's words as confirmation of a dominant-party model. Juan Sebastián Chamorro, one of the presidential hopefuls jailed before the 2021 election, said the president aspires to a single-party system inspired by models such as China's. The Costa Rica-based group Nicaragua Nunca Más said the Sandinista Front has become a party with no real opposition within the country, and pointed to the closure of thousands of civil organizations, the cancellation of parties and the shuttering of media outlets.

The announcement runs counter to Washington's policy, which since the 2018 crisis has conditioned any resolution on the restoration of democracy and free elections with international observation. In January, the State Department accused Murillo of having assumed the co-presidency without a mandate or legitimacy. Since 2018, the United States has imposed sanctions on dozens of officials and entities linked to Ortega's government.

World.title: Rubio says talks on Venezuela's democratic transition will begin in early August
World.content:
Rubio says talks on Venezuela's democratic transition will begin in early August

20th Monday, July 2026 - 19:51 UTC Full article

“I believe the first official conversations will begin the first week of August,” Rubio said at a news conference at Andrews Air Force Base

U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Monday that talks to begin a democratic transition in Venezuela will start in early August. Rubio, who leads Washington's relationship with Caracas, said a group representing the National Assembly elected in 2015 —the last one the United States recognizes as legitimate— met with the interim government and agreed to establish a forum for reconciliation talks and to begin the transition process.

“I believe the first official conversations will begin the first week of August,” Rubio said at a news conference at Andrews Air Force Base, before traveling to the Philippines for the ASEAN summit. The announcement coincides with a State Department statement last week backing a joint agenda set to begin on August 1, aimed at stability, democracy and national recovery, with the interim government's endorsement.

The United States has maintained a close relationship with Caracas since January 3, when it launched a military operation that captured Nicolás Maduro and flew him to New York to face criminal charges. Delcy Rodríguez, until then vice president, took over as interim president. Since then, Rubio has laid out a three-phase plan: stabilization, economic recovery and transition.

The process is advancing amid divisions within the opposition. The agenda does not include María Corina Machado, whose supporters have pressed for her role after arguing she won the 2024 election. Instead, representation falls to Dinorah Figuera, who holds —in a post disputed with Jorge Rodríguez— the presidency of the 2015 Assembly and returned to Caracas last month after years in exile. Figuera met with the U.S. chargé d'affaires and with Jorge Rodríguez, president of the Assembly that exercises effective control in the country and brother of the interim president, to agree on a technical and political working group.

The negotiations come during reconstruction work following the late-June earthquakes, which struck the north of the country. According to still-provisional official figures, the quakes left more than 5,200 dead and tens of thousands injured in La Guaira and Caracas, with hundreds of buildings and numerous public facilities collapsed.

On aid, Rubio said the United States had already contributed more than $180 million of the $300 million pledged. “We've already surpassed $180 million and we're looking for more; we'll do more,” he said, adding that Washington is working to help Venezuela access international financing for reconstruction, whose total cost is still being calculated.

World.title: In accepting life sentence, cartel boss ‘El Mayo’ urges young people not to follow his path
World.content:
Ismael “El Mayo” Zambada García, the Sinaloa Cartel co-founder who was arrested in 2024 after he was kidnapped in Mexico and flown to the United States, was sentenced to life in prison in the U.S. on Monday, 11 months after he pleaded guilty to drug trafficking charges.

Judge Brian Cogan handed down the sentence in the United States District Court for the Eastern District of New York, saying that life imprisonment for Zambada was justified by “the uncountable amount of drugs attributed to him and the number of murders.”

Cogan — the judge who presided over the trials of Joaquín “El Chapo” Guzmán and former Mexican Security Minister Genaro García Luna — also ordered Zambada, 76, to forfeit $15 billion in drug trafficking-related profits and assets.

The U.S. Justice Department (DOJ) noted in a statement that Zambada had “pleaded guilty to being a principal leader of a continuing criminal enterprise and a Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations (RICO) charge.”

Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division said that El Mayo’s sentence to life in prison marked “the end of his reign over the Sinaloa Cartel, one of the most violent and deadly drug cartels in history.”

“He will never again inflict carnage, corrupt public officials, or traffic deadly drugs into our communities that ruin Americans and their families,” Duva said.

Co-Founder of the Sinaloa Cartel, Ismael “El Mayo” Zambada Garcia SENTENCED TO LIFE IN PRISON and Ordered to Forfeit $15 Billion in Drug Trafficking Profits “Today, narco-trafficker El Mayo was sentenced to life in prison, marking the end of his reign over the Sinaloa Cartel,… pic.twitter.com/pWyPn2VJno — Criminal Division (@DOJCrimDiv) July 20, 2026

“El Mayo’s conviction is historic, and it reflects the Justice Department’s commitment to the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations that threaten American lives. To those who remain: we will find you, we will prosecute you, and you, too, will face substantial time in prison,” he said.

It has not yet been determined where Zambada will serve his life sentence. Earlier this month, Frank A. Perez, the drug trafficker’s lawyer, argued in a letter to Cogan that his client needs — and deserves — to be incarcerated in a prison where he can receive adequate medical care for his various health issues.

Perez argued that Zambada should be incarcerated in a prison where his health issues can be effectively treated because he pleaded guilty rather than opting to go to trial.

“In taking full responsibility for his wrongdoing, Mr. Zambada’s comportment has differed markedly from that of other foreign organized crime figures who have been brought to this country through extradition, including his former partner in the Sinaloa Cartel, Joaquin ‘Chapo’ Guzmán, who went through an 11-week jury trial seven years ago,” wrote the lawyer, who asserted that El Mayo’s “approach benefitted the system by reducing the logjam of justice.”

CNN reported that the judge on Monday “revealed sealed medical records, which show Zambada is experiencing declining cognitive abilities and other potentially progressive medical conditions.”

“While prosecutors argued he can receive medical care within the federal prison system, the judge said the Bureau of Prisons should carefully consider his health when deciding where he will serve his sentence,” CNN wrote.

The sentencing of Zambada came almost two years after he was kidnapped in Sinaloa by Joaquín Guzmán López, a son of Sinaloa Cartel co-founder “El Chapo” Guzmán, who is serving a life sentence in the Florence Supermax prison in Colorado. After his kidnapping on July 25, 2024, Zambada was forced onto a private plane and flown to a small airport in New Mexico, where he and Guzmán López were arrested by U.S. authorities. The Sinaloa Cartel kingpin — the father of 16 children, according to his lawyer — had never previously been arrested during his long criminal career.

The Mexican government under both former president Andrés Manuel López Obrador and President Claudia Sheinbaum has asserted that the U.S. government played a role in the capture of El Mayo.

U.S. authorities, including former U.S. Ambassador to Mexico Ken Salazar, denied that was the case, but in light of a journalist’s recent assertion that the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation had admitted involvement in the capture of Zambada, Mexican authorities believe Salazar lied.

The kidnapping of El Mayo triggered a major escalation of a long-running feud between the “Los Mayos” and “Los Chapitos” factions of the Sinaloa Cartel. The former is led by Ismael “Mayito Flaco” Zambada, El Mayo’s son, while the latter is led by sons of El Chapo, namely Iván Archivaldo Guzmán Salazar and Jesús Alfredo Guzmán Salazar. Two other “Chapitos,” Joaquín and Ovidio, are in U.S. custody, as is another son of El Mayo, Vicente Zambada.

The battle between “Los Mayos and “Los Chapitos” has claimed well over 2,000 lives in Sinaloa since September 2024, while thousands more have disappeared in the troubled northern state in the same period.

El Mayo’s courtroom message: ‘There is no future in violence’

Before his life sentence was handed down, an apparently contrite Zambada, dressed in brown and orange prison garb, addressed the U.S. federal court and accepted responsibility for the crimes he committed during his lengthy criminal career.

CNN reported that he “apologized to the countless people and families harmed by his actions and said he wasn’t pleading guilty to hide what he had done, but because he knew it was wrong.”

“He urged young people not to follow his path,” CNN reported, noting that Zambada said:

“Choose a different path. There is no future in violence. It only leads to prison and death. Violence must end in Mexico and elsewhere. Too many lives are being lost. No one wins.”

Asked about those remarks at her Tuesday morning press conference, President Sheinbaum indicated that she agreed with them before highlighting the government’s efforts to address the root causes of crime. However, she declined to explicitly endorse Zambada’s message given that it came from a convicted drug trafficker and leader of one of Mexico’s most powerful criminal organizations.

DOJ: Sinaloa Cartel ‘regularly used brutal violence’ under El Mayo’s leadership

In its statement, the DOJ said that Zambada’s “rise to power began with the [Sinaloa] Cartel’s inception and ended with his arrest in July 2024.”

“Previously known as the Mexican Federation, the Cartel is a drug trafficking organization based in Sinaloa, Mexico, that since approximately the late 1980s has imported lethal quantities of narcotics – including, among others, cocaine, heroin, methamphetamine, and fentanyl – into the United States and laundered billions of dollars in drug proceeds back to Mexico,” the DOJ said.

The Justice Department said that under Zambada’s leadership, the Sinaloa Cartel “recently branched out into the production and trafficking of fentanyl, including by purchasing fentanyl precursor chemicals from Chinese companies and producing many thousands of kilograms of fentanyl in laboratories both in rural areas and major cities in Mexico for distribution in the United States.”

“… Zambada García has devoted his efforts over decades to growing, increasing, and enhancing the power of the Cartel, and to growing his individual power and position in the Cartel after his partner El Chapo was captured in 2016. Under Zambada García’s leadership, the Cartel regularly used brutal violence, intimidation, and murder to silence potential witnesses and dissuade law enforcement from performing its duties,” the DOJ said.

The Justice Department said that Zambada “has operated with impunity at the highest levels of the Mexican drug trafficking world while being assured of his continued success and safety from arrest through his payment of bribes to Mexican government officials and law enforcement officers.”

“He controlled those corrupt officials and officers who protected his workers and drug shipments as his drugs were transported across Mexico and into the United States,” the DOJ said.

“Numerous witnesses have testified, including at the trials of El Chapo and corrupt former Mexican Secretary of Public Security Genaro García Luna, that corruption at all levels was necessary to allow the Zambada Garcia’s criminal enterprise to function so effectively at such a large scale.”

Joseph Nocella Jr., U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of New York, said that Zambada “spent nearly four decades poisoning American communities to make billions of dollars in profit and ordering the murders of anyone who stood in his way.”

“He will spend the rest of his life in a U.S. prison, exactly where he belongs,” Nocella said.

The Sinaloa Cartel Zambada formerly led is one of eight Mexican criminal organizations that have been designated as foreign terrorist organizations by the U.S. government.

With reports from CNN, The Wall Street Journal and La Jornada

World.title: Health Ministry gives progress report on US $10B hospitals investment: Tuesday’s mañanera recapped
World.content:
Sheinbaum’s mañanera in 60 seconds

🏥 Healthcare update takes center stage: Mexico’s Deputy Health Minister Eduardo Clark returned to the mañanera two months after unveiling his ministry’s plan to add over 9,000 public hospital beds during the government’s six-year term, this time with a progress report on the 181-billion-peso (US $10.4 billion) investment.

Mexico’s Deputy Health Minister Eduardo Clark returned to the two months after unveiling his ministry’s plan to add over 9,000 public hospital beds during the government’s six-year term, this time with a progress report on the 181-billion-peso (US $10.4 billion) investment. 🛠️ 30 hospital projects already completed: Clark said 1,474 beds have been added since October 2024 across seven IMSS, 19 IMSS Bienestar and four ISSSTE hospitals, through new builds, replacements and expansions.

Clark said 1,474 beds have been added since October 2024 across seven IMSS, 19 IMSS Bienestar and four ISSSTE hospitals, through new builds, replacements and expansions. 📅 33 more projects due this year across Mexico: Another 1,163 beds are set to be added in 2026, six from new hospital construction and 27 from replacements or expansions, with Clark stressing investments are underway “in all the federal entities.”

Another 1,163 beds are set to be added in 2026, six from new hospital construction and 27 from replacements or expansions, with Clark stressing investments are underway “in all the federal entities.” ⚖️ No personal opinion on El Mayo’s life sentence: Asked about Ismael “El Mayo” Zambada’s life sentence handed down in Brooklyn, Sheinbaum said she had “no personal opinion about that.”

Asked about Ismael “El Mayo” Zambada’s life sentence handed down in Brooklyn, Sheinbaum said she had “no personal opinion about that.” ☮️ Sheinbaum agrees with Zambada’s anti-crime message: On Zambada’s courtroom message urging young people to avoid crime, Sheinbaum indicated she agreed, although she declined to explicitly endorse his words. The president spoke about her government’s efforts to address the root causes of crime.

On Zambada’s courtroom message urging young people to avoid crime, Sheinbaum indicated she agreed, although she declined to explicitly endorse his words. The president spoke about her government’s efforts to address the root causes of crime. 🥬 Government says Mexican lettuce not the source of US Cyclosporiasis outbreak: Sheinbaum said a suspected link between the U.S. cyclosporiasis outbreak and Guanajuato lettuce had been ruled out, and Health Minister Kershenobich confirmed just three “ordinary” cases in Mexico.

Why today’s mañanera matters

Two months after announcing that the federal government is aiming to increase the number of public hospital beds in Mexico by more than 9,000 during its six-year term (October 2024 to September 2030), Deputy Health Minister Eduardo Clark returned to the mañanera to provide an update on the 181-billion-peso (US $10.4 billion initiative).

Federal officials have highlighted that the “fourth transformation” (4T) administrations led by ex-President Andrés Manuel López Obrador (AMLO) and President Claudia Sheinbaum added — and are adding — significantly more beds to public hospitals than governments during the so-called “neoliberal period” between 1982 and 2018. Sheinbaum reiterated that point on Tuesday morning.

Today’s mañanera was also significant as the president indicated that she agreed with a message Sinaloa Cartel kingpin Ismael “El Mayo” Zambada conveyed in U.S. court on Monday before he was sentenced to life imprisonment.

In addition, Health Minister David Kershenobich spoke about the presence in Mexico of cyclosporiasis, the intestinal illness that has recently sickened thousands of people in the United States.

33 hospital projects scheduled for completion in 2026

Deputy Minister Clark told reporters that 30 public hospital projects have been completed since the current government took office in October 2024. Those projects include the construction of new hospitals and the “replacement” and expansion of existing ones.

Clark said that the 30 projects added 1,474 beds across seven IMMS hospitals, 19 IMSS Bienestar hospitals and four ISSSTE hospitals.

The deputy minister said that 33 additional hospital projects are slated for completion this year. Those projects, Clark said, will add 1,163 beds to IMMS, IMSS Bienestar and ISSSTE hospitals.

Six of the 33 projects entail the construction of new hospitals. The other 27 projects are hospital replacements or expansions.

Clark stressed that hospital projects have been completed, and are being completed, across the entire country.

“In all the federal entities, we have hospital projects,” he said.

Sheinbaum says she has no ‘personal opinion’ about El Mayo’s life sentence

A reporter asked the president her opinion about Zambada’s life imprisonment sentence, handed down by Judge Brian Cogan in a U.S. federal court in Brooklyn, New York.

“There is no personal opinion about that,” Sheinbaum said. “It is what it is.”

The reporter noted that Zambada, in court, urged young people to steer clear of a life of crime.

Asked to offer her opinion about that advice, Sheinbaum said that “obviously coming from who it comes, it is difficult to quote him.”

“But, that’s the work we’re doing, … it’s attention to the [root] causes [of crime],” she said, referring to the government strategy of providing increased work and education opportunities to young people as a way to discourage them from joining criminal groups.

The attention to the root causes of crime via the provision of educational scholarships, employment programs and welfare schemes is essentially the “hugs” aspects of the so-called “hugs, not bullets” (abrazos, no balazos) security strategy implemented by AMLO’s government.

Attention to the root causes of crime is one of the four core tenets of the Sheinbaum administration’s security strategy. Compared to the López Obrador administration, the current government has been more proactive in combating organized crime, an approach that has resulted in the arrest of almost 60,000 alleged perpetrators of serious crimes since Sheinbaum took office.

Health minister: 3 cyclosporiasis cases in Mexico

Asked whether it was true that the outbreak of cyclosporiasis in the United States was linked to lettuce from Guanajuato, Sheinbaum said that hypothesis had been ruled out.

Health Minister Kershenobich subsequently said that only three cases of cyclosporiasis had recently been detected in Mexico.

“Those cases are usual. In other words, they are not beyond ordinary epidemiology,” he said.

“Therefore, we don’t have an outbreak of cyclosporiasis,” Kershenobich said.

“In relation to the lettuce plant in Guanajuato, … a sample was taken that returned positive [for the parasite Cyclospora cayetanensis], but the [U.S.] Food and Drug Administration retracted, saying it was a false positive,” he said.

Kershenobich said that Mexican authorities have also taken lettuce samples from Guanajuato as part of their own investigation. To date, he said, there is no evidence that the cyclosporiasis outbreak in the U.S. stems from lettuce grown in Guanajuato.

By Mexico News Daily chief staff writer Peter Davies (peter.davies@mexiconewsdaily.com)

World.title: Mexico’s hosting of World Cup wins praise all around
World.content:
During the FIFA men’s World Cup final in New Jersey on Sunday, U.S. President Donald Trump, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Spanish King Felipe VI praised Mexico as a host of the quadrennial soccer tournament and spoke glowingly about the Mexican team, according to President Claudia Sheinbaum.

Sheinbaum, who attended the match between Spain and Argentina at MetLife Stadium near New York City after receiving an invitation from Trump, said that everyone she had the opportunity to speak to at the final, “from President Trump to [Prime] Minister Carney to the King of Spain,” spoke “wonders of la selección nacional.”

The Mexican World Cup team won all three of its group stage matches, and its round of 32 clash against Ecuador, before losing 3-2 to England in a pulsating, nail-biting round of 16 game in Mexico City. El Tri’s four victories sparked jubilant — and very large — celebrations in Mexican towns and cities, especially the capital.

Sheinbaum said that world leaders and other officials she interacted with on Sunday — among whom were also Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, First Lady Melania Trump and FIFA President Gianni Infantino — also spoke wonders of Mexico as a co-host of the World Cup along with the United States, where the majority of the tournament’s 104 matches were played, and Canada.

“[They spoke about] how well Mexico did hosting the World Cup. Everyone was congratulating the fans [in Mexico],” she said, adding that her interlocutors at MetLife Stadium also mentioned “the happiness” with which the World Cup in Mexico was experienced.

Sheinbaum — who has asserted that Mexico had the best World Cup atmosphere of the three co-hosts — also said that Trump, Carney, King Felipe and others spoke about the warm way in which Mexico welcomed World Cup teams and tourists.

South Africa, Spain, Uruguay, Czechia, South Korea, Japan, Colombia, the Netherlands, Morocco, England and Sweden were among the teams that played matches in Mexico during the June 11-July 19 tournament. Another team, Iran, set up its base camp in Tijuana even though it played its three World Cup matches in the United States. The Iranian team received a very warm welcome from Tijuana locals. For his part, King Felipe watched Spain take on Uruguay in Guadalajara after meeting with Sheinbaum at the National Palace in Mexico City on June 25.

Sheinbaum reiterated at her Monday press conference that “everyone” at the stadium on Sunday congratulated her on the job Mexico did hosting the World Cup and spoke about “how well the Mexican team played.”

The president watched Spain defeat Argentina 1-0 in extra time from a glass-fronted stadium box filled with dignitaries. Mexican Foreign Minister Roberto Velasco attended the final with Sheinbaum, who presented the Golden Ball award to Spanish captain Rodri (Rodrigo Hernández), who was deemed the best player of the 2026 World Cup.

FIFA official: Mexico ‘was ready’ to host the World Cup; Mexican security team did an ‘excellent job’

Rodrigo Martínez-Celis, FIFA’s executive director for safety and security in Mexico, told the news agency EFE earlier this month that Mexico had “more than proven” that it was ready to host the World Cup despite a “narrative” of insecurity.

Before and during the tournament, Sheinbaum maintained that security in Mexico during the World Cup was guaranteed, and asserted that there was “no risk” for tourists who came to the country to attend matches in Mexico City, Guadalajara and Monterrey.
