World.title: Hungary's OTP Bank to buy Luminor
World.content:
OTP Bank has signed an agreement to acquire Luminor, the third-largest banking group in the Baltic region, as it looks to expand its presence in the region.

OTP Group is a leading banking group in Central and Eastern Europe, serving 17.5 million customers across 11 countries. It has continued to operate in Russia after the start of the full-scale invasion and was temporarily sanctioned by Ukraine in 2023.

Luminor is the third-largest provider of financial services in the Baltic region. In 2025, the bank generated a net profit of €158 million.

On Monday, the OTP Group said in a statement that it had signed an agreement with a consortium of private equity funds managed by Blackstone and DNB Bank to buy Luminor.

Luminor in Tallinn. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

"The acquisition of Luminor is not merely a geographical expansion; it represents a strategic entry into a developed, stable region with significant growth potential," said Péter Csányi, chief executive officer of OTP Bank.

The company's goal is to strengthen Luminor's role in the Baltics and "contribute to the development of the region's financial system, lending activity and financial innovation."

Chief Executive Officer of Luminor Wojciech Sass said the deal will give the pan-Baltic bank the support of an experienced international banking group with a strong presence across Central and Eastern Europe.

Completion of the transaction is subject to obtaining the necessary regulatory approvals.

Luminor Bank AS was formed on October 1, 2017, when the merger of the Baltic units of DNB and Nordea was completed.

Expert: Other major banks also operate in Russia

Former Financial Supervision and Resolution Authority head Kilvar Kessler said there is nothing special about OTP continuing its activities in Russia, as many other European banks still operate in the country, such as Italy's UniCredit and Austria's Raiffeisenbank

Last year the bank's assets and gross customer loans in Russia grew by 40 percent and 56 percent respectively.

However, OTP's operations are overseen by both the European Central Bank and the Financial Supervision and Resolution Authority, both of which must approve the proposed merger.

Kilvar Kessler. Source: Siim Lõvi /ERR

"In the current circumstances it certainly has a particular context or flavour, but whether that should rule out OTP as Luminor's owner... Perhaps we need to look at what exactly its Russian business consists of and whether it could in any way negatively affect OTP as Luminor's owner," Kessler said on Tuesday's Vikerraadio's Uudis+ programme.

Speaking about foreign investment in Estonia and its decline, Kessler said he does not see anything particularly significant in Blackstone selling its stake.

"That fund was not created to hold and own a bank over the long term. Its role was precisely to build up Luminor and improve the quality of its loan portfolio – to strengthen the bank," Kessler noted, adding that this is Blackstone's business model.

In Kessler's opinion, OTP's acquisition could have a positive effect for customers in the region.

"I would predict that it will have a positive effect on banking competition in this region, and customers should only benefit from it," he said.

This story was updated to add comments from Kilvar Kessler.

World.title: Iraqi Airways launches new digital data center for automation push
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The management of Iraqi Airways has officially opened a new digital Data Center, marking a major step forward in its comprehensive digital transformation and electronic automation project.

Ahmed Abbas, Director of the Data Center, emphasized that the project builds upon the airline’s broader automation strategy. This plan aims to implement electronic systems across all company divisions and establish an integrated digital ecosystem.

By connecting all departments, branches, and operational units under a single, unified data center, the initiative will enhance information security, unify data management, boost operational efficiency, and ensure the sustainability of digital services.

Key Strategic Objectives

Core Digital Infrastructure: Serves as one of the airline’s most critical infrastructure upgrades, modernizing IT operations to align with global standards.

Accelerated Operations: Streamlines procedures, supports integrated electronic systems, and speeds up daily operational workflows.

Enhanced Service Quality: Leverages modern technology to elevate overall service standards and customer experiences.

Government Alignment: Fulfills national e-governance mandates and Council of Ministers decisions regarding digital transformation and infrastructure development.

By launching this centralized Data Center, Iraqi Airways continues to modernize its civil aviation infrastructure, bringing faster processing, improved security, and higher-quality digital services to both internal operations and passengers.

World.title: E-payment firms to assist CBI in driving Iraq’s digital transition
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Governor of the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) Nizar Hussein met on Tuesday with representatives of licensed electronic payment companies to enhance their role in supporting the country’s digital transformation.

The meeting addressed the role of e-payment firms in carrying out the CBI’s strategy to develop the electronic payments system and enhance financial inclusion.

Hussein noted that in the next term, electronic payment firms must improve the services provided to customers while adhering to the highest quality standards.

The step will boost public trust in electronic payment systems, foster the development of new digital payment solutions, reduce dependency on cash, and develop the digital economy, according to a statement released by the CBI.

Hussein urged electronic payment firms to adhere to international standards governing international financial transactions to open up more chances for sector development, boost card limitations, and introduce new financial services that match residents’ requirements.

The meeting addressed procedures that the CBI would adopt with electronic payment firms to eliminate card misuse, improve the security of the payment system, boost operational limitations, and offer advanced services to residents.

Hussein also called for increasing collaborations with CBI-licensed banks to achieve financial sector integration and develop a modern, secure, and innovative payment system.

World.title: Indian Oil Corp stops loading Iraqi oil amid Hormuz instability
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Sources told Reuters that Indian Oil Corp. (IOC) has stopped loading Iraqi oil from Basrah Oil Terminal due to increasing risk and assaults on vessels crossing the Strait of Hormuz.

Around July 23, the state-run IOC planned to transport 2 million barrels of Iraqi oil via the mega-sized crude carrier Lila Jamnagar.

Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Ltd, a different state refiner, has also halted plans to transport oil from Iraq via the Indian-flagged Aframax tanker Desh Gaurav.

Following the resumption of military operations in the Strait of Hormuz, India has advised shipping companies to refrain from assigning Indian seafarers to vessels operating in that region.

Ship captains were also advised to be cautious regarding security in the Arabian Gulf, the Strait of Hormuz, and surrounding waterways and to continuously check navigational warnings.

Prior to the war, the Strait of Hormuz between Iran and Oman served as the primary transit route for around a fifth of the world’s oil and gas supplies.

Tensions have escalated since the truce between Washington and Tehran was broken in early July. This breakdown has resulted in attacks that have disrupted trade through the crucial waterway.

World.title: Turkish Transport Minister arrives in baghdad to elevate transport ties and Development Road cooperation
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Turkish Minister of Transport and Infrastructure Abdulkadir Uraloğlu arrived in Baghdad on Tuesday, July 21, 2026, to conduct high-level talks with Iraqi officials aimed at taking bilateral cooperation in transport, logistics, and telecommunications to a higher level.

Minister Uraloğlu was officially welcomed at Baghdad International Airport by Deputy Minister of Transport Hazem Razi Lafta, before holding bilateral talks with Iraqi Minister of Transport Wahb Al-Hasani at the state guesthouse in Baghdad.

Strategic Focus: The Development Road Project Primary Agenda: Fast-tracking execution phases of the multi-billion-dollar Development Road project, an international rail and highway network linking Grand Faw Port in southern Iraq directly to Turkey and European commercial markets.

Diplomatic Context: The visit serves as a key logistical precursor ahead of Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi’s upcoming official state visit to Turkey scheduled for July 28, 2026.

The visit underscores the massive economic weight and trade synergy between the two neighboring nations:

Heavy Commercial Volume: Bilateral trade volume between Iraq and Turkey stands at approximately $15 billion to $17 billion annually, with joint diplomatic initiatives aiming to expand total trade to $24 billion.

Key Trading Partner: Iraq consistently ranks among Turkey’s top export destinations globally (exceeding $12 billion in Turkish exports alone), primarily spanning food products, construction materials, machinery, and consumer goods.

Infrastructure Footprint: Turkish construction firms have historically undertaken over 1,100 development projects in Iraq valued at more than $36 billion, making Iraq one of the largest markets for Turkish engineering and infrastructure expertise worldwide.

By coordinating transport routes and cross-border digital networks through the Development Road project, both Baghdad and Ankara aim to secure long-term transit revenue, streamline regional supply chains, and further integrate their high-volume trade partnership.

World.title: National Security Service foils clandestine drone manufacturing cell in Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq’s National Security Service (NSS) announced on Tuesday, July 21, 2026, the successful disruption of a clandestine operation attempting to manufacture unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) inside the capital city of Baghdad.

Executed under the direct supervision of the Judge of the Third Investigative Court, the intelligence-led raid resulted in the arrest of three primary suspects and the seizure of a makeshift production facility.

In an official statement and accompanied by video documentation of the tactical operation, the NSS confirmed that its specialized intelligence units executed judicial arrest and search warrants following precise surveillance.

The security sweep uncovered an active workshop equipped with 25 prefabricated drone airframes, along with specialized carbon fiber sheets, custom molds, and technical assembly tools utilized in the production and fabrication of long-range drones.

Seizure Inventory & Intelligence Breakdown

Arrests: 3 primary suspects apprehended under judicial warrants issued by the Third Investigative Court.

Drone Airframes: 25 completed and semi-completed UAV structural fuselages.

Manufacturing Materials: Industrial-grade carbon fiber panels, custom molds, and precision technical tooling.

Status: Disrupted prior to final assembly and operational deployment.

Ongoing Probe: Investigations are actively expanding to determine potential linkages between the illicit workshop, regional factional networks, or broader national security threats.

The NSS emphasized that the covert operation was completely dismantled before the manufactured drones could reach operational completion or be integrated into regional flight networks.

Legal proceedings have been initiated, and the suspects remain in federal custody as investigators work to identify supply chains and potential organizational ties before referring the perpetrators to the judiciary.

World.title: Iraq receives second batch of equipment for Nasiriyah International Airport
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq has received a second shipment of ground support equipment for Nasiriyah International Airport as building progresses, bringing the long-awaited facility closer to becoming operational.

The Ministry of Transport stated that the equipment arrived following an initial delivery in June and is part of the airport’s ongoing preparations for its opening.

Airport Director Ali Al-Ghurabi stated that the latest shipment includes commercial vehicles and operational equipment required to support aircraft and passenger services once the airport is operational.

The equipment will offer the necessary ground handling and technical support capabilities for international airport operations, assisting in the facility’s preparation for commercial flights, he added.

The airport is one of several transportation infrastructure projects being developed by Iraq as the government seeks to modernize its aviation sector, improve regional connectivity, and spur economic development beyond the country’s oil industry.

Baghdad has increased investment in airports, ports, and trains as part of a larger goal to improve transportation linkages, boost commerce and tourism, and establish Iraq as a regional logistical center linking the Gulf to Europe and Asia.

World.title: Washington approves Iraqi proposal to mediate between US and Iran
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – US President Donald Trump has approved Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s proposal to mediate between the United States and Iran.

This diplomatic breakthrough is intended to diffuse the current crisis in the Strait of Hormuz, according to local news outlet Channel 8 News.

During their recent meeting in Washington, al-Zaidi asked Trump for approval to establish an official Iraqi mediation effort between the United States and Iran.

Trump authorized al-Zaidi to undertake the plan as part of attempts to address the continuing Strait of Hormuz issue.

According to insiders, the mediation would focus on restoring stability to marine shipping and energy flows across the key canal.

Al-Zaidi informed Trump that, while Pakistan has been involved in political and diplomatic discussions, Iraq plans to lead the economic track of mediation.

The Iraqi effort will look for answers to interruptions in commercial shipping and oil shipments via the Strait of Hormuz, which have led to a broader global energy and economic crisis.

According to reports, al-Zaidi plans to visit Tehran on Thursday for a series of high-level talks. He and the accompanying Iraqi officials are anticipated to return to Baghdad later that day.

World.title: Iraq receives Chinese-built ferries for Arab Gulf routes
World.content:
Basra (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq has received a fleet of Chinese-built passenger boats and ferries to be deployed on new maritime routes connecting the country to Arab Gulf states, as part of Baghdad’s efforts to modernize its transportation network and strengthen regional connectivity.

According to Iraq’s Ministry of Transport, the fleet consists of 15 tourist boats, two passenger ferries capable of transporting 200 people each, and a bigger multi-purpose ferry that can transport 500 passengers and 80 vehicles every journey.

The warships will run maritime routes between Iraq and Arab Gulf nations, simplifying passenger travel while promoting commerce and tourism, according to the government.

The acquisition is part of Iraq’s overall strategy to modernize its maritime transport infrastructure and diversify its economy by expanding regional transportation links beyond its road and air networks.

According to the ministry, the new fleet would boost passenger and vehicle capacity while offering safer and more effective transportation services as regional travel demand increases.

The investment comes after Iraq announced several transportation projects, including the near completion of a new marina on the Shatt al-Arab waterway and continued development of the Grand Faw Port, as Baghdad seeks to strengthen its position as a regional transportation and logistics hub.

World.title: Health minister JP Nadda, MoS Jitendra Singh meet Sonam Wangchuk at Medanta Hospital: Report
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Union minister Jagat Prakash Nadda, minister of state for the Prime Minister's office Dr Jitendra Singh went to Medanta Hospital in

and met Activist

to enquire about his health, as per PTI sources.

This came after the Delhi high court on Tuesday ordered the immediate transfer of scientist and activist Sonam Wangchuk from Safdarjung Hospital to Medanta Hospital in Gurugram amid his prolonged hunger strike over the alleged NEET paper leak.

The division bench directed that Wangchuk be treated by doctors at Medanta as per established medical protocol and said he must follow the medical advice of the treating team after his transfer.

The order came after Wangchuk's wife, Gitanjali Angmo, challenged a single judge's decision refusing permission to shift him from Safdarjung Hospital.

During the hearing, the Centre informed the high court that it had "no objection" to Wangchuk being shifted to Medanta Hospital. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, however, urged that Wangchuk "remain under continuous medical supervision" and "not be discharged except on the advice of Medanta's doctors."





Wangchuk entered the 24th day of his hunger strike on Tuesday as the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) stepped up its protest against the Centre over the alleged NEET paper leak and renewed its demand for Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation. Protesters also continued their sit-in at Delhi's Jantar Mantar.

World.title: 'We owe students more than outrage': Education minister Pradhan slams Cong protest
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Union education minister

on Tuesday accused leader of opposition in Lok Sabha

and Congress of "shamelessly exploiting students as political tools" following the grand-old-party's protest outside Prime Minister Narendra Modi's residence over the NEET paper leak.

In a social media post on X, Pradhan said Congress chose to stage a dharna outside PM Modi's residence, causing inconvenience to the public and disregarding established security protocols.

"LoP Shri Rahul Gandhi and Congress continue to shamelessly exploit students as political tools to manufacture disruption during the

," the education minister said.

"Shri Rahul Gandhi and Congress chose to stage a dharna outside the Hon'ble Prime Minister's residence, causing inconvenience to the public and disregarding established security protocols," he added.

Further, Pradhan said Congress "chose spectacle over democratic debate" despite the government conveying its readiness for a comprehensive discussion on the NEET paper leak issue.

"Even after the government conveyed its readiness for a comprehensive discussion, the Congress chose political spectacle over democratic debate. Their objective was never solutions for students; it was disruption for political headlines," he said.





"For Rahul Gandhi, this is not about students. This is about manufacturing confrontation after every genuine avenue for discussion has been opened," he added.

Pradhan said the government owes students answers, reforms and accountability rather than outrage.

"Our government remains 100% committed to discussing NEET and addressing every genuine concern of our youth on the floor of the House. The students of India deserve far better than being treated as props in a political campaign. They deserve certainty over chaos, solutions over slogans and responsibility over disruption," the education minister said.

"We owe our students more than outrage. We owe them answers, reforms and accountability. That is exactly what our government remains committed to delivering," he added.

World.title: Rahul dragged, Priyanka clings to bus door: Five pictures that defined Congress protest outside PM Modi's residence
World.content:
Rahul Gandhi being taken away by police

NEW DELHI: High drama unfolded outside Prime Minister Narendra Modi's residence in Delhi on Tuesday as the Congress, led by Rahul Gandhi, arrived to stage a sit-in protest, catching security personnel off guard.The Congress leaders demanded the resignation of PM Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah, and education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.Rahul Gandhi also appealed to the public to join what was planned as an indefinite protest, following which leaders from other opposition parties joined the demonstration.Congress leaders tied plastic bands around their hands and raised slogans, protesting the government's action.The government sent Union minister Jitendra Singh and home secretary Govind Mohan to urge Rahul Gandhi and the Congress to call off the protest, citing the high-security nature of the area. However, the request was rejected.Singh claimed that he informed Rahul Gandhi that the government had agreed to discuss the NEET paper leak issue in Parliament, following which the Congress MP "changed the goalpost" and demanded the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan.Eventually, Delhi Police detained Rahul Gandhi and other leaders participating in the protest.The Congress claimed that Rahul Gandhi sustained a nose injury while in Delhi Police custody.Meanwhile, party MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra attempted to resist her detention by clinging to the door of a bus in which protesters were being taken away.The dramatic protest came a day after Delhi Police and other security forces stopped a march by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) to Parliament, with protesters demanding the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET (UG) paper leak.The CJP march, held on the first day of the Monsoon Session of Parliament, turned violent, leaving both protesters and security personnel injured.

World.title: The sudden dharna: How Congress surprised its own MPs, govt with protest outside PM's residence
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Chaos erupted in the heart of New Delhi after several Congress leaders, including

,

and

, marched to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's residence at Lok Kalyan Marg and staged a protest against the alleged brutality committed against students during the Cockroach Janata Party's march to Parliament.

During the protest, Congress leaders tied plastic bands around their hands and raised slogans, demanding the resignation of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET paper leak.

However, the protest came as much of a surprise to many Congress leaders as it did to the government.

How Congress chalked out the protest plan

According to news agency PTI, the Congress leadership did not tell its leaders about the protest to maintain secrecy, as otherwise the area could have been blockaded.

MPs were told that they needed to reach party president Mallikarjun Kharge's residence -- 10 Rajaji Marg -- to wish him on his birthday, PTI reported, citing party sources.

Therefore, many MPs were oblivious to what was coming and reached Kharge's residence. They were then asked to follow Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra as the top leaders suddenly moved towards the gate of 7, Lok Kalyan Marg, which is about 500 metres from Kharge's house.





Other party leaders also had no clue about the development, and they reached the spot as soon as word spread.

Only the top leaders were aware of the move, and they reached Kharge's residence after both Houses of Parliament were adjourned. Most MPs, however, had no clue about the plan.

The surprise sit-in by the Congress top brass in the high-security zone sent the government into a tizzy, prompting it to rush minister of state in the PMO Jitendra Singh, along with Union home secretary Govind Mohan, to persuade the leaders of the opposition to vacate the sensitive site.

After meeting Rahul, Jitendra Singh accused him of shifting his demands during the talks.

Speaking to news agency ANI, Singh said he and Union home secretary Govind Mohan were deputed by the government to meet senior Congress leaders after they began a sit-in protest at a location that, according to him, was not designated for demonstrations and was causing inconvenience to the public.

"It was learned that Congress Party national president Mallikarjun Kharge and other senior leaders like Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi and others had suddenly started a protest.

It was also reported that the place was not very conducive to a sit-in protest. It was causing significant inconvenience to the public," he said.

The minister said the government sent the two officials to persuade the Congress leaders to shift the discussion to Parliament instead of continuing the protest.

Later, Rahul , Priyanka , along with Samajwadi Party leader Akhilesh Yadav, were forcibly removed by the police and taken to police stations at Mandir Marg and Chhatrasal Stadium. All the leaders were later released.

World.title: 'Monsoon Session will be washed out': Congress warns Centre over NEET leak, police action on youth protesters
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Congress on Tuesday warned that the ongoing

could be a "washout" if the government continued to refuse discussions on the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak and the police action against youth protesters who attempted to march to Parliament a day earlier.

Congress MP Jairam Ramesh's remarks came after

detained opposition leaders who joined a surprise protest led by the Congress outside Prime Minister Narendra Modi's residence.

He added that Union home minister Amit Shah, under whose ministry the Delhi Police functions, must make a statement on the police action against protesters."

"Our demand has been, and will continue to be, that the home minister makes a statement and that there is a detailed discussion regarding the education system, the examination system, and the atrocities committed against students by the Delhi Police yesterday.

Furthermore, we demand the resignation of the education minister (Dharmendra Pradhan)... However, I do not see that happening. If the government maintains this mindset, then the Parliament session will definitely be washed out," the Rajya Sabha MP told ANI.

Ramesh further stated that the united stand by opposition parties reflected growing concern over the handling of the examination controversy and the alleged police excesses against students.





"Opposition unity and solidarity were displayed in a very powerful and impactful manner," he added.

Earlier, Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and several other Congress leaders were detained by Delhi Police during a protest near Prime Minister Narendra Modi's official residence at Lok Kalyan Marg.

The Congress had marched from Rajaji Marg, demanding accountability over the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak, action over the alleged police crackdown on student protesters, and the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.

Several party leaders and workers were detained as police dispersed the demonstrators.

The protest came a day after clashes between Delhi Police and demonstrators during a march to Parliament over the paper leak, an incident that has sparked a political row and led to repeated disruptions in both Houses of Parliament.

The Monsoon Session of Parliament began on July 20 and is scheduled to conclude on August 13.

World.title: Kalyan Banerjee exits TMC's Martyr's day rally after reported spat with Mamata
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

MP Kalyan Banerjee on Tuesday reportedly left the party's Martyrs' Day rally in Kolkata after a verbal exchange with party supremo

.

According to a report by news agency PTI, Mamata was upset with Kalyan over exceeding his allotted speaking time at the rally, where he spoke for around 23 minutes.

Party sources told PTI that the list of speakers at the rally near the Birla Planetarium was unusually long, and all leaders had been instructed to keep their speeches brief so that everyone could be accommodated.

Kalyan Banerjee, however, continued speaking for nearly 23 minutes, launching a blistering attack on the

as well as the breakaway Trinamool faction led by Leader of Opposition Ritabrata Banerjee.

"Mamata Banerjee alone is the Trinamool. The BJP-backed stage has been set up there, but the workers are not with them.

Those BJP-sponsored MLAs dreaming of taking over are only digging their own grave," he said.

Sources present on the dais claimed that Mamata, who arrived on the stage while Kalyan Banerjee was addressing the gathering, gestured to him to wrap up his speech. When he continued, senior party leader Kunal Ghosh also intervened, they said.

After the speech ended, Mamata Banerjee allegedly expressed her displeasure over the delay, leading to a brief exchange of words before the MP walked off the stage and headed straight to his Kalighat residence without waiting for the speeches of party national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee or the TMC chief.





Sources in the Mamata camp said the delay forced the organisers to drop several scheduled speakers from the programme, including Lok Sabha MPs Mahua Moitra and Kirti Azad, Rajya Sabha MPs Dola Sen and Sagarika Ghose, and Rajeev Kumar.

Kalyan Banerjee, however, rejected reports of any spat with Mamata Banerjee.

"I left after my speech as I had other engagements. There was no altercation. Had there been one, would I have gone to the front of the stage and addressed the gathering the way I did?" he said.

The Trinamool Congress did not issue any official statement on the reported episode.

The development assumes political significance as Kalyan Banerjee is among the few senior leaders who have remained steadfastly with Mamata Banerjee after the Trinamool split following the BJP's victory in the 2026 West Bengal Assembly elections.

Recently, he publicly criticised Abhishek Banerjee during a dispute over legal representation in a Calcutta High Court case, saying Mamata Banerjee would have to decide "who would remain in the party -- Abhishek or me".

The differences were subsequently resolved, with both leaders publicly expressing mutual respect.

World.title: 'TVK covering up misrule, public will teach befitting lesson': Stalin slams CM Vijay over DMK MLA's arrest
World.content:
NEW DELHI: DMK supremo MK Stalin on Tuesday hit out at Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay over the arrest of a party MLA, warning that the people would teach the ruling TVK a "befitting lesson" if it tried to "cover up its misrule" through arrests.

"If this government thinks it can cover up its misrule with arrests, the people themselves will teach a fitting lesson to such arrogance," Stalin, Vijay's predecessor as chief minister, said in an X post.

He referred to an editorial in an English daily that criticised the TVK-led Tamil Nadu government for initiating criminal proceedings over political criticism.

Stalin's remarks came amid an escalating confrontation between the ruling TVK and the principal opposition DMK.

On Monday, DMK MLA GV Markandeyan was arrested over his purported "we will crush your bones" remark allegedly directed at chief minister Vijay.

After several hours of questioning, Markandeyan was produced before a local court, which remanded him to judicial custody.

Stalin condemned the police action, describing it as an attempt to criminalise "political criticism", and warned of consequences.

TVK, launched by Vijay in February 2024, emerged as the single-largest party in the Tamil Nadu assembly elections in April and later formed the government with the support of the Congress, VCK, IUML, and the Left parties.

Vijay, an actor-turned-politician, succeeded Stalin as chief minister after the DMK government was voted out following a single term in office.

(With PTI inputs)

World.title: Gold ornaments, bronze objects stolen from temple
World.content:
Burglars decamped with gold ornaments and bronze objects worth around ₹10 lakh from a local Siva temple in Vannivedu village near Walajah town in Ranipet on Tuesday.

The police said that it was around 8 a.m when temple priest K. Manoj, 53, a resident of Walajah, opened the main entrance of the temple and found the locks damaged.

Initial inquiry revealed that Manoj went inside the temple premises and found a lock of sanctum sanctorum where the main deity was placed. Gold ornaments, bronze objects, and cash from hundis were stolen. On being informed, Walajah police inspected the spot. Fingerprint experts and sniffer dogs were also roped in to take clues from the spot.

Instances of theft had occurred in the premises more than 40 times in the past two decades. The police said that the isolated location of the temple and lack of security measures including CCTV cameras in the temple could have been reasons for the theft. A probe is under way.

World.title: Around 1.75 tonnes of red sanders stolen from sandalwood depot
World.content:
Unidentified persons have stolen around 1.75 tonnes of red sanders that is worth around ₹50 lakh at the Government Sandalwood Depot in Tirupattur town on Tuesday.

Forest officials said that it was during a routine inspection of stocks of wooden logs in the depot on July 18 that a team of forest officials found that 1.75 tonnes of red sanders were missing in one of the storehouses at the depot, which usually had around 100 tonnes of seized red sanders for many years.

Forest officials said that stocks at the government depot were mostly sandalwood and red sanders that were seized from smugglers during surprise checks in areas along Tamil Nadu - Andhra Pradesh border. The seized logs were used to make incense sticks.

Forest officials said that based on a complaint by Jothi Lingam who was in charge of the depot, a case was registered by Tirupattur Town police. A probe is under way.

World.title: Two persons held for feeding gutka to baby
World.content:
Two commuters were arrested by Government Railway Police (GRP) at Jolarpet railway station in Tirupattur on Tuesday for reportedly feeding gutka to a baby.

The police said the arrested persons were identified as B. Sivakumar, 57, and Puthagunda Reddy, 38. They are residents of Kadapa in Andhra Pradesh. Initial inquiry revealed that the duo was travelling in an express train towards Bengaluru from Chennai when a fellow passenger R. Murali, 39, a resident of Jolarpet, saw Sivakumar allegedly feeding a small quantity of gutka to a one-year-old baby in the train.

The police said that the baby belongs to V. Raj Khan, 28, and Harina, 26, a native of West Bengal. The couple was working as wage labourers in Kerala. They were on their way to Karnataka to meet relatives. The couple was sleeping when the incident took place.

The police said an argument broke out between Murali and the duo in the train. A video of the incident, including that of the child being fed gutka surfaced on social media, inviting public outcry. The police said that Murali sought help from the child helpline. A case was registered at Jolarpet railway station. Arrested persons were lodged at sub-jail in Tirupattur town. The affected baby was treated at Government Taluk Hospital in Tirupattur town where doctors said the child is stable. A probe is under way.

World.title: Storage in Karnataka’s Cauvery reservoirs stands at 52% of total capacity as CWMA is set to review situation on July 22
World.content:
The Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA), which is the apex body that monitors implementation of Cauvery water release to lower riparian States as per the Supreme Court’s verdict, is meeting in Delhi on Wednesday to review the situation.

This meeting has assumed importance as it comes at a time when the catchment areas in Karnataka’s Cauvery basin are facing deficit rainfall. While the entire State is facing a rainfall deficit of about 35%, the Kodagu region that forms the biggest catchment area for the Cauvery besides being the point of origin for the river, has reported a shortage of 45%.

Rainfall deficit in Kodagu will have serious impact on the southern part of the State that depends on Cauvery water.

Cumulative storage

The cumulative storage in the four reservoirs in Karnataka’s Cauvery basin – Harangi, Hemavati, KRS and Kabini – accounts for just 52% of their full storage capacity as of now. Of this, the storage at KRS is particularly poor as it accounts for a mere 35% of its full capacity. The inflows too are poor as KRS reported inflows of 775 cusecs on July 21.

The Karnataka government has already declared that it would not release water for irrigation purposes and that whatever storage is there in the reservoirs has to be used only for drinking purposes.

The deficit rainfall resulting in poor storage has come in the way of adhering to the stipulated quota of release of Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu as per the Supreme Court’s directive. It is being said that only 3.4 tmcft of water has been released by Karnataka to Tamil Nadu from June 1 to July 19 as per the measurement at Biligundlu measuring gauge as against the stipulated quantum of 28.3 tmcft.

Speaking to The Hindu, Karnataka Water Resources Minister Ramalinga Reddy said, “In view of drought, we have decided to use the water stored in reservoirs of the Cauvery basin only for drinking water requirements.”

Southwest monsoon key

Meanwhile, weather experts are concerned over deficit rainfall under southwest monsoon in Karnataka. Pointing out that the southwest monsoon is the mainstay of the State’s weather system as it accounts for nearly 75% of the calendar year’s rainfall, they say that if the monsoon continues to be poort, the State would face a crisis.

The Karnataka Cabinet that met a few days ago under the chairmanship of Chief Minister D. K. Shivakumar has decided to submit a memorandum to the Centre in about 15 days seeking declaration of drought.

The Wednesday’s meeting of CWMA comes close on the heels of the meeting by the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee (CWRC) that took stock of the issue. In its earlier meeting held on June 23, the CWMA had directed the basin States to make judicious use of water available in reservoirs, particularly for drinking water needs.

World.title: Centenarian regains mobility after complex hip replacement surgery
World.content:
A 100-year-old woman has regained the ability to walk after undergoing a complex hip replacement surgery for a severe fracture sustained at the age of 99, underscoring the role of timely surgical intervention and multidisciplinary geriatric care in managing high-risk orthopaedic cases among elderly patients.

The surgery was performed at SPARSH Hospital, Yelahanka, where the patient from Jabalpur in Madhya Pradesh was admitted last year with a displaced left femoral neck fracture with a complex subtrochanteric extension, an unstable injury that is particularly difficult to treat in older adults. Her advanced age, coupled with a history of chronic bronchial asthma, placed her in the high-risk category for surgery.

According to the hospital, the orthopaedic team performed a long-stem, distal-fixing bipolar hemiarthroplasty, a procedure aimed at providing stable fixation by anchoring the implant deeper into the femur. Such an approach is often considered in patients with poor bone quality to facilitate early mobilisation and reduce complications associated with prolonged bed rest.

The patient had an uneventful post-operative recovery and was discharged three days after the surgery. She has since regained independent mobility after turning 100. Her milestone birthday was celebrated at the hospital on Tuesday (July 21), according to the hospital communique.

Venugopal N., senior consultant, Orthopaedics, SPARSH Hospital, said treating a complex hip fracture in a 99-year-old patient with chronic bronchial asthma required careful surgical planning because of compromised bone quality and the heightened risks associated with prolonged immobilisation. He said the choice of a long-stem, distal-fixing implant enabled early weight-bearing and contributed to the patient’s recovery.

Thirunavukkarasu Sivaraman, consultant lead, Department of Anaesthesiology and Pain Management, said a customised anaesthesia plan and specialised perioperative monitoring were adopted to manage the patient’s age-related risks and pre-existing medical condition during the surgery.

World.title: Applications invited for trustees in more temples
World.content:
The Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR&CE) Department has again called for applications from interested individuals for appointment as trustees in a total of 8,193 temples across the State. Recently, applications were called for non-hereditary trustees of 1,012 temples. The last date for submitting application form is on August 20, 2026.

Many people who did not make it last time are applying this time too. Existing trustees appointed by the previous government have resigned on their own or have been asked to step down though their two-year-long tenure may not be over as yet.

“I applied last time too. But somehow, I was not chosen. It was perhaps because the person who was chosen had political support. I have lived near this temple all my life and I have always wanted to do service there. I am part of an organisation that works around the temple. We have cleaned up the tank. I want to keep the mada streets clean,” said a person who is preparing his application form for a Perumal temple.

This time, apart from Aadhar cards and address proof, applicants have been asked to submit a no-objection certificate from the respective temple and a verification certificate from the police.

A resident of Tiruvallur, whose family has been associated with a Paadal Petra sthalam, said that he was definitely going to apply for the post of a trustee. “There is so much that needs to be done in the temple. The department is running it badly. Since it is treated as a sub-temple of another temple, officials don’t come here as often, they don’t have time for proper inspection of properties. A proper board of trustees interested in the development of the temple will do so much good for it,” he said.

Sources in the department said that district level committees were yet to be formed. “These committees will choose trustee for AC-level temples. For larger temples, the Commissioner will choose and for still larger ones, the government will take a call. Without the approval of the Board of Trustees, the monthly budget of the temples cannot be cleared. We cannot pay salaries of the staff even,” pointed out a source.

World.title: Karnataka High Court stays probe against man for tweet on Bantwal woman’s murder case
World.content:
Observing that “courts cannot permit criminality to be inferred by imagination when the words themselves refuse to yield such meaning”, the High Court of Karnataka has stayed investigation into two separate criminal cases registered against a man at two different police stations for a single tweet related to recent murder of a young woman at the Bantwal bus stand in Dakshina Kannada district.

Justice M. Nagaprasanna passed the interim order on petitions filed by 37-year-old Kiran, while observing that the language used in the tweet, prima facie, did not contain any explicit reference to a specific religion, community, or caste.

The petitioner, a resident of Bengaluru, was booked under Section 353(2) [publishing false information with an intent to create or promote... feelings of enmity, hatred or ill will between different religious, racial, language or regional groups or castes or communities] of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) in a case registered at Bantwal police station, and under Section 192 [wantonly giving provocation with intent to cause riot...] of the BNS in a case filed at the High Grounds Police Station in Bengaluru.

The tweet on X had stated: “Monster with wrist watch on his left hand, pants above his ankles, killed a girl at Bantwal bus stand, Karnataka. He probably knows that even if they arrest him, Congress will quietly withdraw the case. Be that as it may, just hope the RSS gets registered soon.”

The court pointed out that “it is only after an exercise of interpretation and inference, attempt is made to give it a communal colour.”

While the former sentence in the tweet, on its plain reading, does not reveal any exhortation against a religious or identifiable group; the latter “is a comment on the governmental action” of withdrawing criminal cases on which the High Court itself had made critical remarks earlier, Justice Nagaprasanna pointed out.

The court further said that “it is unable to discern, albeit, prima facie, from the language employed, any overt or tacit reference that unmistakably targets a particular community” while stating that it is a fit case, based on principles laid down by the apex court, to interdict the investigation against the petitioner.

World.title: Awareness, early diagnosis crucial for treating severe heart valve disease, say doctors
World.content:
Doctors at Sri Ramachandra Medical Centre (SRMC), on Tuesday, highlighted the growing use of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), a minimally invasive procedure to replace narrowed aortic valves in elderly patients and stressed the importance of early diagnosis of severe heart valve disease.

Addressing a press conference, S. Nagendra Boopathy, professor of Cardiology, senior interventional cardiologist and lead, Structural Heart Disease Interventions, said the increasing adoption of TAVI has been driven by growing clinical confidence, supported by long-term evidence, and greater awareness among patients about treatment options.

He said recent international follow-up data spanning seven years had further strengthened confidence in the procedure’s long-term durability and outcomes.

“Symptoms such as breathlessness, fatigue, and reduced activity are often mistaken for ageing. Early diagnosis through echocardiography and timely intervention can significantly improve outcomes. Chennai’s collaborative Heart Team approach and growing experience in managing complex heart valve disease are helping improve patient outcomes while giving families greater confidence in treatment decisions,” Dr. Boopathy said.

Doctors said eligibility for TAVI is determined after assessing a patient’s overall life expectancy, existing comorbidities, and medical history.

S. Ramesh, professor and head of Cardiology, said access to specialised heart valve care continues to be concentrated in urban centres. He noted that while Tamil Nadu is projected to become India’s oldest State by 2031, a large proportion of its elderly population lives outside Chennai, where access to advanced cardiac evaluation remains limited.

World.title: Hanumankind attends CJP’s Jantar Mantar protest as Indian rap community backs NEET stir
World.content:
Bengaluru-based global rap star Sooraj Cherukat, better known as Hanumankind, who has performed at some of the world’s biggest music stages including Coachella and New York’s Nassau Coliseum, ahead of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s address to the Indian diaspora in 2024, marched alongside students and civil society groups on Monday in New Delhi’s Jantar Mantar, demanding Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation over the NEET paper leak controversy and alleged irregularities in higher education.

Wearing a blue India cricket jersey, a black mask and a hat, Hanumankind, one of India’s most well-known and internationally visible rappers at this point, initially blended into the crowd until protesters recognised him. Videos circulating on social media show the rapper pausing to interact with several of them during the Cockroach Janata Party’s (CJP) attempt to march to the Parliament on Monday. He also posted photos and videos of the police lathi charge unleashed upon protesters on his Instagram and wrote in a story, “There’s no justification for this kind of force being used against the people that showed up today. Believing we deserve better is not a crime”. He also re-posted a note that read: “I witnessed two very different demonstrations. One created by the people. One created by the response.”

The 33-year-old rapper, originally from Kerala, whose career has been defined by sold-out venues and international acclaim and who enmeshes Indian music and motifs alongside slick English rap, was joined by a bunch of rappers at the ‘Chalo Sansad’ protest. These included Delhi-based Garv Taneja, who goes by the stage name Chaar Diwari; Encore ABJ aka Abhijay Negi, one half of Delhi-based hip-hop duo Seedhe Maut; Ravi Mishra aka RAGA; and Vivek Arora aka Karma, among others.

In a social media video, Taneja said, “I am here in support of Sonam ji (Wangchuk) and ask for accountability of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)”. Negi also posted videos and photos from the protest along with his well-known song, Red, with lyrics that go ‘Bhoori hai khaal, Bhoore kandhe pe haath APJ, Bose, Bhagat Singh, Chandra Shekhar Azad… Mai anti-government, ye bole anti-national’.

Twenty-five-year-old rapper and part-time English and critical thinking teacher Sanchay Wadhva, who goes by the stage name Sanchay with an X and was present at Monday’s protest along with his students, said that the presence of someone of the stature of Hanumankind, is significant for the cause. Over the last couple of years, Hanumankind has become one of those few Indian rappers whose fame extends well beyond the country, and his global visibility made his appearance at Jantar Mantar particularly notable. “For Hanumankind to be there, he is not just representing himself. He is a part of the culture of hip-hop and rap music. If his showing up can influence and motivate even 15-20 people more to join, that is a big thing and that’s what really matters,” Wadhwa told The Indian Express.

“Hip hop itself has grown out of being socially conscious music. It doesn’t matter if one’s music is political or not, if one makes conscious political music or not. Rap is all about what you see…. It is a mirror to society,” said Wadhwa about hip hop that emerged in the Black and Latino neighbourhoods of Bronx in New York, which was synonymous with poverty, discrimination, police violence and marginalisation.

Meanwhile, Delhi-based rapper Dominick Messiah, who works as a store manager at a solar panel company, had been making regular trips to the protest site in Jantar Mantar even before Monday’s march which saw security officers use lathicharge and teargas shells to disperse the crowd. Last weekend, he performed his track ‘Uthalo ye awaaz tum, Bachalo ye samaj tum’ at a cypher organised at Jantar Mantar. A cypher is a collaborative space where rappers gather in a circle and take turns trading verses over a beat.



“Hip-hop started as a way for people to speak about their pain and the injustices they faced,” he said. “Being here, at this protest, and rapping about it, that’s what the culture is really meant for.” “The tear gas shelling was so brutal that for 10 minutes I didn’t even feel alive. But I am so glad to see the rap community’s support with mainstream and less popular artists also attending the protest. I am

World.title: ‘Doing seva’: Meet volunteers keeping Jantar Mantar functioning and clean
World.content:
Written by Reva Thakkar & Anusree K C

On Tuesday afternoon, as the number of protesters in front of the re-erected stage at Jantar Mantar steadily swelled, a group of men were hard at work, scooping out mud from a clogged drain with their bare hands.

One of them, Suhail Khan, said he had been coming to Jantar Mantar every day since activist Sonam Wangchuk was taken away by police on July 18. “It is our responsibility to keep a place clean, whether it is our home, a mandir, a masjid, a gurdwara, or any other place in our country. Wherever we stay, eat, or protest, we will keep it clean,” Suhail said.



With Suhail was Pramod Pal, who said he had come from Faridabad because it was important to keep the protest area clean. “If we are not here today, the [hygiene] situation may be worse tomorrow,” he said. There is a more personal reason too, Pramod said: “I am here for my daughter… She too may want to become a doctor one day.”

Also Read | What I saw at Jantar Mantar protest after the tear gas shells landed

Suhail and Pramod are among the many volunteers at Jantar Mantar, working silently to keep the protest site clean and functional as the tide of protesters ebbs and flows through the day and night.

Some of the volunteers have registered with student organisations; others have simply turned up to help. (Express Photo) Some of the volunteers have registered with student organisations; others have simply turned up to help. (Express Photo)

Some of the volunteers have registered with student organisations; others have simply turned up to help.



“Mera naam Hindustani hai,” said a man who was walking around, collecting garbage in a large bag. He had been at Jantar Mantar since morning, he said — moving with his bag from the stage to a dumping spot created by the volunteers at the far end of the protest area, near the police barricades and a water truck. The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) held its first protest at the site on June 6, and Tuesday was his 32nd day volunteering, he said.

“What is the definition of a volunteer? Everyone is doing seva here,” the man said. “Some people are fanning others, some are getting water, and some doctors are helping with medical aid for those who need them. Everyone is here to help,” he said.



Among the doctors is Dr M K Bundwal who sat behind a wooden table stacked with medicines, boxes of oral rehydration solution (ORS), ointments, and bandages in a makeshift clinic under a yellow plastic sheet. Along with a team of around 10 volunteers, he has been attending to anyone who needs medical help at the protest site, including the occasional policeman.

‘Will keep coming back’ | CJP protester returns to Jantar Mantar from hospital

“In the beginning, people were coming with complaints of headaches, nausea, and dehydration. Yesterday (when the march to Parliament turned into violent daylong protests), there were a lot of people with head and leg injuries. We needed an ambulance for two people,” Dr Bundwal said.



Another doctor, who said his name was Suresh Gavai and he had come to Delhi from Kalyan in Thane district, said: “Yesterday, they (the police) broke our set-up, and we had to rebuild it. We have no electricity here now.”

Dr Gavai said he had left his two children back at home, and they were attending the protests that were being organised in Maharashtra.

World.title: Farmer leader Raju Shetti, Mahadev Jankar picked up by Delhi police
World.content:
Farmer leader Raju Shetti, who heads Swabhimani Shetkari Sanghatana, was picked up by Police on Tuesday morning from Kisan Ghat in New Delhi.

Another leader Mahadev Jankar, who heads the Rashtriya Samaj Paksh, was also detained and taken to an unknown location.

Speaking to The Indian Express, Shetti said, “I reached Kisan Ghat around 10.15 am. Along with me, Mahadev Jankar and other leaders and representatives of 154 organisations from various parts of the country were also present. The Delhi police came to the spot and asked us to board a police vehicle. We have no idea where we are being taken. I overheard that we are being taken to Sonepat. We have not been given any reason for being detained in this manner.”

World.title: ‘Would tell him salary of cook’: R Madhavan on teaching son Vedaant respect; expert reflects
World.content:
In a conversation with Radhika Gupta on the YouTube channel 100 Year Life Project by ACKO, actor R Madhavan reflected on the values he consciously tried to instil in his son, Vedaant Madhavan, who is pursuing his dream of winning an Olympic medal for India.

Speaking about his parenting approach, Madhavan said, “One of the most important skills a child should have is the attitude of gratitude. Although we came from a very middle-class background, I was able to afford everything Vedant wanted because of the kind of success God bestowed upon me. But I also realised that came with its own set of challenges.” He added, “I realised there were two things I needed to teach Vedaant. One was the attitude of gratitude. It’s very important for children to know that they are privileged because somebody else has worked their backside off to give them this lifestyle.”



DISCLAIMER: This article is based on information from the public domain and/or the experts we spoke to.

To make the idea more tangible, he shared, “Sometimes I would tell him the salary of my cook and say, ‘Do you know what this toy you’ve been gifted costs? This man would have to work an entire year, living in that kitchen, to afford even a part of it.’ That struck Vedant a lot.” Madhavan also emphasised treating everyone with dignity, saying, “The second thing I made sure Vedant did was acknowledge everyone — the liftman, the guard, the drivers, the ayahs. I told him not to address them casually but respectfully, as didis and bhaiyas.” He explained, “It’s not just about good manners. It’s about situational awareness. I wanted my child to be aware of where he is, who he’s dealing with, and to greet people who may not have as much money.”

Recalling moments that reassured him as a parent, he said, “If the watchman came and said, ‘Your son is a very polite child. He always says namaste to me,’ I felt my job was well done.” He further noted, “I can’t tell you how many times that has stood him in good stead and helped when he really needed it. People remember him because he’s far more polite than most others. It helps to get noticed in today’s world.”



Madhavan also spoke about another lesson that influenced his parenting. Recalling advice from a family he lived with while studying in Canada, he shared, “She gave me one piece of advice that I followed wholeheartedly, and it really worked for my son. She said, ‘Don’t give your child free time.’” Elaborating on what he meant, he said, “Indulge them in whatever they want to do. The interests will change; the level of commitment will change, but make sure they don’t have free time till they’re 15 or 16. Let them move from one activity to another.”

However, he stressed that these activities should remain enjoyable: “It should be fun. It shouldn’t be a chore because the child is going to hate it. Whether it’s basketball, tennis, golf, kabaddi, spending time with the staff’s children or even learning how to make dough—just make sure their time is filled.” According to Madhavan, keeping children meaningfully engaged can leave less room for unhealthy influences during adolescence.



But how well do these parenting strategies align with what child psychology and developmental science recommend? We asked an expert.

Gratitude begins with awareness

Counselling psychologist Athul Raj tells indianexpress.com, “Children don’t develop gratitude because we ask them to say ‘thank you’. They develop it when they begin to notice the people and the effort behind the life they enjoy. That’s why conversations about money should never stop at how much something costs. They should also include what it takes to earn it and the invisible labour that makes our daily lives comfortable. In many Indian homes, children are constantly watching how adults speak to domestic workers, drivers, security guards or the person collecting the garbage. Those moments teach them far more than a lecture on values ever will.”



How everyday respect shapes lifelong values

Raj mentions, “I often tell parents that children are studying them all the time. They notice who gets your patience, who gets your respect and who gets ignored. A child may forget many of the values you tried to teach, but they rarely forget the values you practised. When a parent greets a security guard by name or thanks someone who works in the house, the child learns that respect is not reserved for people with power or influence. That shapes empathy because they begin seeing people as individuals rather than by their occupation or social status. It also builds emotional intelligence by helping children understand that small interactions have an emotional impact.”

These everyday moments quietly influence the kind of friend, partner, colleague and leader a child eventually becomes. Respect that is practised consistently across social differences becomes part of a child’s character, not just their manners.



Why boredom isn’t the enemy

Click below to reveal the expert’s answer:

Should children always stay busy, or is boredom actually good for them? Raj states that meaningful activities are important because they help children build confidence, discipline and a sense of purpose. But there is a difference between a child being engaged and a child being constantly occupied. Many parents become uncomfortable the moment a child says, “I’m bored,” and rush to fill that space. Yet boredom is not always something that needs fixing. Very often, it is where imagination begins. “When children are left with some unstructured time, they learn to tolerate frustration, entertain themselves, make decisions and discover what genuinely interests them instead of waiting to be directed. If every minute is planned, children may become high achievers but struggle when life doesn’t provide structure. Healthy development comes from balancing opportunities to learn with opportunities to simply think, explore and be. Children need both guidance and space, because independence grows in the moments when adults step back,” concludes Raj.
