Tech.title: Google Releases 3 New Gemini Models, 3.5 Pro Still Not Available
Tech.content:
Google released three new AI models on Tuesday, all built on Gemini 3.5 Flash. The new models are more token-efficient, faster and more reliable across the board. The tech giant also provided an update on the much-anticipated Gemini 3.5 Pro and what’s to come after.

A new AI model from the likes of Google, Anthropic or OpenAI is released seemingly every week, with the latest, ChatGPT-5.6, released earlier this month. Google’s latest releases aren’t flagship models compared to what’s on the horizon, but each has its place, including a new model solely focused on cybersecurity.

Here’s what’s new in the latest Gemini models from today’s announcement.

Gemini 3.6 Flash

Google called 3.6 Flash its “workhorse” model that’s now better at coding, knowledge work and multimodal performance. It also promises reduced token usage by up to 17%, and at a lower cost per token versus its predecessor, 3.5.

Google says it built the model based on both developer and customer feedback. A series of benchmarks shows 3.6 Flash’s gains in performance and average tokens per task compared to its predecessor.

Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite

Google’s fastest and most cost-effective model can deliver 350 output tokens per second and “significantly” outperforms previous generations when it comes to agentic workflows, according to the blog post.

Like 3.6 Flash, this model now supports computer use as a built-in tool to take on more agentic tasks.

Gemini 3.5 Flash Cyber

3.5 Flash Cyber is a specialty model that prioritizes cybersecurity workflows in order to find and fix vulnerabilities. It works alongside an infrastructure agent called CodeMender to help cybersecurity teams quickly identify and patch issues.

According to a separate article from Google DeepMind, the new model is already finding and fixing bugs in Google’s internal codebases in Android, Chrome and YouTube. This model will initially be limited to governments and trusted partners, but access will expand in the future.

Gemini 3.5 Pro is still on the way

While the three latest models are the primary focus for Tuesday’s announcements, Google gave a brief update to its upcoming flagship AI model, Gemini 3.5 Pro. The model is said to currently be in testing with partners, and it plans to make it available as soon as it’s ready. How long that will take is anyone’s guess, but Google’s also already looking ahead to the next generation of AI, too.



Google says it has already begun pretraining for Gemini 4, which will be released at an undetermined date.

Both Gemini 3.6 Flash and 3.5 Flash-Lite are available starting today for developers in the Gemini API via Google AI Studio and Android Studio and the Gemini app. 3.6 Flash is also available in Google Antigravity, and 3.5 Flash-Lite is rolling out to Google Search.

Tech.title: ChatGPT Browser Atlas Will Be Discontinued by OpenAI in August
Tech.content:
OpenAI’s ambitions to challenge Google Chrome and Mozilla Firefox as a web browser are coming to an end. OpenAI/Jeffrey Hazelwood/CNET

OpenAI is abandoning its attempt to compete directly with Google Chrome and Mozilla Firefox as a standalone browser maker. The AI company announced plans to sunset Atlas, a stand-alone browser it released last fall, and roll its technology into a suite of tools in its desktop app.

OpenAI said earlier this year that it was developing a “superapp” for Macs and Windows, but did not mention at the time that Atlas would be rolled into that.

At the time of its release, Atlas seemed like a natural evolution of OpenAI’s takeover of the world, bringing its popular chatbot ChatGPT to web browsers with the potential to turn web searches into conversational prompts. But OpenAI had stiff competition from other AI-enabled browsers, including Perplexity’s Comet, Microsoft’s Edge with Copilot and Brave, among others.

In its race to keep up with its biggest competitor, Anthropic, OpenAI appears to be narrowing its focus to advancing its core AI technology rather than pursuing what the company calls “side quests.” OpenAI just released its latest version of ChatGPT, 5.6.

(Disclosure: Ziff Davis, CNET’s parent company, in 2025 filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging it infringed Ziff Davis copyrights in training and operating its AI systems.)

The Atlas sunset date is set

In a post on X, OpenAI developer James Sun said Atlas is expected to go away as a stand-alone product on Aug. 9. He wrote that its abilities will be part of the new features in the desktop app and other products.

“All these capabilities were built on what we learned from Atlas users who took a leap of faith on a new browser,” Sun said. “You taught us how agents can help make browsing and doing work on the open web better, and we are applying these learnings to these new products.”

Tech.title: Samsung’s New AI Health Assistant Aims to Make Health Metrics Actually Useful
Tech.content:
The Samsung Health service is getting a built-in AI-powered personal health assistant. The new Samsung Health Assistant is launching now in beta for eligible people in the US. It aims to address a common problem in digital health today: health data and metrics are often scattered across multiple apps and devices, leaving you with plenty of numbers but not enough clarity on how to interpret them for your health routine.

At the core of the experience is a “holistic” approach to health, according to the company’s press release. Samsung says the Health Assistant connects information from Samsung Health’s five wellness pillars — sleep, activity, nutrition, mindfulness and vitals — and translates that data into explanations and tailored recommendations. You can also access items like their Energy Score, with guidance delivered where you already track and manage your health.

Samsung says that the recommendations are validated by physicians and certified health coaches, and supported by Samsung Health’s knowledge base to help identify patterns and signals you might otherwise miss. Looking ahead, Samsung says that capabilities will expand toward deeper coaching and more services, including areas like weight management, and that it will use its Personal Data Engine for personalization that can take into account context such as schedules and preferences.

“By leveraging our ecosystem and partnerships, we aim to deliver a holistic understanding of health and drive real action, helping users build healthier habits and bringing real change to their lives,” Dr. Hon Pak, senior vice president and head of Samsung’s digital health team, said in a statement.

You can view your Energy Score and receive health recommendations directly from the Health Assistant. Credit: Samsung



A bevy of AI health assistants

This new feature lands in an already crowded field.

The market for AI health assistants and chatbots has become saturated with products promising “personalized” insights, like ChatGPT Health and Amazon’s Health AI tool. But many struggle to deliver sustained value, especially when data is fragmented, recommendations are generic and you can’t easily connect day-to-day behaviors to longer-term goals.

Samsung’s bet is that tighter integration with an existing health ecosystem, paired with an interpretation layer that ties multiple wellness domains together, can make AI guidance feel more actionable than a standalone assistant.

Tech.title: Return to Halo Almost 25 Years Later With Xbox Game Pass
Tech.content:
Bungie released Halo on Xbox in 2001, and it changed gaming and pop culture forever. I remember the first time I picked up an energy sword. It felt like I was playing something special. Now, about 25 years later, I can revisit that iconic experience when the Xbox brings a remade version of the game to Game Pass on July 28.

Xbox Game Pass, a CNET Editors’ Choice award pick, offers a wide selection of games you can play on your Xbox Series X, Xbox Series S, Xbox One and PC or mobile device for as little as $10 a month. And with a subscription to the higher-tiered Game Pass Ultimate ($23 a month), you can access hundreds of games, including new ones the day they’re released, each month.

Here are all the games Xbox is bringing to Game Pass soon.

Shift at Midnight

Coming to Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass on July 21.

I’ve seen people post demo videos of this game online, and I’m excited to finally play it. It’s a horror game where you work as a convenience store clerk, but you have to investigate your customers since some of them are monsters in disguise. Let the wrong customer in, and you’ve got to set traps, hide and defend yourself from otherworldly horror. Don’t forget to restock the shelves and take out the trash before you clock out.

Halo: Campaign Evolved

Coming to Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass on July 28.

Step into the boots of the legendary Master Chief as he takes on the Covenant and the Flood in the first installment of one of the most well-known gaming franchises in history. This remade version of the iconic Halo: Campaign Evolved includes 4K visuals, updated animations and more. There are also three new missions that take place a year prior to the start of the game. So grab your rocket launcher and some plasma grenades and get ready to take on the Covenant and the Flood for the hundredth — or first — time.

Beast of Reincarnation

Coming to Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass on Aug. 4.

Game Freak is widely known as the developer behind the Pokémon games, but its upcoming game Beast of Reincarnation is a different kind of beast — pun intended. You play as Emma and her trusty dog companion Koo as they try to save a post-apocalyptic Japan from corrupted creatures in this role-playing game. This game has real-time and turn-based combat, so it should present an interesting challenge.

Heretic and Hexen

New to Game Pass Premium on Aug. 4. Previously on Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass.

Face down demons, cultists and other infernal creatures with medieval weaponry and magic in these cult-classic games from the ’90s. If you look at these ported games and think they just look like Doom but with swords, you aren’t far off. Developer Raven Software used a modified version of the Doom engine to create Heretic and Hexen, so the games should look and feel familiar.

Other games coming to Game Pass

Those are a few of the games I’m looking forward to on Xbox Game Pass, but Microsoft is adding more to the service this month. Here are the other games you can try soon.

Hell Is Us – Coming to Game Pass Ultimate, Game Pass Premium and PC Game Pass on July 23.

Mistfall Hunter – Coming to Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass on July 30.

Corsair Cove – Coming to Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass on July 31.

These games are leaving Game Pass on July 31

While Microsoft is adding several titles to Game Pass soon, it’s also removing eight others from the service on July 31. So you still have some time to play these games for the first time, but hurry before you have to buy them separately.

For more on Xbox, here’s what to know about the recent Xbox layoffs. You can also check out our Xbox Game Pass review and which Game Pass plan is right for you.

Tech.title: Are Meal Delivery Services Good for People on GLP-1s? Here’s What an Expert Told Me
Tech.content:
Eating on GLP-1s presents unique challenges. We asked an expert if a curated meal delivery service can help. inspired_by_the_light/Getty Images

GLP-1 receptor agonists — the class of drugs behind brand names such as Ozempic, Mounjaro, and Wegovy — have exploded in popularity by mimicking hormones the body naturally produces to manage blood sugar, curb appetite and slow digestion.

These medications work in part by tamping down hunger, which is a major reason they’ve proven effective for weight loss. But that same appetite suppression means people taking them often have to rethink how they eat to make sure they’re still getting enough essential nutrients. If you’re not used to planning meals or tracking your calorie and macronutrient intake, that shift can take some getting used to.

To help make sense of it, I spoke with Juliana Vocca, a registered dietitian with a master’s degree in nutrition science and founder of Prime Women Nutrition. She shared her go-to food strategies for people on these medications, along with a few dietitian-recommended meal kit options for anyone looking to simplify the process.

What should you eat on GLP-1s?

Protein and fiber have outsized importance for someone on GLP-1s. Getty Images

There are three key nutrients to consider while on GLP-1s: protein, fiber and hydration.

“Protein helps maintain lean muscle mass, while fiber and hydration help keep things moving through the body, resulting in better tolerance,” explains Vocca. “Because GLP‑1 medications slow digestion and curb appetite, every bite needs to count. That means focusing on foods that support muscle, steady energy and comfortable digestion.”

The Best Meat Delivery Services out of Dozens We Tried See at Cnet

Good sources of lean protein at every meal include chicken, fish, eggs, tofu, Greek yogurt, cottage cheese and beans. These help to preserve muscle during weight loss and are easier to digest than heavy, high-fat alternatives.

“Aim for 1.2 to 2 grams of protein per kilogram of body weight or around 90 to 150 grams per day,” she advises.

For fiber, options such as vegetables, berries, lentils, chickpeas, oats, quinoa and whole-grain bread can help keep the body “regular” (a common challenge on GLP-1s) and help patients feel satisfied with smaller portions.

“Opt for healthy fats in modest amounts,” adds Vocca, which can be found in avocado, nuts, seeds and olive oil. “These will also support nutrient absorption without overwhelming a slowed-down GI tract.”



But perhaps the most important element of all is maintaining hydration. “Sip throughout the day to prevent constipation and help your gut cope with slower motility [how food moves through your gastrointestinal tract],” says Vocca. “Also, choose smaller, more frequent meals. Big portions can feel uncomfortable; nutrient‑dense mini‑meals often sit better.”

What vitamins and minerals should patients focus on receiving?

Eating less overall means taking steps to ensure you’re getting enough vitamins and minerals. Kinga Krzeminska/Getty Images

Because GLP-1 medications naturally reduce appetite and slow digestion, people often eat less overall.

“This means fewer opportunities to get key nutrients, not because of the medications themselves, but because overall intake drops,” shares Vocca. “The vitamins most commonly affected are vitamin D, calcium, iron and B vitamins.”

“A healthcare professional can help determine whether supplementation is appropriate; however, it is not recommended to start with supplementation. Food should always be the first option,” she adds.

Here are Vocca’s tried-and-true ways to make up for potential deficiencies:

Vitamin D: “Consume fortified orange juice and dairy foods, mushrooms and fatty fish like salmon. Three ounces of salmon can provide 50-100% of your vitamin D needs. Many people take vitamin D3 with a fat‑containing meal to support absorption. Supplement with Vitamin D3 at 1000- 2000 IU.”

Calcium: “Calcium-rich foods include dairy, fortified plant milks, tofu, sardines and fortified cereals. One cup of milk or yogurt can provide 30% of your daily needs. It’s also helpful to know that calcium and iron compete for absorption, so many people avoid taking them simultaneously. Supplement with 500 mg of calcium citrate.”

Iron: “Iron-rich foods include red meat, poultry, seafood, beans, lentils, spinach and iron-fortified cereals. One-third of a cup of multi-grain Cheerios provides 100% of your daily iron requirements. Pair iron-rich foods with vitamin C (citrus, peppers, strawberries) to dramatically increase absorption. “

Vitamin B: “Vitamin B is found in animal products such as meat, fish, eggs and dairy, and is also added to grains and cereals. Choose a B-complex vitamin for supplementation. Take them in the morning to help support energy. Use a dissolvable vitamin B12 supplement if you struggle with digestive issues to improve absorption.”

But again, always consult your doctor before taking a supplement or drastically changing your diet.

How to overcome your lack of appetite on GLP-1s

Protein shakes, yogurt drinks, Greek yogurt and cottage cheese can help you meet protein goals while on GLP-1s. Giselle Castro-Sloboda/ CNET

Hunger suppression means the medication is doing its job, but it can make mealtimes uncomfortable.

“When appetite is low, smaller, more frequent eating times every 3 to 4 hours work far better than forcing large meals,” says Vocca. “The goal is steady intake, not volume.”

Protein should also be part of every bite, though patients don’t need to consume an entire steak to reach their goals. Instead, 10 to 20 grams at each meal should suffice and can be obtained from ready-to-drink protein shakes, yogurt drinks, Greek yogurt or cottage cheese.

“Gentle, bland foods, such as oatmeal, might be tolerated better, as these tend to go down more easily when appetite is low or nausea is present,” adds Vocca.

These meal delivery services are designed for folks on GLP-1s

Factor and other popular meal delivery services have designed meals and menus with GLP-1 users in mind. Factor/CNET

If cooking and meal prepping sound too intimidating, Vocca recommends a bevy of specialized programs, including meal kit services that cater to specific diets.

“These remove the burden of meal planning and help ensure you meet nutritional needs, such as hitting your daily protein goal, while also managing reduced portion sizes and potential side effects,” she says, noting that some of the top programs are also geared specifically to the GLP-1 lifestyle. The most respected and highly reviewed companies include WeightWatchers, Factor, Clean Eatz Kitchen and ModifyHealth.

ModifyHealth is another service I’ve tested that caters to specific diets, including GLP-1-friendly. Joey Skladany/CNET

“Clean Eatz Kitchen meals are high in protein, soft and portion-controlled. Factor offers fresh, high-protein meals with plenty of options, though portions can be larger than some can tolerate. And ModifyHealth meals are gentle on digestion and protein-forward,” she details.

The meal delivery service with the most ‘GLP-1-friendly’ meals

Most BistroMD meals are around 300 calories and high in protein. David Watsky/CNET

Among all the services CNET tested, BistroMD stood out as the top pick. The program offers more than 150 dietitian-designed meals and snacks — including breakfasts, lunches and dinners — purpose-built for weight loss and GLP-1 users. The company also offers GLP-1 medication directly alongside its meal plans.

While on GLP-1s, choosing quality food, protein-rich foods is important. David Watsky/CNET

BistroMD’s GLP-1 program is designed to support weight loss, help preserve muscle mass and ease common side effects associated with GLP-1 medications. It can be added to any BistroMD plan, unlocking access to the full library of 150-plus weekly meals — the largest selection of any service in our evaluation.

Each meal targets a specific nutritional profile: roughly 25 to 30g of protein, 20 to 25g of net carbs, 5g of fiber, 8 to 12g of fat and 500mg of sodium. Managing Editor David Watsky, who reviewed the service hands-on, found the meals generally healthy, well-portioned and competently prepared — with the meat dishes earning particular praise.

bistroMD has more than 150 meals geared towards weight-loss, low-calorie and GLP-1 users. Screenshot by David Watsky/CNET

Pricing runs $11 to $15 per serving, plus a $20 shipping fee, landing BistroMD in the midrange for meal delivery. That said, costs can climb quickly, so it may not be the best fit for budget-focused shoppers.

Some handy kitchen tools to consider while on GLP-1s

A single-serving blender is key for making protein-rich shakes and smoothies. Beast Health

Should you want to cook your own meals and be in complete control over what goes into your body, there are a handful of helpful tools that Vocca wants patients to consider as necessary kitchen investments:

A digital food scale: “This helps to ensure you accurately meet your protein needs.”

A high-powered, single-serving blender: “This lets you make shakes on days when your appetite is low.”

A slow cooker: “This helps to keep lean meats moist, tender, appetizing and easier to digest.”

“I also use an air fryer to help add flavor and keep vegetables tender,” she adds. “Using an insulated 32-oz tracker water bottle is also important for ensuring adequate hydration.”

Eating with purpose

Adapting to new ingredients, meal sizes, and eating frequencies can be difficult.

“Your body and your relationship with food are undergoing a major software update. Progress comes from consistency, not perfection,” Vocca reminds.

But by shifting your mindset from eating less to eating with purpose, you’ll soon prioritize the foods and/or meal kits that keep your body energized, satiated, and, most importantly, healthy.

Tech.title: This Low-Price Acer Phone Has a Rear Display Like a $1,000 Flagship
Tech.content:
Acer Mobile Latam earlier this month unveiled the new Sospiro A15 phone, set to arrive this summer and turning heads with its full-color rear selfie screen. That’d be cool enough if this were a $1,000-plus flagship like the iPhone 17 Pro or Xiaomi 17 Pro Max — which it borrows heavily from in design — but the A15 is a budget phone expected to cost around $150 to $250. Holy affordability, Batman. What gives?

It’s been a little over a decade since we last saw an Acer-branded smartphone in the US. However, Acer Mobile Latam isn’t the same Acer you probably know for its laptops, tablets and monitors. The Sospiro A15 is manufactured by Senwa Global International, which licenses the Acer name for electronics products across Latin America and is a totally separate operation from anything Acer sells in the US today. That means the A15 won’t be sold by US carriers, but the phone is still worth a look to see how the brand managed to ape a flagship-level feature at a budget price.

Trickle-down gimmickry

The rear of the A15 is dominated by an iPhone 17 Pro-esque plateau housing a pair of 64-megapixel cameras, along with this phone’s claim to fame: a 1.88-inch full-color rear display. With just 284×240 pixels and TFT technology, this surely isn’t the brightest or highest-quality screen, but it probably gets the job done, displaying notifications and music controls, and doubling as a selfie viewfinder.

For comparison, the 976×596-pixel Magic Back Screen on the Xiaomi 17 Pro Max is a 2.9-inch LTPO AMOLED panel running at 120Hz with peak brightness of around 3,500 nits — larger, crisper and bright enough to read in broad daylight. It’s the same concept, but at a very different level of execution, which makes sense given the wildly different budgets.

No surprises, Acer is using cheaper components and betting that budget buyers will be happy with a slightly worse screen for a significantly lower price. It’s a clever move considering the phones that the A15 will actually compete with have no selfie screens to speak of.

A modest spec sheet

Beyond the selfie-screen razzle-dazzle, the Sospiro A15 is a budget phone with budget phone components and specs. The main 6.67-inch IPS display’s 1,600×720-pixel resolution and 120Hz refresh aren’t bad. The 5,000 mAh battery and 18-watt wired charging are fine. And while 6GB of RAM and 128GB of storage are nothing to get excited about, its SD card slot with up to 1TB of expansion is increasingly rare in 2026. Perhaps the biggest budget-spec tell is the midtier Unisoc T615 octa-core SoC, which you’d expect to find on phones battling in the sub-$200 price range.

You don’t often see a rear display on a mobile phone, and usually it’s on pricey flagships. The Acer Sospiro A15 offers it on a budget-minded device.

None of this is embarrassing for the segment; it’s just not the segment most tech enthusiasts usually think about. To its credit, the A15 distinguishes itself with creature comforts like a side-mounted fingerprint reader, face unlock and NFC with Google Wallet support. The handset also has an IP64 rating — splash resistance that most budget phones skip — which is a nice inclusion at its expected price.

Price and availability

Acer hasn’t announced pricing for the Sospiro A15, which is expected to arrive this summer. Based on the specs, we expect something in the $150 to $250 range once local pricing firms up. The phone won’t be sold in the US, but shoppers in the Latin American markets looking to flex a selfie screen could buy five or six A15s for the price of the Xiaomi 17 Pro Max (which starts north of $1,000 in the markets where it’s sold) and still have money left for cases.

There’s more to both of these phones than just the gimmick of their rear screens, but that doesn’t change the fact that a budget phone now includes a feature Xiaomi was charging flagship money for less than a year ago. When everything is getting more and more expensive, that feels like a small affordability win.

Tech.title: Meta’s Quest Game Subscribers Will Be Getting Some Xbox Extras
Tech.content:
Meta hasn’t done a lot with its Quest VR platform this year (in fact, it’s done more to dismantle it), but it’s throwing an Xbox bonus into its gaming subscription plan to try to sweeten the deal.

Horizon Plus, the monthly gaming subscription service for Meta’s Quest VR headsets, is adding an Xbox Game Pass starter edition that includes a limited amount of cloud gaming time a month.

The starter pass only allows 10 hours of Xbox gaming a month, which isn’t a lot, but it could be a welcome extra for anyone who’s already paying $60 a year or $8 a month for the service. It has access to the games on Xbox’s Essential Edition Game Pass (about 50 games), which normally costs $10 a month for unlimited access.

This is Meta’s latest collaboration with Microsoft, which previously included an Xbox-themed Quest 3S headset and a dedicated Xbox cloud gaming app on the Quest.

Usually you have to pair an Xbox controller to the Quest to play Xbox games, but Meta’s also introducing a software update for its Touch controllers that will mimic the inputs needed for Xbox games. It won’t be the same as the gamepad-like layout on Valve’s upcoming Steam Frame, but it looks like a move designed to keep the Quest competitive with what Valve’s SteamOS-ready VR headset has coming.

Meta’s subscription service is well worth signing up for, because its 100-plus games include many of the best titles on the platform. It also raises questions on whether Meta might be readying a new Quest headset in the next year, too, something that Meta’s CTO, Andrew Bosworth, has heavily hinted at.

Tech.title: This Wearable Aims to Improve Your Blood Pressure. It’s Now in the US, and I Got a First Look
Tech.content:
The Hilo Core blood pressure system comes with a wireless cuff and a thin wristband that can continuously track your blood pressure. Giselle Castro-Sloboda/ CNET

Swiss health tech brand Aktiia announced Tuesday that its blood pressure health system, Hilo Core, is now available in the US. Backed by 22 years of research, the device delivers long-term blood pressure insights so users can better understand their heart health, which is especially significant considering that about half of US adults have high blood pressure (also known as hypertension).

According to the company, Hilo is also the world’s first blood pressure health system that combines an FDA-cleared cuff, which helps establish a baseline blood pressure reading, with a lightweight wearable wristband that provides ongoing blood pressure readings between cuff measurements.

“What we’re doing here is redefining completely the experience of blood pressure from a one-graph reading with a cuff on the arm to something that is embedded into your life,” Josep Solà, Aktiia co-founder and chief technology officer, told CNET during a Zoom call.

Ahead of its US launch, I’ve spent the last few days testing Hilo. This is what I’ve learned.

How Hilo works

Hilo focuses on your diastolic and systolic numbers, which are used to measure blood pressure. Systolic, the number on top of your reading, measures the maximum pressure in your arteries when your heart pumps out blood, while the bottom diastolic number shows the minimum pressure in your arteries when your heart is at rest and refills with blood.

Monitoring your blood pressure numbers can help prevent strokes and heart attacks.

An example of how Hilo reads your blood pressure trend over the course of a week. Hilo/Giselle Castro-Sloboda/CNET

I got to try Hilo firsthand and found it simple to use and set up. The Hilo Core kit includes a thin, screenless wristband wearable with a 15-day battery life and an FDA-cleared cuff that connects to a mobile app. Cuff measurements are required only during the first four days of activation for calibration, and thereafter on a monthly basis. This approach aims to give you a more comprehensive picture of your blood pressure fluctuations over time, rather than focusing on a single reading.

I took my cuff readings first thing in the morning after waking up and before eating or drinking coffee because certain foods and beverages can affect your readings.

After an initial four-day calibration, the Hilo cuff is used to measure your blood pressure monthly. Giselle Castro-Sloboda/CNET

The cuff reading felt similar to when I have my blood pressure taken at a doctor’s office, so it wasn’t anything out of the ordinary. The only difference is that the cuff is wireless and controlled by the app. The app recommends sitting still and relaxing to get the most accurate readings.

As for the Hilo band, it can capture up to 35 blood pressure readings per day. It also uses your sleep, heart rate and step count to provide contextualized insights.

To collect this data from the wrist, Hilo relies on optical blood pressure monitoring technology: photoplethysmographic — or PPG — light sensors, typically found in wearables, that can estimate blood pressure without requiring frequent cuff inflation.

The Hilo band is thin and includes light sensors that estimate blood pressure without a cuff. Giselle Castro-Sloboda/CNET

After you’ve calibrated your wristband, all you need to do is wear it like any other wearable. It’s lightweight, so you barely feel it, and it continuously reads pulse waves of your arteries every 90 minutes.

Setup was fast, and within minutes of the three inflating-and-deflating cycles performed by the cuff, I was able to view the cuff readings sent to the app. You can use the cuff for spot checks monthly or to validate the wearable’s readings.

For individuals who need to check their vitals regularly, I can see this device making it easy for them to track their blood pressure daily with minimal effort.

Is Hilo medical-grade?

In Europe, both the Hilo cuff and band are certified as medical devices. In the US, the Hilo cuff is FDA-cleared as a medical device, while the Hilo band is considered a wellness product and has not yet received FDA clearance. Just keep in mind that the system is meant to make you more aware of your daily blood pressure and isn’t meant to replace your doctor.

As always, consult with your practitioner before making any lifestyle changes or if you have questions. Before purchasing any health monitoring device like this one, you may also want to ask your doctor whether it’s right for your specific health condition.

However, Hilo is working toward getting approved to be included in a regulated medical platform used by healthcare professionals.

Hilo vs. other wearables that monitor blood pressure

There are already wearables, such as the Apple Watch and Oura Ring, that use their own tech to detect blood pressure changes to provide users with blood pressure awareness, but they aren’t currently approved for medical use, either. Now, there’s also the Signal Ring, which claims to replace a blood pressure cuff in providing accurate readings. Unlike Hilo, these wearables don’t come with a cuff that can establish a baseline reading or be used for monthly spot checks.

Previously, there was the Omron HeartGuide, a blood pressure monitor that used an inflatable cuff built into the wearable. It’s since been discontinued, but according to Hilo, its system differs from the HeartGuide because its wearable band doesn’t have a screen and uses optical sensors rather than an inflatable cuff. Hilo comes with a separate cuff for extra assurance that its readings have a baseline and are correct. With the HeartGuide, you’d chose when you’d take your blood pressure measurements, while Hilo automatically conducts readings every 90 minutes, including overnight.

Past success in Europe

Hilo already exists in Europe and has found success in helping people monitor blood pressure. According to a press release, a study conducted by the company from 2022 to 2025 with about 30,000 European participants found that, compared to people who didn’t regularly use a similar EU version of the Hilo app, those who consistently used it reduced their systolic blood pressure by up to five times over six months.

Solà told CNET that Hilo Core is generally used by people who have been diagnosed with high blood pressure, and those in their 50s and 60s.

How Hilo is different from traditional blood pressure cuffs

What the Hilo calibration process looks like during the first four days. Hilo/Giselle Castro-Sloboda/CNET

Normally, the recommended method to track blood pressure readings at home via a blood pressure cuff or monitor, but Solà wanted an easier approach: “I realized that they could shift this pain [of repeatedly using a blood pressure monitor] to a wearable device that does everything automatically.”

According to Solà, Hilo observed that those who were most engaged with the app saw greater improvement in their blood pressure readings over time.

“Normally, anyone who is diagnosed with high blood pressure has to measure it at least two times a day,” Solà explained. “What we’re seeing is that the average number of times that our users open the app to get their blood pressure numbers is up to three times a day.”

Having this knowledge at your fingertips can make you feel more in control and motivated to change your lifestyle habits, allowing you to see improvement in your blood pressure readings. It also gives you a clearer picture of your blood pressure health, which you can share with your doctor.

“We’re the companion to help them control blood pressure because we empower them with the data that they need,” Solà said.

The Hilo band makes it possible to continuously track your blood pressure. Hilo

What Hilo hopes to achieve in the US

Hilo’s goal with this launch is to help Americans with hypertension lower their blood pressure, as it did in Europe.

“This has the potential to help these patients resolve this hypertension problem,” said Solà. “The sooner you become aware of being hypertensive, the sooner you can start managing your blood pressure to help make it go down.”

Hilo’s privacy policy

Concerns about privacy are always at the forefront when someone chooses to monitor their health with a wearable. Hilo says that user data collected by the system is only used to improve Hilo’s products and services. The company doesn’t sell health data to third parties, and any data used for research or similar purposes is anonymized or aggregated.

An annual subscription is required

The Hilo Core kit is available for $90 at Amazon and Hilo.com. There is also a $150 annual subscription fee, which could be a barrier for those seeking an affordable way to regularly monitor their blood pressure. You can get pre-approved for HSA and FSA eligibility through your health insurance.
